stories.title: Alok Kumar likely to be next UP Chief Secretary:Veena Kumari also in race; suspense over SP Goyal’s extension
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the state may get a new Chief Secretary. The current Chief Secretary, Shashi Prakash (SP) Goyal, is due to retire on January 31, 2027. Among the contenders for the post, Alok Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, is currently considered the frontrunner. Additional Chief Secretary of the Sugar Industry and Cane Development Department Veena Kumari Meena, CM Yogi’s Additional Chief Secretary Sanjay Prasad, and Census Commissioner of India Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan are also among the contenders. Government may push for an extension for SP Goyal Senior government officials believe that the Model Code of Conduct for the elections may already be in force when SP Goyal retires. In such a situation, to avoid administrative reshuffles, both the state government and the Election Commission may consider giving SP Goyal a three- to six-month extension. This could help ensure that the election process is completed smoothly. After the election results, the new government could choose a new Chief Secretary according to its own preferences. However, some officials believe that if SP Goyal does not seek an extension himself, or if CM Yogi does not write to the Centre requesting an extension for him, Uttar Pradesh could get a new Chief Secretary in the middle of the election process. Know the names being discussed for the next Chief Secretary Alok Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, is considered the strongest contender for the post of Chief Secretary. According to sources, Manoj Kumar Singh, CEO of the State Transformation Commission, is backing his candidature. Some Union ministers are also reportedly in favour of appointing Alok Kumar as Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary. Alok Kumar is regarded as one of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s trusted officers. This is why he has been handling key departments such as MSME and Industrial Development since December 2023. If he is appointed Chief Secretary, he would have nearly three years in office, giving him sufficient time to work. This is one factor that puts him in a stronger position than the other contenders. 1993-batch IAS officer Veena Kumari Meena is also a strong contender for the post. If the government chooses her, she would become Uttar Pradesh’s first woman chief secretary. Since returning from central deputation in 2019, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has consistently entrusted her with key responsibilities. She served as Principal Secretary of the Stamp and Registration and Geology and Mining departments from August 2019 to January 2020. From May 2020 to March 2023, she handled the Food and Civil Supplies Department. Since June 2023, she has been continuously heading the Sugar Industry and Cane Development Department. Sanjay Prasad is an influential 1995-batch officer. He is currently the Additional Chief Secretary to the Chief Minister. He also holds charge of the Home, Information and Estate departments. Since March 2019, he has consistently been among the key officials at the Pancham Tal (the Chief Minister’s Office). Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan is also an influential 1995-batch officer. He is currently the Census Commissioner of India. From 2017 to 2018, he served as Secretary to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath before going on central deputation. He is considered to be among the officers close to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, as well as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. Why have the other senior officers fallen behind? Several officers rank senior to the contenders after SP Goyal in terms of seniority. However, as per the rules, an officer must have at least six months of service remaining to be eligible for appointment as Chief Secretary. Therefore, they are considered out of the race: Know more about SP Goyal before his retirement

stories.title: Who owns Neem Karoli Baba’s birthplace?:Granddaughters accuse trust of grabbing it; grandson blames 6 brothers-in-law
stories.summary: A film based on Neem Karoli Baba, Hanuman Ansh, has earned more than ₹100 crore. However, the house where Neem Karoli Baba spent his childhood has now become the centre of a dispute between his family and a trust. 6 of Baba’s granddaughters have submitted a complaint to the District Magistrate, accusing trust secretary Sanjay Gupta of attempting to take possession of the property. Meanwhile, the Uttar Pradesh government is preparing to develop a corridor linked to Neem Karoli Baba there. In such a situation, questions over the ownership and management of properties associated with Baba’s legacy have become significant. So, who owns Neem Karoli Baba’s ancestral house? Why have his granddaughters accused the trust of taking possession of it? Read the full report… First, understand what the dispute is about… Neem Karoli Baba was born in Akbarpur village, around 15 km from Firozabad. House No. 154-V in the village panchayat is his ancestral home. It is maintained by the Shri Thakur Hanuman Trust. The ancestral residence has Baba’s meditation room, dining hall, guest room, and bedroom. This property is at the centre of the dispute. In a complaint submitted to the District Magistrate, Baba’s six granddaughters have accused trust secretary Sanjay Gupta of attempting to take possession of the property. Neem Karoli Baba was a householder saint. He had two sons and a daughter. His elder son, Aneke Sharma, has one son, Dhananjay Sharma, who lives in Firozabad. His younger son, Dharma Narayan Sharma, has six daughters. It was the granddaughters who filed the complaint alleging the encroachment. Baba’s daughter, Girija Bhatele, lives in Agra. Baba’s grandson says sisters’ husbands are behind the dispute We spoke to Neem Karoli Baba’s grandson, Dhananjay Sharma, about the entire dispute. He said, “When this temple was built, my father and uncle had said that after their death, the house should be handed over to the trust. No documentation was done at the time, so there is no proof. The house is built on just 450 square feet. It is not property worth crores. Maharaj Ji’s name is so revered that such a dispute will only tarnish his reputation.” Dhananjay said the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department is preparing to develop a corridor on 5 hectares of land in the village. The land has also been identified. It will be developed along the lines of Kainchi Dham. However, a dispute has now been raised over the property, with allegations that the trust has taken possession of it. “It would be considered encroachment if someone from outside the family had taken possession and refused to vacate the house. But here, the trust is responsible for its entire maintenance,” he said. Dhananjay said, “On August 14, all the sisters came to the village for the death anniversary of their aunt, their mother. There was no talk of any dispute at that time. Everyone sat together and had a meal in the same house. Later, a complaint was submitted to the DM. It is not the sisters but their husbands who are behind all this. Manoj Rawat is at the forefront. I find it strange that the DM accepted their letter when there is no dispute here. My aunt has been the president of the trust from the beginning.” Now, hear the side of Baba’s granddaughters… Baba’s six granddaughters are Sunita Sharma, Archana Sharma, Vandana Sharma, Bhavana Rawat, Ritu Tiwari and Richa Rawat. Manoj Rawat, whom Dhananjay Sharma mentioned, is Bhavana Rawat’s husband and lives in Agra. He is providing documents related to the case to the DM. We spoke to him and told him that Dhananjay had said the complaint was tarnishing Baba’s name. Manoj said, “I understand that too, but there is a limit to everything. When things went beyond the limit, we had to take this step.” Manoj said, “This is not a matter of land, but of emotions. It is our property, and it is not right that we should be stopped from entering it. We submitted documents related to the property to the DM on 7th September. Maharaj Ji’s name is recorded in the Gharoni (property record). After him, the names of his sons and then their daughters should be recorded. We have also submitted the family registers to the DM.” Speaking about the trust’s authority, Manoj said without naming anyone, “When one person has all the authority, there is a possibility of irregularities. They start thinking they are everything. We want the trust to be dissolved and the government to set up a new trust. The Firozabad DM should be its ex-officio president, along with the Tundla tehsildar and another official. Other people from Akbarpur should also be included. This would ensure that these officials keep changing and no one develops a permanent mindset of control.” Trust says dispute has been created deliberately Baba’s wife, Rambeti, established the Shri Thakur Hanuman Ji Trust in 1996. Baba’s daughter, Girija Bhatele, is currently its president. 17 other people are also members of the trust. It manages properties associated with Baba across the country. We spoke to an office-bearer of the trust about the matter. Speaking on condition of anonymity, he said, “There has never been any dispute within the trust so far, and there is no possibility of one in the future either. This dispute has been created deliberately. Truth always prevails. Those creating the dispute will eventually calm down themselves.” Government is developing Neem Karoli corridor The Tourism Department is giving special focus to Neem Karoli Baba’s birthplace. A modern convention centre is also being built here at a cost of around ₹9 crore. It will have a multipurpose hall, a cultural block and a modern exhibition hall. Items associated with Neem Karoli Baba will be displayed in the exhibition hall. Uttar Pradesh Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh visited Firozabad recently. He said the government was developing the area as a religious and cultural tourism centre. This would boost local employment and economic activity. “Our aim is to provide everyone visiting the area with easy connectivity, modern facilities and a spiritual experience,” he said.

stories.title: Govt teacher shot dead in Bijnor:Was returning home from school, also dealt in property; accused walks into police station
stories.summary: A government schoolteacher was shot dead in Bijnor on Tuesday. The teacher was returning home by motorcycle after teaching at school when the accused youth pressed the gun against his abdomen and shot him 150 metres from the school. Local residents took him to hospital, from where he was referred to AIIMS Rishikesh. The teacher died during treatment at around 5 p.m. Meanwhile, the accused went to the police station and surrendered. The teacher was also involved in property dealing. The murder is suspected to be linked to a dispute over this. After the post-mortem, the body is expected to reach the village by Wednesday morning. The incident took place at 2 p.m. in the Najibabad police station area. He travelled 10 km from home to teach at the school Naushad Ahmad (40) lived with his family in Rahatpur Khurd village. He was a government teacher at Purushottampur Primary School. The school is around 10 kilometres from his home. Naushad's family consists of his mother, two wives, and five children. Naushad married Bhuri 20 years ago. They have two daughters and a son. He married Shabana 10 years ago, and they have a son and a daughter. Naushad's eldest daughter is married. The entire family lived together. Alongside teaching, Naushad also worked as a property dealer. He was returning home from school after classes ended On Tuesday, Naushad was riding home on his motorcycle after classes ended when a young man shot him in the abdomen. Naushad fell to the ground along with his motorcycle after being shot. When people nearby rushed to the spot, the accused, Gaurav Rathi (30), fled. The accused went to the police station and surrendered People took the teacher to HMN Hospital in Najibabad. As his condition was critical, doctors referred him to AIIMS Rishikesh. Naushad died at around 5 pm while undergoing treatment there. Meanwhile, Gaurav Rathi went to the police station and surrendered. Village head Mohammad Mustafa said they had learnt that the teacher had been shot. "The reason is still unclear. He has two wives and young children at home. He died while undergoing treatment at AIIMS." Station in-charge Amit Kumar said further action would be taken based on a complaint from the victim's family and the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Gas leak at sewage treatment plant in Meerut:8–10 people fall ill, nearby homes evacuated
stories.summary: Gas leak occurred at a sewage treatment plant (STP) in Meerut at around 8.30pm on Tuesday. People living nearby began experiencing breathing difficulties. Around 8–10 people fell ill and were immediately admitted to hospital for treatment. The sewage plant is located in Pallavpuram Phase 2 in Modipuram. As soon as the incident was reported, the DM and SSP reached the spot. Nearby houses were evacuated. Fire brigade personnel, wearing masks, are trying to control the gas leak. A team from the Jal Kal Department has also reached the site. See some pictures... Gas leaked due to missing washer Daurala Organic safety officer Vishal Gupta said, “Chlorine gas is used at the STP plant. The gas is heavier than air. The employees who added the chlorine had not fitted a washer in the tunnel pipe. During checking, the washer was found to be missing. This caused the gas leak. As the gas is heavy, it could not disperse into the air. The gas is now being dissolved using water. It will take around one to one-and-a-half hours for its effect to subside.” Now know about chlorine gas... A sewage treatment plant treats wastewater and makes it fit for reuse. Chlorine is used in the process to disinfect the water. Chlorine is useful when used in controlled quantities, but a leak in the form of gas can cause serious problems for people living nearby. When chlorine gas comes into contact with air, it can cause irritation to the eyes, nose and throat. People exposed to it may experience coughing, breathing difficulties, eye irritation and chest discomfort.

stories.title: Ghaziabad student dies after jumping from 15th floor:She wrote: I cannot bear the pressure of studies, Mum and Dad... I Love You
stories.summary: On Tuesday evening, a Class 10 student in Ghaziabad died by suicide after jumping from the 15th floor. A suicide note was also found with her. It said, “I cannot cope with the pressure of studies. I am taking my own life because of the pressure of studies. I do not blame anyone. I consider myself responsible. Mum and Dad… I love you.” The incident took place at Gaur Siddhartham Society in the Vijaynagar police station area. After hearing the sound of her fall, the security guard and nearby residents rushed to the spot. Vijaynagar police also arrived after being informed about the incident. During this time, the girl’s family became angry with people who were making videos at the scene. Police sent the girl’s body for post-mortem. Student suffers severe head injury, body covered in blood Shanaya Bisht (16), a resident of Gaur Siddhartham, was studying in Class 10 at Indirapuram Public School. At around 6:45pm on Tuesday, she jumped from the 15th floor of her flat. She suffered severe head injuries, and her face and body were covered in blood. A young man living in the society said, “We suddenly heard a loud sound and rushed to the spot. The guard also arrived. Her family came soon after. By then, the girl had died.” Police recover two-page suicide note Police also recovered a two-page suicide note from the spot. The student wrote that she was troubled by the pressure of studies. Police are examining the suicide note and her handwriting. ACP Kotwali Upasana Pandey said Vijaynagar police received information through Dial-112 at around 7pm on Tuesday that a student had fallen at Gaur Siddhartham Society. Police took the student to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Her body was sent for post-mortem. ‘Mom and Dad, take care of Grandma and Riddhi’ “Please do not worry about me anymore. Live your lives happily. I do not blame anyone. To all my friends, please do not ruin your lives because of me. Mum and Dad, you have another daughter, Riddhi. Please do not let her future be affected because of me. Mum and Dad, take care of yourselves, Grandma and Riddhi. Maasi-Mausa, Mama-Mami, Chacha-Chachi and Nani, all of you stay happy too. Riddhi and Mishti, I am sorry. Please do not think too much about me either. Be successful.” Family angry with people making videos The girl’s family also reached the spot after her death. They objected to residents of the society making videos. The family members said, “You are making a video of our daughter.” Police are speaking to the girl’s family to find out the circumstances that led her to take the step. They have also spoken to residents of the society about the incident.

stories.title: SP district secretary shot dead in Prayagraj:Three bike-borne assailants open fire before fleeing
stories.summary: Three unidentified bike-borne assailants opened fire at former village head and Samajwadi Party district secretary Pawan Yadav in Prayagraj at 6 p.m. on Tuesday. Pawan Yadav was seriously injured after being shot. He was sent to the district hospital for treatment, where he died. Police have begun searching for the assailants. The incident took place in the jurisdiction of Handia police station. See 3 pictures... Read the full details of the incident According to the information available, former village head of Mugrarav village and district president of the former village heads' association, Pavan Yadav, was talking to some people near Pillar No. 52 in the Handia area. At that moment, three unidentified youths riding a motorcycle arrived there. It is being reported that two of the assailants were wearing helmets. One of the motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at Pavan Yadav. Injured, he fell to the ground The bullet struck Pavan Yadav in the back, injuring him and causing him to fall to the ground. After the shooting, the assailants fled towards Baraut on the motorcycle. A crowd gathered at the spot after hearing the sound of gunfire. Pawan Yadav is also the Samajwadi Party's district secretary As soon as news of the incident reached them, ACP Handia Sheshdhar Pandey and Inspector Om Prakash Singh arrived at the spot with a police team. The police officers inspected the scene and gathered information from people in the area. Injured Paavan Yadav was immediately sent to the district hospital for treatment, where he died during treatment. Pawan Yadav is also the Samajwadi Party's district secretary. Police have launched an investigation to identify and arrest the unidentified attackers. They are also examining footage from CCTV cameras installed nearby. The reason for the firing is not yet clear. Police said the cause of the incident and details about the attackers would be established after the investigation is completed.

stories.title: Rinku Singh, Priya Saroj to marry on 4 December:Wedding to be held at Ramada Hotel in Lucknow; engaged 15 months ago
stories.summary: The wedding date of Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj and cricketer Rinku Singh has been finalised. The two will get married at the Ramada Hotel in Lucknow on 4 December. Since the wedding date was finalised, both families have been busy making preparations. In addition to family members, close relatives and special guests may attend the wedding. Rinku Singh is among the prominent players in the Indian cricket team. Priya Saroj, meanwhile, is the Samajwadi Party MP from Machhlishahr in Uttar Pradesh. Two got engaged on 8 June 2025 The ring ceremony of cricketer Rinku Singh and SP MP Priya Saroj was held at The Centrum hotel in Lucknow on 8 June 2025. Rinku and Priya entered the hall holding hands. When Rinku put the ring on Priya's finger on stage, she became emotional and burst into tears. After this, the two raised their hands to express their love and thanked the people who had attended the ceremony. Priya wore a pink lehenga, while Rinku wore a white sherwani. During the ring ceremony, Shah Rukh Khan's film Dunki song "O Maahi, O Maahi" was playing in the background. After the ring ceremony, Rinku and Priya cut the cake and fed it to each other. They then danced enthusiastically with the guests and family members. See four pictures from the engagement ceremony- Priya and Rinku exchanged designer rings Priya put a designer ring, ordered from Kolkata, on Rinku's finger, while Rinku put a designer ring bought in Mumbai on Priya's finger. The two rings cost ₹2.5 lakh. Priya's lehenga was designed by renowned Delhi fashion designer Mahima Mahajan, while Rinku's sherwani was prepared by a designer from Mumbai. 300 VIP guests, including Akhilesh, attended Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, Jaya Bachchan, Shivpal Yadav and Iqra Hasan were among the 300 VIP guests who attended the ring ceremony. Akhilesh had photographs taken with both of them. BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla, former cricketers Piyush Chawla and Praveen Kumar were also present at the ceremony. In addition, bowler Yash Dayal, whose deliveries Rinku hit for five consecutive sixes to achieve stardom in cricket, also attended the ceremony. Rinku and Priya first met at the cricketer's wedding Rinku and Priya's love story is interesting. It began around three years ago. In IPL 2023, Rinku hit five consecutive sixes to help Kolkata Knight Riders win in the final over. After this, Rinku grew closer to the senior cricketers in his team. During this period, a senior cricketer got married in Delhi. The cricketer invited Rinku and Priya, a friend of his wife, to the same ceremony. Rinku and Priya met for the first time at this party. The cricketer's wife introduced them, and this is where their conversations began. A person associated with Rinku's family had said that the KKR cricketer's wife and Priya had studied at Delhi University. Priya Saroj completed a BA LLB from Delhi University. The two became friends while studying. The story is being updated...

stories.title: Ethanol plant to come up in Mathura’s Chhata:NSG personnel to be trained in Ayodhya, Yogi Cabinet approves 23 proposals
stories.summary: A cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was held in Lucknow on Tuesday, where 23 proposals were approved. An NSG regional centre will be set up in Milkipur, Ayodhya, where personnel will receive training. An ethanol plant will be established in Chhata, Mathura, while a new university has been approved for Aligarh. The cabinet also approved a proposal to provide high-tech weapons to the Special Protection Force (SPF). PRD personnel will get cashless treatment worth up to ₹5 lakh. The revised proposal for the Chitrakoot Link Expressway was also approved, along with a plan to make council-run primary schools smarter. Sugarcane Minister Laxmi Narayan Chaudhary said the Chhata ethanol plant will be inaugurated by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath this year. Chaudhary said a sugar factory in Chhata had been shut down 19 years ago. The proposal to restart the facility has now been approved. The plant will produce ethanol from sugarcane and paddy and will operate for 11 months a year. It will produce 3.96 crore litres of ethanol annually. The project is an extension plant. Sugar production will begin once the availability of sugarcane increases. The plant will cost ₹200 crore. There is also a possibility of building a warehouse and a complex. Around 96 acres of land is available for the project, which is expected to generate employment for thousands of people. The sugar factory requires 50 lakh tonnes of sugarcane, but there is currently not enough supply to operate it at full capacity. Therefore, an ethanol plant will be set up for now. Chaudhary said the factory was shut down because no payment was made during the Samajwadi Party government. He said the factory was originally built with a capacity of 1,250 TCD, which was later increased to 2,500 TCD as sugarcane availability grew. Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh said new bus stands will be built in Shohratgarh and Barhni in Siddharthnagar and Sawayajpur in Hardoi. Land belonging to the Revenue Department will be transferred to the Transport Department for the projects. The rules for setting up Automated Testing Centres have also been changed. Earlier, at least 2.5 acres of land was required for an ATS. Several centres could not be set up due to a lack of available land. Letters of Intent (LOIs) had been issued for 82 ATS centres across the state, but work could progress at only 42 locations. Under the new rules, a one-line ATS will require 1,500 sq m of land, while a two-line centre will require 3,000 sq m. If two-wheeler testing is also included, a three-line ATS will require 3,500 sq m of land. Up to 3 ATS centres to open in each district Earlier, applications for ATS centres were invited through a portal, which was later closed. The portal will now remain open permanently, allowing interested applicants to apply at any time. A maximum of three ATS centres can be opened in each district. A single machine can test around 24,000 vehicles a year. Anyone will be eligible to apply for an ATS. After an LOI is issued, applicants will get six months to start the centre. A 20% reservation will be provided to Agniveers in the recruitment of enforcement constables in the Transport Department. They will also get a seven-year relaxation in the upper age limit. 900 new courts to be built in UP, 6,656 new posts created A total of 900 new courts will be built across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh to hear pending cases. Around 1.20 crore cases are currently pending in district courts. The new courts will include 237 HJS courts, 391 Civil Judge Senior Division courts and 292 Civil Judge Junior Division courts. A total of 6,656 new posts will also be created for these courts. Renting houses and shops to become easier, stamp duty reduced Stamp and Registration Minister Ravindra Jaiswal said renting houses and shops in Uttar Pradesh will now become easier. Earlier, stamp duty was charged at 4% of four times the circle rate of the rented property. For example, if the circle rate of a house was ₹2 lakh, four times the amount would be ₹8 lakh. At 4%, the stamp duty payable was ₹32,000. Under the new system, stamp duty will be ₹1,000 on an annual rent of ₹2 lakh, ₹3,000 on ₹5 lakh, and ₹4,000 on an annual rent of ₹10 lakh. The move will make it easier for people to rent houses and shops.

stories.title: ‘Rohini is far better than Mayawati’:Karni Sena chief says she will be fielded against Chandrashekhar from Nagina
stories.summary: Karni Sena president Suraj Pal Singh Ammu made a major statement about Rohini Ghavri, the former girlfriend of MP Chandrashekhar, in Lucknow on Tuesday. He said, ''My daughter (Rohini Ghavri) is a lakh times better than Mayawati and is well-educated. We will field Rohini in the Lok Sabha election from Nagina." Rohini Ghavri also attended the Karni Sena's Swabhiman Sankalp programme at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. Rohini said, "Young people want categorisation in reservation. If the government does not listen to us, we will change the government. The kind of rules being introduced are causing division in society. We do not want division at all." Key remarks by the former Karni Sena president... We also fought for the Ram temple This is not a temple belonging to the Vishva Hindu Parishad and the RSS. We also fought for the Ram temple and contributed money towards it. Therefore, we also have the right to know how the Ram temple funds were accounted for. We want there to be no caste-based politics in the country. Move beyond dynastic politics: Akhilesh ji, move beyond dynastic politics. We are fighting for the poor. We have no issue with reservation. We want reservation to be available to Brahmins, Banias and every poor person. Justice is needed for daughters, reservation is needed for the poor, and the UJC should be rolled back. Addressing PM Modi, he said, "Listen to what is in our hearts first, and we will listen to your ‘Man Ki Baat’. When we do not listen to the concerns of poor Brahmins, when we do not listen to the concerns of poor Banias, when we do not listen to the concerns of any poor person, how can we listen to you?" Chandrashekhar Ravan is a Muslim: Chandrashekhar Ravan is a Muslim. What do you all say? Something wrong has happened to our girl. A case of love jihad should be registered against her. Why has a case not been registered against Chandrashekhar for 8 months? We are seeking justice from the Supreme Court. She is a daughter of Madhya Pradesh, a daughter of the poor, and our daughter. She must get justice. Read what Rohini Ghavri said We do not want the community to be divided: The youth want categorisation in reservation. If the government does not heed our demands, we will change the government. The kind of rules being introduced are dividing society. We absolutely do not want society to be divided. We are fighting for categorisation. False case under the SC/ST Act: If someone is falsely charged under the SC/ST Act, I stand with that person. But if a Dalit family's child is wronged because of someone's casteist mindset, causing harm to the family, then you must stand with me at that time too. Karni Sena state president Abhinav Singh also raised the issues of casteism and political representation. He said the Karni Sena was often defamed by being labelled casteist, even though caste certificates were issued under the government system and caste was also sought in forms. He said India would change and casteism would end on the day people began tearing up their caste certificates. Karni Sena is preparing to field more than 50 candidates in the upcoming Assembly election. The candidates may belong to any caste, sect, or religion. Anyone who loves India and wants to change the country's image will be allowed to contest the election. We are people who believe in Lord Ram. We have 100 percent faith in Yogi Adityanath.

stories.title: Monkey bites UK tourist at Taj Mahal:Clings to her hand after attack, had also bitten 6-year-old boy
stories.summary: A monkey attacked a woman tourist from the UK who had arrived to visit the Taj Mahal in Agra on Tuesday morning. The woman ran to protect herself, but the monkey bit her hand. People present at the scene managed to rescue her from the monkey. Other tourists who had come to visit the Taj informed the security personnel, after which the woman was immediately sent for treatment. Earlier, in July, a Korean woman was also attacked by monkeys. In fact, tourists visiting the Taj complex remain at risk because of monkeys on a regular basis. Monkey lunges at woman and bites her hand Susan, who had arrived in Agra from the United Kingdom, reached the Taj Mahal at 9:30 a.m. on Tuesday. At around 10 a.m., she was touring the Taj complex with friends when several monkeys suddenly chased her. Susan ran to one side to protect herself. Just then, a monkey lunged at her and bit her right hand. Susan somehow freed herself from the monkey. The injured Susan then began screaming loudly in pain. People nearby immediately informed the guards, after which Susan was taken to a nearby hospital for primary treatment. Tourists say: Ensuring our safety is the ASI's responsibility Tourists present around Susan raised questions about the menace of monkeys in the Taj Mahal complex. They said the ASI should improve arrangements in this regard because it is entirely responsible for ensuring tourists' safety. Tourists said effective measures should be taken to prevent such incidents at a world-famous place like the Taj Mahal, so that people visiting the site face no danger. Monkeys bit a 6-year-old child in the Taj complex On 31 August, six-year-old Ayansh, who had arrived from Haryana to visit the Taj Mahal, was bitten on the hand by a monkey near the guest house. The family informed CISF personnel about the incident. The child was then sent to the hospital for treatment. Earlier, a monkey attacked tourist Mohammed Ali, who had come from Karnataka, near the Western Gate. The monkey bit him on the leg, injuring him. Monkeys have also injured a Korean woman A monkey attacked a woman tourist from South Korea near the eastern gate in July. The monkey bit her hand, causing it to bleed. She was taken to a health centre for treatment. A monkey also attacked a woman tourist from West Bengal. The monkey lunged at her after spotting ice cream in her hand. In June, a monkey bit Chhattisgarh tourist Savitri Bai Kashyap from behind near Amrood Tila.

stories.title: Woman injured in Ayodhya shooting dies in Lucknow:Ruckus outside mortuary; Swami Prasad Maurya says ‘Justice must be served’
stories.summary: Parvati Devi, the mother of Ram Lagan Maurya, who was injured in the Kandaila shooting in Ayodhya, died during treatment in Lucknow on Tuesday. Parvati Devi was injured in the firing on 25 August. She was referred from Ayodhya to KGMU in Lucknow after her condition became critical. She died during treatment. Her son, Ram Lagan Maurya, had died earlier. After the deaths of the mother and son, a large number of people gathered outside the mortuary in Lucknow at around 3 p.m. on Tuesday. The people created a disturbance and demanded the arrest of the absconding named accused. Supporters of Swami Prasad Maurya also reached the spot. This led to a tense atmosphere there for a long time. See three pictures... Meera Singh, Vijaybhan Singh and Vijay Pratap Singh have been named in the case. Police have registered a case against all three under Sections 103 and 109 of the BNS, among other provisions. As all three remain absconding, the Ayodhya SSP has announced a reward of ₹25,000 each for information leading to their arrest. Police have also taken action against Rajmani, Sachin Upadhyay, Prajwal Singh, Deepak Prajapati, Manish Sharma and Indrabhanu Singh in the case. However, the three named accused remain at large. Ram Lagan Maurya was seriously injured in the firing in Kandaila on 25 August. He died during treatment. After the death of her son, Parvati Devi was also battling for her life in critical condition. She has now died as well. The deaths of the mother and son have plunged the family into grief. Relatives and local residents are demanding the early arrest of the named accused. The story is being updated...

stories.title: Man draped in black cloth steals 10.50 kg of gold:Spends 7 hours searching showroom, drinks water; former employee commits biggest jewellery theft in Mathura
stories.summary: Police arrested the man who allegedly stole 10.50 kg of gold and ₹15 lakh in cash from a jewellery showroom in Mathura within seven hours. The gold was valued at ₹14 crore. The accused has been identified as Pappu, a former employee of the businessman. He had been dismissed from the shop six months ago. Police recovered 8 kg of gold and ₹11 lakh in cash from him. The accused took the DVR of the CCTV cameras installed at the shop with him. SSP Shlok Kumar deployed 10 teams to crack the case. Police examined more than 125 CCTV cameras installed in and around the shop. They tracked Pappu’s movements after he left the showroom, and he was seen on some of the cameras. When police showed the CCTV footage to the jeweller, he said he suspected that the person seen in it was Pappu, who had previously worked at the shop. Police then arrested him. Gold and cash worth ₹14 crore stolen in 7 hours Amit Kumar Sarraf lives in Baldevganj. He owns a showroom in the bullion market called Jugal Kishore Amit Kumar and Sons. His showroom was burgled on Sunday night (13 September). The thief took 10.50 kg of gold and ₹15 lakh in cash from the shop. Police investigation revealed that Pappu climbed onto the roof of a neighbouring shop at around 9 pm on Sunday night. He then reached the roof of Amit’s showroom and cut through the iron grille installed there with a cutter. At 9:57 pm, he entered the showroom. He cut open the door of the showroom’s strong room and then opened the safe using a key kept there. He took out the gold and cash and packed them into a bag. Pappu then left the showroom at around 5:15 am. As he left, he also took the CCTV DVR with him to ensure that the recordings did not fall into anyone’s hands. The thief remained inside the showroom for around seven hours. During this time, he also drank water there. He did not touch the silver jewellery, brass utensils or gold-plated jewellery kept in the shop. Thief had covered himself with black cloth CCTV footage from the building opposite the showroom shows that when Pappu came out of the showroom, he was carrying a yellow bag with the showroom’s name printed on it. He was also carrying a backpack over his shoulder. Pappu had covered his entire face-to-waist area with black cloth. Police began examining the subsequent CCTV footage. It showed him leaving the showroom and walking into the lane. During this time, some of the cloth slipped slightly from his face. Thief’s mother, sister and brother also arrested According to police, the thief boarded an e-rickshaw from Baldevganj crossing after passing through the scrap market. He got off before reaching the police outpost and then went to the railway station through the lanes. Police showed the CCTV footage to jeweller Amit. He said that, judging by his build, the man appeared to be Pappu, his former employee who lived in Kosi Kalan. Police then conducted raids to search for him and took Pappu into custody. ADG SK Bhagat held a press conference at 3 pm on Tuesday evening. He said that, besides the 10 police teams, the STF had also been involved in solving the theft. Police have arrested Vishnu alias Pappu Soni, a resident of Mohalla Ramnagar, along with his brother Mohan Soni, and his mother and sister.

stories.title: 'Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha are very smart', says Shubhanshu Shukla:Astronaut tells they need the right guidance; attends Lucknow’s Gomti Book Festival with wife
stories.summary: Lucknow’s astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla told Dainik Bhaskar that Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha are very smart and highly intelligent. “They only need to be shown the right direction; they will reach their destination on their own. I also came this far after moving from a classroom in this city. These children can also achieve this,” he said. Astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla arrived at the ongoing Gomti Book Festival in Lucknow on Tuesday with his wife, son and parents. His book, ‘The Second Orbit’, was launched here. Last year, he travelled to space as part of a joint NASA-ISRO mission and stayed there for more than a month. After returning to Earth, he received a grand welcome in Lucknow. See three pictures- Space is a lot of fun Shubhanshu Shukla told the children, “Space is a lot of fun. When I was there, I did a lot of gymnastics. You can do things there that you cannot do here (on Earth). When I reached space for the first time and looked at Earth, I thought to myself that it was home. It was not about any particular city or state.” He also shared his complete experience of spending eight minutes inside the rocket during the mission with the children. He told them that breathing becomes difficult during that period.

stories.title: Husband and wife’s naked bodies found in forest:Bijnor man found hanging from tree, woman’s body found in river 1 km away, feet tied
stories.summary: The bodies of a husband and wife were found at separate locations in a forest outside their village in Bijnor, around 1 kilometre apart. The wife's nude body was found lying in a river, with her hands tied. The husband's body was found hanging from a tree. They had left home on Monday to cut wood. When they did not return for a long time, their family members began searching for them. The police and family members continued searching until late at night, but found no clue. The family resumed the search on Tuesday. The husband's body was found hanging from a tree in the forest, around 2 kilometres from their home. A noose had been made from the clutch wire of a motorcycle. He was wearing his wife's salwar. Around 1 kilometre away, the wife's semi-nude body was found in a river. The incident took place in Jalalpur Kazi village, 6 kilometres from the district headquarters. The young man's sister suspected that both had been murdered and that her sister-in-law had been raped. The police sent both bodies for post-mortem examinations. The police are currently awaiting the post-mortem report. Read the full story... Deshraj, also known as Chhote (40), a resident of Jalalpur Qazi village, worked as a woodcutter. His family includes his wife, Sushma (37), elder daughter Kamni, and sons Hani and Siddharth, along with his younger daughter Kashish. According to the family, Deshraj went to cut wood on the canal embankment with his wife Sushma at around 10 a.m. on Monday. The couple had been going to the same place to cut wood continuously for the past three days. When the couple had still not returned home even after a considerable amount of time had passed on Monday, their family became worried. They began searching for them. A sickle and slippers were found at one spot in the forest, but there was no trace of either of them. The family then informed the police. The police and relatives launched a joint search for the couple. Despite the search continuing until late at night, no trace of them could be found. Wife's body found in river, husband's body found hanging from tree When police resumed the search with the family on Tuesday morning, Deshraj's body was found at around 10 a.m., hanging from a tree by a motorcycle clutch wire. He was wearing his wife's salwar. His wife's body was found half-naked in the river, with her feet tied with a dupatta. The two bodies were about one kilometre apart. Sister Suspects Murder Deshraj's sister Moni said that when they reached the Ganga today, they found her sister-in-law's body. Her braid was also tied, and there was a noose around her neck. When the body was taken out of the water, it was bleeding. There were no clothes on the lower part of her body. This was clearly murder, not suicide. It could not have been suicide; she was killed. Deshraj's daughter Kashish said that she had been at home and that her parents had left at around 9 a.m. yesterday. Police said-post-mortem report will clarify the cause of death ASP City Dr Krishna Gopal Singh, who reached the scene, said- The bodies of a husband and wife have been found. Both bodies have been sent for post-mortem. A case has been registered on the basis of the complaint, and the entire matter is being investigated.

stories.title: 5 women flee with jewellery in their mouth in Bijnor:Gave shopkeeper a chemical-coated note, stole jewellery worth ₹6 lakh after he felt dizzy
stories.summary: Five women allegedly used chemical-coated notes in Bijnor to buy toe rings and a gold nose stud, leaving the jeweller’s son feeling dizzy. Taking advantage of the situation, they allegedly hid gold jewellery worth around ₹6 lakh in their mouths and fled. According to the shopkeeper, five women had arrived at his shop. They bought jewellery and paid with allegedly chemical-coated notes. Shortly after accepting the notes, the shopkeeper’s son began feeling dizzy. The women then asked him to show them more jewellery, and he continued showing them various items. As he was feeling dizzy and was not fully attentive, the women allegedly stole the gold jewellery. The incident took place on 7 September in Rasulpur Nangla village in the Chandpur area, 45 km from the district headquarters. CCTV footage of the incident emerged late on Monday evening. On the basis of a written complaint filed by the jeweller, police registered an FIR against five unidentified women. Police are working to identify the women using the CCTV footage. See 5 pictures- Here are the full details- Dinesh Verma (50), a resident of Rasulpur Nangla, runs a jewellery shop in the village. Dinesh has two daughters, Ayushi and Sakshi. Both are married. He also has two sons. His elder son, Vipul (24), runs a cosmetics shop in the village, while his younger son, Om Verma (16), works with his father at the jewellery shop. According to Dinesh, at around 2 pm on 7 September, five women wearing burqas came to his jewellery shop. The women began looking at several gold and silver ornaments. During this, one of the women bought a pair of toe rings and a gold nose stud. After making the purchase, the women gave Dinesh’s son, Om Verma, money for the jewellery. Dinesh alleges that the notes had been coated with a chemical. After taking the money, his son’s condition suddenly deteriorated and he was unable to work normally. Women kept looking at the jewellery The women took advantage of Om Verma's feeling dizzy. They kept asking him to show them different pieces of jewellery, and Om continued showing them gold and silver items. During this, one of the women allegedly stole 40 to 50 grams of gold jewellery worth around ₹6 lakh from the shop. The stolen jewellery included three gold pendants, three gold maang tikkas, four pairs of gold earrings and around 30 to 35 gold neck amulets. The five women then left the shop. When Dinesh reached the shop after the women had left, he found that his son did not seem well. When he asked him, his son said he was feeling dizzy. Dinesh then checked the stock kept in the shop and found that some jewellery was missing. The CCTV footage from cameras installed in the shop was subsequently examined. What did the CCTV footage show? The CCTV footage shows two women sitting and looking at the jewellery. During this, the woman wearing a yellow scarf repeatedly picks up jewellery and examines it. As soon as the shopkeeper looks away, the woman puts the jewellery in her mouth. She then picks up some more jewellery and examines it before hiding it in her mouth a second time in the same manner. After a while, when the shopkeeper looks away again, the woman takes the jewellery out of her mouth and hides it in her clothes. Dinesh Verma said the cameras recorded the entire incident, showing all five women entering the shop, looking at the jewellery and leaving with the items. After viewing the footage, Dinesh informed the police about the incident and submitted a written complaint regarding the stolen jewellery. Women are being identified based on CCTV footage Dinesh Verma submitted a written complaint to the police on 12 September. According to Chandpur Station House Officer Rahul Singh, a case has been registered on the basis of the complaint. The shop’s CCTV footage has been made part of the investigation. Police are identifying the women based on the footage and investigating their role. They are also investigating whether the notes actually had any chemical applied to them and what caused the shopkeeper’s son’s health to deteriorate.

stories.title: Wife dies during delivery hours after police detain husband:Family in Firozabad alleges cops kicked her in the stomach; 6 policemen suspended
stories.summary: A pregnant woman died in Firozabad after giving birth, after her husband was detained on suspicion of theft. The family alleges that on Sunday night, when the woman protested against the police taking her husband to the station, police personnel pushed her and kicked her in the stomach. Despite this, the police took her husband to the station. After her husband was taken to the station, the woman’s condition began to deteriorate. Her family took her to hospital that night. She gave birth to a son at the hospital on Monday morning and then died. Angered by the incident, family members and villagers surrounded the police station and created a ruckus for two hours. They broke chairs inside the station. SP Aditya Langhe suspended six police personnel, including two sub-inspectors, on Tuesday morning. The incident took place in the Shikohabad police station area, 28 km from the district headquarters. SP Aditya Langhe said- The police knew that his wife was due to give birth. Despite this, bringing the young man to the police station at night was negligence. Therefore, action was taken. A post-mortem was conducted by a panel of doctors to ascertain the exact cause of the woman’s death. The report has not yet arrived. The allegations against the police are being investigated. See two pictures of the commotion- Policemen entered the house by jumping over the gate Gaurav, 30, a resident of Labhua village, works as a photographer. He runs a studio called Rudra Photo in the village. Gaurav married Anjali, 28, 12 years ago. Anjali was nine months pregnant. Gaurav said, “A theft took place at villager Jahesh Kumar’s grocery shop on Friday night.” “The owner of the shop where the theft took place had a dispute with my uncle and village head Kailash Babu a year ago. He had intervened at the time and brokered a settlement between the two sides. The father of his associate Ajendra had also supported the village head’s side at the time. Because of this old enmity, the shopkeeper gave the police my name and Ajendra’s name in connection with the theft.” Gaurav said, “The power went out at 10:30 pm on Sunday night. It was very hot, so I was going to sleep on the roof with my wife Anjali and our child. I went up to the roof to put down the bedding and pillow when policemen jumped over the gate and entered the house. They began dragging me away. My wife pleaded with the police to release me.” Policemen pushed my wife aside and took me to the police station Gaurav said, “The police personnel said that the sub-inspector was standing on the road and that they would send me back home after questioning me.” After this, his wife folded her hands and told the police personnel, “You can conduct whatever questioning is required at home. Do not take my husband with you at night.” During this, the police personnel pushed Anjali, causing her to fall to the ground. Gaurav alleges that sub-inspector Dharampal Singh kicked him in the stomach. Despite his wife’s pleas, the police took him to the police station. He pleaded to be allowed to go home, but they did not release him. The police personnel misbehaved with him and threatened to assault him when he protested. Wife’s condition worsened after husband went to police station Relatives said Anjali’s condition deteriorated further after Gaurav went to the police station. They took her to the Combined District Hospital in Shikohabad. Her condition there was critical, and she also suffered heavy bleeding. At around 9:30 am on Monday, Anjali gave birth to a son. Her condition worsened further after the delivery. Doctors referred her to another hospital. The family took her to the private Laxmi Foundation Hospital in the city. Anjali died during treatment there. 2-hour protest at police station after news of death As news of Anjali’s death reached the village, her family and villagers reached Shikohabad police station in tractors. The women threw chairs inside the police station and began raising slogans against the police and administration. On being informed of the disturbance, SP Rural Anuj Chaudhary reached the spot. Police from Makkhanpur, Sirsaganj and Nasirpur police stations were called in. The family demanded action against the police personnel responsible and an impartial investigation. Police officials assured them that action would be taken. The villagers then calmed down. Anjali’s body was taken for post-mortem under police security. Her last rites were performed in the village late on Monday evening. Haemoglobin was 5 grams, blood pressure suddenly dropped Joint Hospital CMS Dr RC Keshav said- Anjali’s haemoglobin was around 5 grams. Her blood pressure suddenly dropped after delivery. She was referred to the medical college when her condition became critical. A panel conducted the post-mortem to establish the exact cause of the woman’s death. The cause of death will become clearer after the post-mortem report and investigation.

stories.title: Youth forced to give blood to pay phone instalment:Lucknow men abducted him, held him captive for forced labour and threatened to throw him into Gomti river
stories.summary: A shopkeeper in Lucknow has been accused of making a young man bleed over a mobile-phone instalment. According to the family, the accused forcibly took the young man from his home, held him captive for five days and made him work as a labourer. They made his elder brother transfer ₹2,799 online towards the instalment. Even then, they did not release him and demanded another ₹12,000. They also threatened to kill him and throw him into the Gomti if he complained to the police. The family then informed the police, who rescued the young man from the shopkeeper’s custody. The family alleges that when they complained at the police station, the police took no action and instead threatened to implicate the young man. On Monday, the victim’s mother reached the DCP’s office and filed a complaint. The DCP directed the Nigohan station house officer to immediately register a case and arrest the accused. The incident took place in Rajaramkheda village under Nigohan police station. Phone bought for ₹21,500, payable in 12 monthly instalments The victim Naval’s elder brother, Rajkumar, said that a year ago, they bought a Samsung phone from Geeta Mobile Shop in Nigohan town with zero down payment. The phone cost ₹21,500 and was to be paid for in 12 monthly instalments of ₹2,799. The very next month after the phone was bought, employees from the shop arrived and took the mobile phone away. Son was forced to work The victim’s mother, Jadurai, said that on 8 September, two people arrived in the village on a scooter and took Naval away. The accused took him to a blood bank in Lucknow, where they had his blood extracted. They then held him captive for five days in a house in the Sadar area and forced him to work. The mother said, “After taking Naval hostage, the accused called his elder brother Rajkumar and had the instalment payment of ₹2,799 transferred online. When they were asked to release Naval, the accused demanded another ₹12,000. They threatened to kill him and throw him into the Gomti if the money was not paid. The family then informed the police. After police intervention, the accused agreed on the fifth day to send Naval to the police station in a Rapid cab. They made his elder brother pay the cab fare as well.” Family members said police intimidated them when they demanded action According to the family, Naval was in a distraught condition when he reached the police station. When they demanded action, the police instead intimidated them, saying that Naval would also be framed. He was then sent home. After reaching home, Naval told his family what had happened to him. His mother then went to the Nigohan police station to file a complaint, but alleged that she was turned away. DCP Mohammed Mushtaq said- The victim’s complaint has been taken seriously. The station house officer has been directed to immediately register a case and arrest the accused. The police’s negligence will also be investigated.

stories.summary: A woman was bludgeoned to death in Lucknow's Krishnanagar area. The incident is reported to have taken place near Mansarovar Market. She was killed late on Monday night and her body was dumped by the roadside. On Tuesday morning, local residents saw the bloodstained body and informed the police. This is the second murder in Krishnanagar in 24 hours. Police reached the spot, took the body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. A forensic team also reached the spot. The woman has been identified as Radha, aged around 30-32. Earlier on Monday, a 32-year-old man was killed by having his throat slit. His body was found on a pile of sand by the roadside. See three pictures- Inspector says-man living with her has fled Krishnanagar Inspector P.K. Singh said, "She was a nomadic-type woman. Serious injury marks were found on her head. Enquiries with local residents revealed that she lived on the street with a man named Bhola. The man has been missing since the incident. CCTV cameras installed around the scene are being examined."

stories.title: India’s first supercomputer shuts down:New data analysis and computational work affected; installed at IIT-BHU in 2019
stories.summary: Services of the Param Shivay supercomputer, established at IIT-BHU around seven years ago, are currently affected. New data analysis and computation-related work cannot be carried out on the supercomputer. However, users can download and back up their existing essential data. The institute said this situation is not due to a permanent shutdown, but has arisen because of system maintenance and modernisation. Now, learn how the matter came to light Discussion about Param Shivay intensified at the institute after an old message concerning it was circulated. The message informed users that Param Shivay’s services would remain suspended from 5 September and that, during this period, users would only be able to retrieve their data and create a backup. They were also advised not to submit new computational jobs. The message also stated that the SLURM compute-node configuration had been removed, making it impossible to submit new jobs on the system. Users were given a final reminder to download and back up essential data stored on the server. In addition, researchers and users requiring computing facilities were informed that they could apply for other National Supercomputing Mission (NSM) facilities through the relevant portal. Param Shivay was established in 2019 The Param Shivay supercomputer was installed at IIT-BHU on 19 February 2019 in a building located near the Department of Electronics Engineering. Since then, it has served as an important resource for high-speed data processing and computation at the institute, as well as for scientists and researchers associated with BHU and various institutions across the country. With the help of supercomputers, scientists can complete complex calculations, large-scale data analysis and research-related tasks in less time. The computing capacity of Param Shivay has also been used in several ongoing research projects at IIT-BHU and BHU. With its services currently affected, researchers whose work requires high-performance computing may face difficulties. Repair and modernisation work under way Dr Nisha Singh, a system analyst at the Supercomputing Centre, said server maintenance work had been under way since 5 September. Necessary repairs were being carried out on the system, and efforts were being made to restore it to normal as soon as possible. She clarified that the system was not merely being shut down, but was also being modernised. Computing services are expected to resume smoothly after the maintenance and upgrade process is completed. Areas where ‘Param Shivay’ was used Indigenous supercomputer software had been developed for scientific applications. It was being used for simulation and modelling in several areas, including climate modelling, weather forecasting, space engineering, seismic analysis, finance, disaster simulation and management, large-scale data analytics and information gathering.

stories.title: 'How to kill someone and make it look like suicide':Daughter-in-law googled this before murdering her millionaire father-in-law
stories.summary: New revelations are emerging in the police investigation into the murder of Kanpur millionaire pharmaceutical businessman Vineet Minocha. According to the police, before the murder, the accused daughter-in-law, Shalu, searched on Google: “How to kill a man so that it looks like suicide, not murder?” The police have obtained 1,000 pages of call detail records (CDRs) for seven mobile numbers belonging to the businessman’s son, Subrat, Shalu and contract killer Vishal. The records contain call details from 1 May to 6 September. DCP Qasim Abidi said information about conversations before and after the murder was being gathered from the CDRs. The investigation revealed that Vishal called a friend five times after the murder. He then travelled by Uber to his hideout. The police are examining Uber’s route map, the driver’s statement and digital payment records. The businessman was murdered on the night of 5 September. The accused daughter-in-law, Shalu, domestic worker Vishal Gautam and his associate Rajkishore are in jail. During questioning, Shalu had said, “My father-in-law had imposed restrictions on me. That is why I had him murdered.” Shalu and Vishal questioned in jail, asked more than 30 questions According to sources, Investigating Officer Inspector Keshav Kumar Tiwari questioned Shalu and Vishal in jail. More than 30 questions were asked. These covered the planning of the murder, their conversations with each other and their activities after the incident. Businessman’s son Subrat also under investigation According to the DCP West, Subrat and Vishal spoke around 309 times between 1 May and the murder. The two remained in contact despite Vishal being dismissed from his job over allegations of theft. Subrat has also been questioned about the identification of Vishal in CCTV footage. The statements and digital records are now being matched. The police are preparing to seek the remand of Shalu and Vishal. They may then confront Subrat with both of them. Vishal changed his SIM 2 days before the murder According to the police, Vishal had two SIM cards. After planning the murder, he deactivated his old SIM and took a new number two days before the crime. He used this number to stay in contact with Subrat and Shalu. On the day of the murder, Subrat spoke to Vishal 25 times, while Shalu spoke to him 14 times. 2022 will is also under investigation Vineet Minocha ran a pharmaceutical firm called ‘Pharma Traders’ on Birhana Road. He managed the business with his son, Subrat. The firm’s annual turnover is reported to be ₹50 crore to ₹60 crore. Police are also investigating the angles of a property dispute and greed. According to the police, in 2022, Vineet made a will bequeathing property worth crores to his wife, Punita, son Subrat and daughter Shubhani. Punita had been living separately from her husband in Ghaziabad with their daughter for a long time. She is a marriage counsellor. Mother did not attend Subrat’s roka ceremony According to Shalu’s brother Dheeraj Arora, a roka ceremony was held in Lucknow after Subrat and Shalu’s marriage was fixed. Subrat’s relatives attended, but his mother, Punita, did not come. She spoke to Shalu over a video call and blessed her. Punita had been living in Ghaziabad even before the wedding. Police are looking for answers to these questions

stories.title: 6-year fight ends as ₹3.94 lakh fine waived:Gorakhpur Chamber of Commerce fought a long battle; Bhutan-bound goods had been seized
stories.summary: A state tax department mobile squad seized goods belonging to a Kolkata firm six years ago. The traders termed the action wrong, but the department ultimately imposed a fine of ₹3,94,642. When they received no relief, an appeal was filed in the matter. As the firm was based outside the state, it contacted Chamber of Commerce president Sanjay Singhania. Under Sanjay's supervision, the facts of the case were presented before the appellate authority. A decision was delivered nearly six years later, and the fine was cancelled. Sanjay Singhania said, "On 3 February 2020, the mobile squad stopped a commercial vehicle near Tenua toll plaza. The trader then contacted the Chamber of Commerce." He said the trader was openly harassed in violation of the rules. The matter was also raised at a Vyapar Bandhu meeting held under the chairmanship of the district magistrate. However, the trader did not receive justice. The mobile squad officer then imposed a fine of ₹3,94,642. The goods were being sent to Bhutan The truck that was seized was carrying goods to Bhutan. A hearing in the matter was under way before the Additional Commissioner, Grade 2. After hearing both sides, an order was issued stating that no intention to evade tax had been found. The fine was subsequently waived. Singhania said the decision was a stinging slap in the face of officials involved in irregularities. He said the victory belonged to the entire trading community. The president of the Chamber of Commerce said that transparency and ease of doing business in every activity were the organisation's top priorities. He said that he and his organisation would always stand up to protect the interests of traders.

In Siddharthnagar, a wall collapsed amid the rain. The 20-foot-long wall came crashing down in just 4 seconds. In Lakhimpur, erosion along the Sharda River has intensified. Seven houses were washed away into the river within 24 hours. In Chandauli, Musakhad, Latifshah and Bhaisoda dams overflowed on Tuesday morning due to rain. Around 2,270 cusecs of water were released from the three dams. Water was seen cascading from Latifshah Dam like a waterfall. The Ganga has risen again in Badaun, with water flowing over a bridge. Several areas are now facing the threat of flooding. Heavy rain lashed Kashi at around 11 am today. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 72 districts. Four people have died in rain- and flood-related incidents in the past 24 hours. Two youths were killed by lightning in Ballia, while a farmer died in Balrampur. In Farrukhabad, a three-year-old child drowned in floodwater. See photos of rain and flood- Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said — A system has formed over the Bay of Bengal. stories.title: UP IAS officer Divya Mittal’s resignation accepted:Writes 'Prashast punya panth hai, badhe chalo, badhe chalo'; quit service 15 days ago
stories.summary: The Central Government has accepted the resignation of Uttar Pradesh-cadre IAS officer Divya Mittal. She resigned from the service on 30 August, citing personal reasons, family priorities and new goals in life. In May, Divya Mittal was removed as Deoria District Magistrate and appointed Special Secretary in the Revenue Department. At around 11 pm on Monday, she posted on X confirming that her resignation had been accepted. Along with the announcement, she quoted a line from poet Jaishankar Prasad's play Chandragupta: "Prashast punya panth hai, badhe chalo, badhe chalo." Here are the full lines of the poem quoted by Divya Mittal… Himadri tung shring se, Prabuddh shuddh Bharati, Svayamprabha samujjwala, Swatantrata pukarti! Amartya Veer Putra ho, Dridh-pratigya soch lo, Prashast punya panth hai, Badhe chalo, badhe chalo! Asankhya kirti-rashmiyan, Vikirn divya daah-si, Sapoot matribhoomi ke, Ruko na shoor sahasi! Arati sainya sindhu mein, Subadavagni se jalo, Praveer ho jayi bano, Badhe chalo, badhe chalo! "Prashast punya panth hai": This means that the path of protecting the motherland and securing freedom is vast, clear and sacred. "Badhe chalo, badhe chalo": The poet calls upon the brave sons of the country and soldiers to continue moving forward on this sacred path without stopping or being afraid. Divya had 17 years of service left A 2013-batch officer, Divya had served for 13 years and had 17 years of service remaining. After completing her BTech from IIT Delhi and MBA from IIM Bangalore, she worked in London. She left a job paying lakhs of rupees and returned to India. She cleared the UPSC examination twice within two years. She became an IPS officer on her first attempt and an IAS officer the following year. Divya's husband, Gagandeep Singh, is also a 2011-batch Indian Trade Service (ITS) officer. He too resigned from his post in 2022. Gagandeep founded a company called 'Neurocap'. The company is involved in trading in India and abroad. Divya Mittal has served as District Magistrate of Mirzapur, Basti and Deoria. She is considered to have a very strict image and was known to reprimand officials on the spot. She was transferred from Deoria to Lucknow just four months ago. Divya left her London job to join the civil services Divya is originally from Rewari in Haryana. After studying at IIT and IIM, she worked in London. She met Gagandeep Singh there. The two had a love marriage. However, a few years later, both husband and wife left their jobs in London and returned to India. Divya began preparing for the UPSC examination. Without coaching, she cleared the IPS examination on her first attempt and was allotted the Gujarat cadre. She continued preparing for the IAS examination while undergoing IPS training. The following year, in 2013, she was selected for the IAS. Divya's husband is from Punjab and cleared UPSC on his first attempt Divya's husband, Gagandeep Singh, comes from Gidderbaha in Punjab's Bathinda district. He studied Chemical Engineering at IIT Delhi from 1998 to 2002. He then studied management at IIM Bangalore from 2003 to 2005. Gagandeep cleared the UPSC examination in 2010 on his first attempt and was selected for the Indian Trade Service. Four years ago, in 2022, he resigned as Joint Director-General in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

stories.title: Minister Nishad meets Opposition Leader:Posts photo with SP leader, sparking speculation over a possible switch
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Dr Sanjay Nishad met Assembly Leader of the Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey at his residence on Monday. Nishad Party president Sanjay Nishad presented him with a bouquet. The meeting took place at a time when elections in Uttar Pradesh are due to be held in the next few months. The meeting has fuelled speculation in political circles about whether Sanjay Nishad could join the Samajwadi Party. This comes after Nishad recently began targeting his own government. Three days ago, following the murder of Vinod Sahani in Gonda, he staged a protest against his own government. He has also indicated on several occasions that if he does not receive due respect, other options would remain open to him. However, Sanjay Nishad described the meeting as a courtesy call. Posting photographs on Facebook, he wrote, “Paid a courtesy call on Mata Prasad Pandey ji at his residence. During the meeting, we discussed various contemporary issues.” Akhilesh also met Mata Prasad Pandey two days ago Mata Prasad Pandey is reportedly unwell these days. Two days ago, Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav also visited him and enquired about his health. For now, Sanjay Nishad has given no indication of any political change. Read when Sanjay Nishad confronted the government Businessman murder case: After the murder of Gonda utensils trader Vinod Sahani, Sanjay Nishad staged a sit-in outside KGMU in Lucknow. He then also staged a sit-in at the Gonda Collectorate. He said, "I warn the administration that crime has no caste. The accused should be killed in an encounter, and bulldozers should be used on their illegal properties." August 2026: Sanjay Nishad warned the government over the issue of reservation for the Nishad community. He said, "We are with the BJP, but if there is a delay in reservation, we will stage a sit-in. You can take away the ministerial post if you want." June 2026: He raised questions over the encounter of Kamlesh Bind in Ghazipur. He said, "The main accused in the Vineet Rai murder case are still untouched. Take action against them and show us. This is an attitude marked by discrimination against the Nishad-Bind community. Some officials are creating an atmosphere against the government." January: At the Nishad Party's foundation day, Sanjay Nishad said, "The fishing community is not the vote bank of any single party. It has the power to make or unmake governments." July 2024: After the Lok Sabha election, Sanjay Nishad questioned the government and officials over bulldozer action. He said, "Using bulldozers against criminals is justified, but not against the poor. Demolishing poor people's homes without an investigation harmed the BJP in the election." April 2023: Sanjay Nishad expressed displeasure over the failure to release funds for the Fishermen's Welfare Fund. He said, “This is an insult to the fishing community. If money is not provided even for the work announced in the manifesto, how will the work be carried out?” Had allied with the SP in 2018 In 2018, the Nishad Party allied with the SP. The minister's son, Praveen Nishad, contested the Gorakhpur Lok Sabha by-election on an SP ticket and entered the Lok Sabha after winning the election. However, the following year, in 2019, the Nishad Party joined hands with the BJP.

stories.title: Trader’s son says, ‘Minister Nishad is coming to make photo-videos’:Father raised Nishad community’s voice; was beaten to death in Gonda
stories.summary: Raja Sahni, son of Gonda trader Vinod Sahni (Nishad), who was killed, said his father had been raising his voice for the Nishad community. He alleged that his father responded to people on Facebook in the same language they used with him. “Mahant Raju Das abused my father, but no encounter took place against him. His people were not killed, but my father was murdered. Sanjay Nishad is only coming here to get his video made for social media,” Raja said. Family demands arrest, strict action against accused Raja said the family’s immediate demand was the arrest of the accused at the earliest. “The action that Chief Minister Yogi talks about, including encounters and bulldozers, should be taken. If action is not taken now, then when will it be? We are continuously receiving threats on social media,” he said. He said the family was not satisfied with the action taken so far and remained concerned about its safety. Family speaks to Dainik Bhaskar about its concerns The Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to the bereaved family and learnt about their grief, concerns and demands following Vinod Sahni’s murder. Read the full report... First, know what happened Utensil trader Vinod Kumar Sahni, 45, lived in Reksadia village under the Parspur police station area. His family includes his wife, Usha; two daughters, Ragini and Vijaylakshmi; and son Raja Sahni. His elder daughter Ragini is married. His younger brothers, Vinay and Amit, also live with their families. Vinod attacked while returning home from shop At around 8 pm on Wednesday, September 9, Vinod was returning home after closing his shop when 8-10 people allegedly stopped and attacked him. He was beaten severely and left covered in blood. As his condition was critical, doctors referred him to King George’s Medical University (KGMU) in Lucknow. Vinod died during treatment at around 3 pm on Thursday, September 10. Sanjay Nishad stages protests after trader’s death After learning about Vinod’s death, Minister Dr Sanjay Nishad reached KGMU and sat in protest. Following this, the SP suspended three police personnel. The next day, Sanjay Nishad reached Gonda and marched on foot from the Circuit House to the Collectorate, where he staged another protest. So far, three accused have been arrested in connection with the case. Now, read what the family told us... Son says, ‘I am receiving threats on social media’ Vinod Sahni’s son, Raja Sahni, said there had been a delay in arresting the accused. “The kind of encounters and bulldozer action Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath talks about is needed.” He added, “We have continued to receive threats even after my father’s murder. They tell us, ‘This is nothing yet; more will happen.’” Facebook dispute took place 18 months ago Raja said the Facebook incident took place around a year and a half ago. Someone had tagged his father in a post using abusive language, to which he responded in similar language. His father was subsequently jailed and fined in the case. Raja recalls Ayodhya ‘fish feast’ controversy Speaking about the ‘fish feast’ controversy in Ayodhya, Raja alleged that Mahant Raju Das had used extremely abusive and profane language. He said his father had raised his voice against the remarks. ‘The administration is trying to suppress the case’ Raja alleged that the administration was trying to suppress the case by preventing people from outside the area from coming. He said Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad belongs to their community, but alleged that his efforts to seek justice had not produced the expected results. Raja said, “We feel he comes because he wants to post videos on social media.” Brother says family may be forced to leave home Vinod’s younger brother, Vinay Kumar Sahni, said opponents disliked his brother for raising his voice for the fishing community. He said, “None of our demands have been met so far. We are receiving threats on social media. We will have no choice but to leave our homes.” He added, “Sanatan has grown so much that it is gradually becoming hollow from within.” Cause of murder unclear, investigation under way on several fronts... Had switched between SP, Nishad Party and Azad Samaj Party Vinod was active in politics and had initially joined the Samajwadi Party, but left within a few days. He later joined the Nishad Party, but eventually quit after opposing the party’s policies and its leader, Sanjay Nishad. Joined Mukesh Sahani’s VIP before his murder Vinod later joined Chandrashekhar Azad’s Azad Samaj Party for some time. After his murder, Chandrashekhar claimed that Vinod had contacted him a few months ago to contest the election from the Colonelganj Assembly constituency. At the time of his death, Vinod was associated with Bihar-based leader Mukesh Sahani’s Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP). Sanjay Nishad active since Vinod Sahani’s murder Sanjay Nishad has remained active since Vinod Sahani’s murder. He has stayed in touch with the bereaved family, staged a sit-in protest and taken out a foot march demanding justice. Vinod had accused Sanjay Nishad of betraying the community However, Vinod Sahani had repeatedly accused Sanjay Nishad and his sons of deceiving the Nishad community. He had alleged that they were only enjoying the benefits of power, cheating the community and betraying its interests. Some of Vinod Sahani's posts against Sanjay Nishad... Questions raised over Sanjay Nishad’s support for Vinod After Vinod’s death, Dr Sanjay Nishad described him as the Nishad Party’s “district campaigner”. However, questions are being raised over why Sanjay Nishad came out in support of Vinod despite his repeated opposition to the minister. Nishad Party confirms Vinod left three years ago Ram Anand Nishad, Nishad Party’s Gonda district president, confirmed that Vinod had left the party three years ago and was currently associated with the VIP. He acknowledged that Vinod had consistently written against the party. However, Ram Anand said party office-bearers had to be present when the minister visited because they belonged to the same community.
