stories.title: ‘I came to make others contest, not contest myself’:Rohini Ghavri says she will back those, not Akhilesh or Congress, who give Valmiki's political representation
stories.summary: After spending 6 years in Switzerland, Rohini Ghavri has returned to India to work towards strengthening the Valmiki community politically. She completed her doctorate and worked in Switzerland for two years before returning. After visiting Delhi, Haryana and Meerut, she has now reached Lucknow. In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Rohini spoke openly about the creamy layer in reservations, political representation for the Valmiki community, the 2027 Assembly elections, Akhilesh Yadav, Mayawati and Chandrashekhar Azad. She said her personal goal is not to contest elections but to help people from her community contest and reach the Assembly and Parliament. Read the full interview… Question: Why did you return to India after spending 6 years in Switzerland? Answer: I went to Switzerland for my studies and completed my PhD. People often forget their families after living abroad, but I could not forget the pain of my community and its people. I was constantly writing about their issues. I returned to India to do the work I wanted to see bringing about change in my country. Question: You had said that you would make a person from the Valmiki community, CM within the next 5-years. What is the roadmap? Answer: I am not saying that the Chief Minister has to be from Uttar Pradesh. We have a significant population in states such as Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, and Madhya Pradesh. Every section of society has been given opportunities in our country. We demand that a community which was for years considered fit only for sanitation work should also reach positions of power. Question: You had spoken about economic-based reservation and changes to the existing caste system? Answer: We support the classification of reservations as per the Supreme Court’s 1st August, 2024, judgment. If it can be implemented in Haryana, Telangana, and Punjab, why not in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, or Rajasthan? Only a few castes have been benefiting from reservation for generations. The benefits of reservation should reach people from communities living in slums. Question: Do you want the creamy layer system to be implemented? Answer: Absolutely, I support the implementation of the creamy layer. My mother, grandmother, and maternal grandmother were sanitation workers. I benefited from reservation, went abroad to study, and later worked on a good package. Now, the next generation of my family should not get the benefit of reservation. Question: Have you decided to enter politics? Answer: The journey from a slum to Switzerland was extremely difficult for me. I went from a home where I had to depend on others for food as a child to eventually reaching Switzerland. Now, my next goal is to bring my community into positions of power. Even in the 80th year of Independence, the Valmiki community is still looking for national leadership of its own. Question: There is talk of you joining Akhilesh Yadav or Congress? Answer: Our condition is clear: We will go with the party that gives us political representation. We will support any party that implements reservation classification and gives the Valmiki community its due share. If the BJP accepts our demands, we will go with the BJP. If Akhilesh Yadav implements reservation classification and gives us proper representation, such as 10 tickets, we will support him. Question: Will you contest the 2027 UP Assembly elections? Answer: I have not come here to contest elections, but to help people from my community contest them. A true leader is one who creates new leadership. Simply holding a position and sitting there is not leadership. Question: What guarantee is there that the people you help contest elections will stay with you after winning? Answer: The first priority is to get tickets for my brothers and sisters, help them win, and get them into the Assembly. Question: How do you view Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘PDA’ (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) slogan? Answer: Akhilesh ji’s work over the past year has been commendable. He is trying to bring together victims, Dalits, the oppressed, and minorities. He is also talking about issues concerning youth and education. UP wants change, and he should be given a chance once. Question: Is there a possibility of meeting Akhilesh Yadav during the two days? Answer: Absolutely. I had also spoken to him while I was living in Switzerland. At the time, he told me to let him know when I came to Lucknow. I will meet him and put the demands and rights of my community before him. Question: Have you spoken to or met your sister Mayawati? Answer: I have not spoken to Behenji directly, but I have been in touch with people close to her. Behenji will always remain my role model. Question: Of the three models of the Dalit movement: BSP, SP’s PDA, and Chandrashekhar Azad, which do you consider better? Answer: When the BSP first emerged, its model was widely appreciated. People joined and supported it. This is why Behenji became Chief Minister four times. The PDA model is still new. Akhilesh Yadav has been working for a long time, and now a large section of the Jatav community is also aligning with him. They see him as an alternative. I have also seen people from the Valmiki community joining him. As for the third model, I do not consider it a model. It is a strategy to establish one individual. I do not see any model for the welfare and upliftment of the community in it. Question: What would you say about slogans raised in your support during Chandrashekhar Azad’s programme in Barabanki? Answer: I came to know about it late at night. I do not know who those people were. The police have also denied that any such incident took place. But whoever does anything wrong will face the consequences. People across the country who consider me their sister are standing up for justice for me. Question: After returning to India, Karni Sena appears to be supporting you Answer: Karni Sena has supported my fight without any vested interest. Since I addressed the United Nations (UN) in 2023, people from all sections of society have been standing with me. Question: Based on your experience of working with Chandrashekhar, what do you consider his strengths and weaknesses? Answer: His strength is his ability to influence people through his words. But his weakness is that he has no clear vision, policy, or blueprint. A person who is concerned about his position, pension, bungalow, and luxury rather than the welfare of society cannot be a leader of social movements. Question: What was the reason for separating from Chandrashekhar? Answer: A person who cannot be honest in personal relationships cannot be honest in society or politics either. Several state presidents of the organisation were in touch with me, and the truth from within the organisation was that only hype was being created in the name of the community. There was no ground-level work. Question: How did your family and father support you in this fight? Answer: My father is known for his honesty in Indore. He even left his job for our education. When I faced a crisis, my parents and brother stood firmly by me. It is because of my family’s trust that I am standing fearlessly today. Question: Will you get married? Answer: Absolutely not. ''I have made a very strict decision on this. I don’t have time anymore. I am 33 years old. The five to six years that were wasted could have been the time when I got married. That opportunity was lost. If I had met an honest person at that time, perhaps I could have built a family. I also wanted to become a bride. I had dreams too. I had dreamed of a beautiful wedding. I had the same dreams as any ordinary girl, about what kind of lehenga I would wear and what kind of gold jewellery I would buy. But I know what it feels like to have those dreams shattered. Even after making so many sacrifices, people are still telling me that I am wrong. Why? Because I am an ordinary girl and he is an MP. The same people who are abusing me today, I feel, will soon circulate edited pictures of me without clothes and say, ‘This is the kind of girl she is.’ Where is the Bahujan unity? No Brahmin is doing this to me. No Rajput is doing it. Neither a Thakur nor a Muslim. It is the same people from the Bahujan community who talk about unity.'' Question: After turning 33, are you planning to dedicate your entire life to society? Answer: Yes, I have given up my personal life. I no longer have any plans to marry or start a family of my own. Inspired by the lives of Babasaheb Ambedkar, Manyavar Kanshi Ram, and Behen Mayawati, I have decided to dedicate my entire life to fighting for the rights of the Valmiki community and the Bahujan community.

stories.title: UP leaders are organising religious stories, not public rallies:Raja Bhaiya invites Dhirendra Shastri; Manoj Pandey organises Shiv Mahapuran
stories.summary: UP Assembly elections may be fought this time with faith at the centre. Several political leaders are turning to religious events to strengthen their electoral prospects. Ram Katha, Shiv Mahapuran and Shrimad Bhagwat are being organised in different places, with well-known storytellers being invited for these events. Leaders are also planning to attract large crowds through bhajan evenings during Ganesh Utsav and Navratri. What can leaders gain from organising so many religious events in UP? Experts believe it is no longer easy to gather crowds in the name of election rallies. Religion and faith make it easier to bring people together at one place. Such events can also help leaders build and strengthen several electoral equations. This trend is more visible among leaders from eastern UP. UP Cabinet minister Manoj Pandey is organising a Shiv Mahapuran Katha by famous storyteller Pandit Pradeep Mishra, popularly known as ‘Sehore Wale’, in Unchahar, Rae Bareli. Around 50,000 to 80,000 people are reportedly gathering every day. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also visited the event on 13 September and addressed the gathering. BJP organisation office-bearers are also visiting the venue. Kunda MLA Raja Bhaiya is set to organise a Hanumant Katha by Pandit Dhirendra Shastri, popularly known as Bageshwar Baba, from 17 to 19 November. More than 2 lakh people are expected to come to Kunda every day from Pratapgarh, Kaushambi, Prayagraj and nearby districts. Raja Bhaiya’s party is preparing to field candidates not only from Babaganj but also from several seats in Pratapgarh, Kaushambi and Prayagraj in the upcoming Assembly elections. In Diuli, Ballia, minister Dayashankar Singh had organised a Shiv Mahapuran Katha by Pandit Pradeep Mishra near Baba Balkhandi Temple from 9 to 15 June. Earlier, from 20 to 28 March, he had organised a Shri Lakshmi Narayan Yagya at Rajghat on the banks of the Saryu in Ayodhya. On the final day, the entire pandal caught fire and was destroyed. Former BJP MLA Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh organised a Ram Katha by Sant Riteshwar Maharaj in Kaiserganj, Gonda, from 4 to 6 January. During the event, Sant Riteshwar Maharaj praised Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh for his spirituality and spirit of service. BJP aspirants are also organising religious events Neeraj Bora (BJP MLA, Lucknow North) From 1 to 9 June 2026, he organised a Ram Katha by Jagadguru Rambhadracharya at his office on Sitapur Road. Yogi Adityanath also attended the event. During the Katha, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya said politics should not be about holding a position but should be a means of serving religion and people selflessly. Ketki Singh (BJP MLA, Bansdih, Ballia) From 22 to 30 June 2026, she organised a grand Shri Ram Katha by Rajan Ji Maharaj. The event was held at Baba Amarnath Temple premises in Karihara, Beruarbari. Around 50,000 to 60,000 people attended every day. Dr Uday Pratap Singh (BJP ticket aspirant) To strengthen his claim for the Prayagraj West and South seats, he spent crores of rupees to organise Pandit Dhirendra Shastri’s ‘Shri Hanumant Katha’. The event was held from 21 to 23 April 2026. Abhay Singh (MLA, Gosainganj, Ayodhya) From 14 to 20 March 2026, he organised a Shrimad Bhagwat recital at his ancestral home in Rajepur village, which was attended by several ministers and MLAs. Through the event, he attempted to change his strongman image and embrace the BJP’s political identity after joining the party. Udaybhan Karwariya (BJP leader, Prayagraj) A nine-day Shri Ram Katha was held at Devbra Dham in Handia from 28 March to 5 April 2026. The storyteller was Rajan Ji Maharaj. RSS pracharak Sanjay Bhai Joshi also attended the event. Arun Singh (Chairman, District Cooperative Bank, Unnao) He is staking his claim for the BJP ticket from Bhagwantnagar Assembly seat. Arun Singh has organised a Shiv Mahapuran Katha by Pandit Pradeep Mishra, which will be held from 30 October to 5 November 2026. Rajeshwar Singh (BJP MLA, Sarojini Nagar) He organised a music show by Honey Singh on 22 November 2025 and a grand roadshow by Sanjay Dutt on 22 February 2026. After receiving feedback that elderly voters were unhappy despite the efforts to attract young people, he organised a bhajan evening by Kanhaiya Mittal at Natkur ground in Sarojini Nagar on 22 April 2026. Grand plan for bhajan evenings during Navratri BJP MLAs and legislators from its alliance partners are preparing to organise bhajan evenings on a large scale during Navratri. Some MLAs are booking bhajan singer Kanhaiya Mittal, while others are competing to bring Bundelkhand-based bhajan singer Sunil Lodhi, who has gained attention through songs from the film ‘Hanuman Ansh’, to their constituencies. How do religious events influence voters? Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says reels and videos of storytellers’ discourses go viral on social media in large numbers today. Compared with political speeches, ordinary people tend to trust the messages delivered by religious storytellers much more and accept them more easily. This is why MLAs, ministers, MPs and election aspirants are spending lakhs and crores of rupees on events featuring high-profile storytellers to strengthen their presence among voters. This can be understood through these examples: Jagadguru Rambhadracharya has praised CM Yogi Adityanath and PM Narendra Modi on several occasions and supported Yogi’s style of functioning. Rajan Ji Maharaj described BJP’s victory in West Bengal after the Assembly elections as “Raghunath Ji’s blessing”. This was seen as a hint towards the future Hindutva agenda of the Shubhendu Adhikari government. Pandit Pradeep Mishra compared the RSS with Lord Shiva at an event in Bhopal. He said that just as Shiva consumes poison to protect the nation, the Sangh too is working to protect the nation by taking on its share of poison. SP leaders are also joining race for faith SP leader Pawan Pandey is set to organise a Bhagwat Katha from 2 to 9 October, which Akhilesh Yadav will also attend. Earlier, when Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati visited Ayodhya on 17 July 2026, SP leader Pawan Pandey gave him a grand welcome. He took the Shankaracharya to his ancestral home in Krishnapur on Rasoolabad Marg, where a sizeable crowd of 8,000 to 10,000 people gathered. Akhilesh Yadav will inaugurate Kedareshwar Temple in Etawah in October. More than 1 lakh people are expected to attend the event. Meanwhile, Congress and BSP have not organised major events through religious storytellers so far.

stories.title: Trader dies in Lucknow, Sanjay Nishad stages protest:Says entire police outpost should be dismissed; victim was attacked with sharp weapon in Gonda
stories.summary: A trader from Gonda died during treatment in Lucknow on Thursday afternoon. Upon receiving the news, Minister Sanjay Nishad reached KGMU and began a sit-in protest. He said that the entire police outpost should be dismissed for negligence; otherwise, he would hold a protest in Gonda as well. In fact, Gonda utensil trader Vinod Kumar Sahani was attacked with sharp weapons late Wednesday night. He was then brought to Lucknow for treatment. He died during treatment at around 3 p.m. today. Gonda police have so far arrested two suspects in the case. See 2 pictures... The traders were returning home after closing their shop Utensil trader Vinod Kumar Sahni (45) was a resident of Reksadia village in the Paraspur police station area. At around 8 p.m. on Wednesday, he was returning home after closing his shop. Meanwhile, he was stopped and attacked on the way. He sustained serious injuries in the attack. Injured Vinod was initially taken to the Paraspur Community Health Center. When his condition worsened, doctors referred him to Gonda Medical College. From there, he was sent to KGMU in Lucknow. He died during treatment at around 3 p.m. on Thursday. Demand for the dismissal of police personnel Upon learning of Vinod's death, Cabinet Minister Dr. Sanjay Nishad arrived at the post-mortem house at KGMU in Lucknow. He met with the family members and assured them of all possible assistance. Dr. Nishad condemned the attack and the death. Dr. Sanjay Nishad demanded the dismissal of the Paraspur station house officer, the Shahpur outpost in-charge, and the concerned staff. He said that if no action was taken, the SP's residence and office in Gonda would be surrounded on September 11. Police said-search for the accused is ongoing Paraspur police have registered a case under sections related to attempted murder against Shubham Singh alias Golu Singh, Akash Singh, Subhash Singh, and 5-7 unidentified people. Three police teams have been formed to arrest the accused. Paraspur police station in-charge Kamla Shankar Chaturvedi said: Teams have been deployed to apprehend the accused in the murder case of the trader. The police are investigating all aspects related to the incident.

stories.title: Lucknow cop beats BJP booth president, smashes his head:Enters house, hits brother with stick and kicks wife; team had arrived to probe dispute
stories.summary: In Lucknow's Banthra police station area, Sub-Inspector Sachin Yadav smashed open the head of a BJP booth president, hitting him on the head with the butt of a pistol. When the booth president's brother stepped in to save him from being beaten by the Sub-Inspector, the Sub-Inspector's team thrashed him with lathis. They kicked his wife in the stomach, causing her to collapse to the ground. The booth president had quarrelled with his neighbour during the day over setting up a shop. When he went to lodge a complaint, the police accepted it and assured him they would investigate. Subsequently, the person he had quarrelled with also arrived at the police station. Following this, the Sub-Inspector reached the location with his team to conduct questioning. The incident occurred at 11 pm on Wednesday in Khasrawara village, under the jurisdiction of the Banthra police station. Arvind Rawat, the victimised BJP booth president, lodged a complaint about the matter with the ACP on Thursday afternoon. Videos showing the Sub-Inspector's team barging into the BJP booth president's house and assaulting people emerged in the evening. On Wednesday, BJP booth president Arvind Rawat of Khasrawara village got into an altercation with fellow villagers Sahil, Sarjan, and Rahul over setting up a shop. A physical fight also broke out between both parties at around 8:30 pm. Following this, Arvind reached the Banthra police station, where he submitted a complaint against the other party alleging abuse, assault, and death threats. After this, the police asked him to go back home, saying they would investigate. A short while later, members of the other party also arrived at the police station and submitted a complaint levelling similar allegations against Arvind. When complaints regarding the same incident came from both parties, the police reached Arvind Rawat's house at 11 pm. Everyone was asleep. They woke them up and began assaulting them alongside the questioning.

stories.title: ‘Shalu feared killing ants, how could she order a murder?’:Brother says she cared for businessman father-in-law; husband never visited her in jail
stories.summary: On the fifth day after the murder of Kanpur medicine trader Vineet Minocha, the family members of the alleged mastermind, daughter-in-law Shalu, came forward. Shalu's elder brother Dheeraj Arora and sister Sonia Mehrotra declared her innocent at a press conference. They said, "How could a girl who cannot even kill an ant arrange the murder of her father-in-law?" Dheeraj, who arrived in Kanpur from Lucknow, said that he had been unable to contact Shalu's husband, Subrat, since the murder. Despite making several attempts, Subrat refused even to speak with him. Shalu has been in jail for three days, but her husband Subrat has still not gone to meet her. Shalu's brother said-My sister took complete care of her father-in-law Dheeraj said that he met Shalu twice in jail. Shalu is still in jail with the mindset that Subrat will come to meet her, but he has not come. It is possible that he is experiencing some kind of mental trauma. Shalu is distraught, crying constantly in her son's memory. She keeps repeatedly asking about her son Shrijay and her husband Subrat. Brother said that Shalu shared a very good relationship with her father-in-law. She took care of even his smallest needs. She was fulfilling the roles of a good daughter-in-law, wife, and mother. She was one of those women who kept the entire family united. Shalu's father-in-law was diabetic and disciplined about his diet. Shalu took complete care of his food and dietary needs. Shalu and Subrat got married in Nainital in 2020 Dheeraj Arora, a resident of Thakurganj in Lucknow, said that he has two sisters, Sonia and Shalu. The youngest member of the family, Shalu, had completed her B.Com and B.Ed. in Lucknow. She married Subrat Minocha in Nainital on November 23, 2020. Subrat's grandmother had been ill for a long time. She had come to Kanpur a few days earlier, accompanied by a staff nurse. Dheeraj said that no one used to be at home when the child was being brought back from school. That was when his father-in-law, Vineet Minocha, had CCTV cameras installed to keep an eye on the house. Shalu had also told them that the cameras had been installed because of the grandmother. Sister says claim that Shalu received insufficient household expenses is false Sister Sonia Mehrotra categorically rejected the claim that Shalu was given insufficient money for household expenses. Sonia said that whatever household allowance Shalu received, even if it ran out, she was given extra money whenever she asked for it. Shalu was not under any kind of restriction. Shalu herself had told her these things. Shalu said in jail- I did not have my father-in-law murdered Dheeraj said that my sister could not even frame her own résumé. She would tell me, "Brother, prepare my résumé." How could such an innocent girl have planned a murder? Asked why the contract killer Vishal mentioned Shalu's name after the encounter, Dheeraj said, "That is precisely what is surprising-why did Vishal mention Shalu's name? Only the police can explain that." Subrat was the one who gave Vishal's number to Shalu. He had told her to contact Vishal whenever she needed any minor household work done. Shalu used to call him only for domestic chores. Vishal was merely a staff member, and nothing else is known about him. When they went to meet Shalu in jail, she too was surprised as to why Vishal had mentioned her name. Shalu said, "I have done nothing, and I stand firm on this." Dheeraj said that they have complete faith in the police administration and that the murder case would be investigated properly and impartially. Subrat Had Organized the Couple Kitty Party Shalu's lawyer, Shivakant Dixit, said that the party held on the day of the incident was not a high-society party but a normal couple kitty party. It was attended by people associated with the pharmaceutical field. Traders from the medicine market on Birhana Road organize a kitty party every month. On the night of the murder, Subrat was supposed to organize a couples' kitty party. Subrat himself had arranged the party at Cosmojin Lounge in Tilak Nagar. Someone else had paid for the kitty party; the circumstances under which this was done are a matter of investigation. Police suspicion has still not shifted away from the businessman's son 49 Deleted Messages May Reveal Links to the Murder The planning of medicine trader Vineet Minocha's murder was woven through 49 deleted messages. These messages were deleted from May 1 until the day of the incident. What did the messages contain, and what kind were they? The accused Vishal and the daughter-in-law who paid for the contract killing did not tell the police. The police are working to recover data from the seized mobile phones of contract killer Vishal Gautam and daughter-in-law Shalu. Shalu and Vishal Gautam made 309 calls to each other from May 1 until the day of the incident.

stories.summary: The Supreme Court took note of the case of stone-pelting at the home of a 14-year-old activist of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), who lives in Ghaziabad, and the threat of rape against her. On Thursday, the Court said, “These allegations could not be taken lightly. No one can be allowed to intimidate or threaten the victim or her family.” The matter came to light when a lawyer told the bench headed by Chief Justice Suryakant that a counter-FIR had also been registered against the girl, while those accused of allegedly attacking and intimidating her had still not been arrested. The Supreme Court has sought a status report from the Uttar Pradesh and Delhi governments on the status of the FIR, the security being provided to the girl and her family, and the action taken against the accused. The hearing took place in connection with a case involving Swatantra Bhardwaj, who is accused of attacking the activist's father. Lawyer says-if anything happens to the girl, it cannot be rectified later During the hearing, the lawyer representing the CJP activist told the court that Parliament Street Police Station was investigating the girl's complaint. The people who attacked and threatened her are roaming freely, while a counter-FIR has been registered against the girl herself. If anything unfortunate happens to the child, subsequent action will not be able to make up for the damage. In response, the CJI said that the investigation and the High-Powered Committee's proceedings are separate matters, but ensuring the child's immediate safety is a distinct and essential responsibility. If the people facing the allegations are roaming freely and threatening the girl or her family not to pursue the criminal proceedings, it is a serious matter. CJP activist expresses gratitude to the Supreme Court A CJP activist expressed gratitude to the Supreme Court for taking cognizance of concerns regarding their safety and providing protection. They said, They are extremely grateful for the Court's concern and intervention. I have complete faith that the concerned officials will respect the Supreme Court's directions and ensure that they are followed with utmost sincerity. Rape threats on social media, father abused The father of a CJP activist claimed on X on Thursday that his minor daughter was being threatened. On Wednesday, the CJP activist had said that she was being sent messages threatening rape and death. She had said, "Some people are calling my statement false. Think for yourself: if these people can use such abusive and objectionable language against me through phone messages, what will happen to my safety if I come face to face with them? How much fear and anxiety would I feel?" See 4 pictures... She released 2 photos showing how she is being subjected to rape threats and her family is being threatened. Had demanded security for her family Earlier, the CJP activist had posted a video on social media platform X at 10:48 p.m. on Saturday night. She said that some people were surrounding her house and that stones and bricks had been thrown at it. She had demanded protection for her parents and family from the Delhi and Ghaziabad police. She had said, "If something happens to my parents, who will be held responsible?" However, residents of the society categorically rejected the activist's statements when speaking to Dainik Bhaskar. During the protest at Jantar Mantar, she had also alleged that her father was assaulted. In this case, accused content creator Swatantra Bhardwaj was arrested on Saturday.

stories.title: Akhilesh says will end outsourcing, give permanent jobs to all:Takes swipe at BJP in-charge, ‘Someone from Mumbai has come to fill treasury’
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday promised that a Samajwadi government in Uttar Pradesh would end the outsourcing system and provide permanent jobs to all workers. Taking a dig at BJP’s Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde without naming him, Yadav said, “In the age of AI, TI has arrived. Someone has come from Mumbai with a treasury to fill it.” Asked about Akash Anand’s expulsion from the Bahujan Samaj Party, Yadav said it was an internal matter of the party and others had no right to comment on it. However, when asked whether the SP would induct Akash Anand, Yadav smiled and said, “If you bring him, I will induct him.” Yadav was addressing a press conference at the SP office in Lucknow on Thursday. He targeted the BJP government over inflation, corruption, healthcare and communalism. He also invited Jagdish Yadav of Lalitpur, known for his long moustache, to sit beside him and gave him an envelope for maintaining his moustache. Here are the key points from Akhilesh Yadav’s press conference: 1. ‘Poor man could not afford to cremate his wife’ Yadav said a man in Jhansi lost his wife after she fell ill but could not afford her treatment. After her death, the family was unable to arrange money even to transport and cremate her body. He said the man remained with the body for hours without receiving help. A constable helped him reach home, but he still did not have money for the cremation and had to immerse his wife’s body in a river. Yadav questioned the government’s claims about economic growth and investment. “You talk about how much our GDP has grown and how much investment is coming in. Tell me, does the Jhansi incident not expose these GDP claims?” he said. “If a poor person cannot even cremate his wife or take her body home, what use are these GDP figures? They are for their friends who are doing big business,” he added. 2. ‘Leg had to be amputated after doctor forgot about plaster’ Yadav also questioned the state’s healthcare system. He said, “What kind of treatment is being provided under this government? I met a young girl yesterday. Her leg had fractured and a plaster was put on it. After applying the plaster, the doctor forgot about it. She later developed an infection and her leg had to be amputated.” He also referred to a case he had raised on August 15, saying a person who had been admitted to a hospital with stomach pain had eventually had to have his arm amputated. Yadav said building hospitals alone was not enough. They also needed good doctors, nursing staff, facilities and diagnostic services. “Their hospitals also need treatment. The government also needs treatment,” he said. He promised that if the SP returned to power, every poor person coming to a hospital would receive treatment without having to show a card. 3. ‘Thankfully, AQI was measured during the rainy season’ Reacting to Lucknow receiving an award, Yadav said, “I have heard that Lucknow has received an award. Thankfully, the AQI was measured during the rainy season.” He also promised that an SP government would connect Lakhimpur and Pilibhit through an all-weather expressway. 4. ‘In the age of AI, TI has arrived from Mumbai’ Taking another dig at the BJP, Yadav said, “In the age of AI, TI has arrived. Someone has come from Mumbai to fill a treasury.” He also said a mobile phone worth ₹3 lakh had been launched, while journalists could only be given “DI”. Yadav alleged that the BJP wanted to contest the election on the issue of communalism because it had no solutions to deal with inflation and corruption. ‘Outsourcing system will be ended’ Yadav reiterated his promise to end the outsourcing system if the SP formed the government in Uttar Pradesh. He said the party would provide permanent jobs instead, making employment security a key part of its proposed government agenda.

stories.title: ‘Do you have a girlfriend’ Businessman’s daughter-in-law asks servant:‘You’re smart, why haven’t you married?’; lured him into trap
stories.summary: You're smart, buddy. Do you have a girlfriend or not? Why haven't you gotten married yet? This message was sent on WhatsApp by Shalu (35), the daughter-in-law accused of murdering millionaire businessman Vineet Minocha (63), to the servant and murder accused Vishal. According to the police, the two had been in contact for about three months. Initially, Vishal used to send good morning and good night messages, but Shalu did not respond. About three months ago, she began messaging him herself. Police say that she gradually gained Vishal's trust and persuaded him to kill her father-in-law. Police found some of their chats on Vishal's mobile phone. However, he had deleted most of the chats after the murder on September 5. Police are working to recover them. On the day of the crime, Shalu and Vishal spoke on the phone 40 times. The surveillance cell's investigation revealed that the businessman's son, Subrat, was also in contact with Vishal. He had spoken to Vishal 300 times over the phone in three months. Notably, during this period, his father had fired Vishal from his job. On the day of the incident as well, Subrat and Vishal spoke 14 times over the phone. The police are now investigating Subrat's role and activities as well. Police may take accused Vishal on remand According to the police, after murdering Vineet Minocha, Vishal threw the duplicate key to the flat late at night at some distance from the apartment. The police are preparing to take Vishal into police custody remand to recover the key. During the remand, he will be questioned again in detail. Five-year-old son is withdrawn after his mother was sent to jail After his mother Shalu was sent to jail, her 5-year-old son has become withdrawn. According to the family, he is neither eating properly nor sleeping peacefully. Throughout the day, he repeatedly asks his family members about his mother and grandfather, Vineet Minocha. He says, When will Mommy come back? Where has Grandpa gone? According to the family, the child was Vineet's favorite. On his birthday last November 16, Vineet gifted him a bike. A video of the occasion has also emerged. It shows Vineet wishing his grandson a happy birthday, after which the child hugs him. Meanwhile, Shalu tells her son, ‘Grandpa has bought a surprise gift for you.’ The child runs into the room, where he finds a sport bike. stories.title: Teacher caught kissing student:Gorakhpur brother confronts him after he kept her back for an extra class; he claims, ‘She is like my sister’
stories.summary: A teacher at a computer centre in Gorakhpur was allegedly caught kissing a female student after stopping her at the centre on the pretext of an extra class. The student’s brother and some youths accompanying him confronted the teacher and slapped him two or three times inside the computer lab. The student’s brother alleged that the teacher had kept his sister back after the regular class and behaved inappropriately with her. The incident took place on Wednesday at a computer centre in Rajpur, around 50 km from the district headquarters. A video of the incident surfaced on Thursday. The teacher, however, denied the allegations and said he considered the student like his sister. He claimed that she had also tied a rakhi to him during Raksha Bandhan. Student allegedly stopped after class Around 40 boys and girls attend computer classes at the centre in Rajpur. According to the student’s brother, the teacher stopped the girl after the class ended. He alleged that the teacher was kissing her when he arrived at the centre with some friends. The brother questioned the teacher about why he was with the student in the room after the class had ended. The teacher replied, “She is like my sister. She also tied a rakhi to me on Raksha Bandhan. She had stayed back for additional studies.” The youths then allegedly slapped the teacher two or three times and abused him. They also warned him to shut down the coaching centre. Youths issue warning over alleged incident The youths warned the teacher of serious consequences if such an incident was repeated. They also repeatedly said that the entire incident had been recorded on their mobile phone. The video has led to anger among local residents, who have demanded an investigation into the matter and stronger safety measures for students at the computer centre. However, the police have not yet confirmed the identities of the teacher, the student or the youths seen in the video.

stories.title: Gorakhpur sees strong sunshine since morning:People struggling with humidity; temperature expected to reach 32°C
stories.summary: The weather in Gorakhpur appeared to be constantly changing since Thursday morning. Light clouds continued to move across the sky, but intermittent spells of bright sunshine caused people to endure humid heat. The slight coolness in the morning soon turned into sticky heat, leaving people outdoors as well as those at home and in offices uncomfortable. The fluctuating weather kept people uneasy throughout the day. According to the Meteorological Department, the maximum temperature today is expected to be around 32 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to remain around 26 degrees Celsius. Although the temperature is within the normal range, humidity levels reaching 70 to 90 percent are making the heat feel more intense. Due to the humidity, sweat is not drying quickly, leaving people feeling sticky and fatigued. Weather may change in evening The weather department has forecast light to moderate rain by evening. If it rains, people may get relief from the day's humidity and heat. There is also a possibility of rain accompanied by strong winds, thunder, and lightning, which could lead to a slight drop in temperature and make the weather somewhat pleasant. Weather pattern to continue to change According to meteorologist Dr. Kailash Pandey, Gorakhpur's weather will not remain completely stable over the next 5 to 7 days. During this period, the sky will remain mostly cloudy, with occasional light to moderate rain or drizzle accompanied by thunder and lightning. Daytime temperatures are expected to remain between 31 and 33 degrees Celsius, while nighttime temperatures are likely to range from 25 to 27 degrees Celsius. Experts say that monsoon-like conditions are currently prevailing in Gorakhpur, with a mix of sunshine, clouds, and rain. While the rain is providing relief to people, the persistent humidity and mugginess are affecting daily life. This situation may continue for the next few days. Important to take precautions Humid weather can also affect health. Doctors say that during this period, it is important to drink plenty of water, eat light and balanced meals, and avoid going out in strong sunlight. Special care has been advised for children and the elderly to protect them from weather-related illnesses.

The pilot cited ill health, following which the passengers became increasingly upset. Passengers were informed that the pilot would not operate the aircraft even before boarding for the flight began. Following this, the passengers created a commotion in the terminal building and accused the airline management of not providing accurate information. The passengers had completed security checks and were waiting for boarding in the security hold area. According to sources, the pilot's scheduled duty hours had also been completed, after which IndiGo began arranging an alternative crew. Passengers accuse airline management The passengers alleged that they were not given accurate information on time. With no clear information about the flight, the passengers began creating a commotion in the airport's terminal building. The passengers alleged that the flight was cancelled just when they were supposed to depart, and that no clarity had been provided about the situation yet. According to sources, the concerned pilot had completed the scheduled duty hours. It is also being reported that following protests from the passengers, IndiGo management has begun arranging an alternative crew so that the flight can depart from Varanasi for Mumbai.

stories.title: Air Force personnel's body found in two pieces in Agra:Torso and head found separately on railway tracks; was travelling to Prayagraj on Howrah Express
stories.summary: On Thursday morning in Agra, the body of a 35-year-old Air Force personnel was found in two pieces on the railway track. His head had been severed from his torso. The body was found lying on the track near Achhnera railway station, 26 kilometers from the district headquarters. Following information from villagers, the Government Railway Police (GRP) and local police reached the spot. Based on the ID card and ticket found in his pocket, he was identified as Nainaram, a resident of Khinvsar in Rajasthan's Nagaur district. He was traveling to Prayagraj on the Howrah Express with his wife, Shobha, and their son. However, it has not yet been clarified whether the Air Force personnel died after falling from the train, while crossing the tracks, or after jumping from the train. The police are questioning his wife and son to gather information. See 2 pictures

stories.title: Lucknow couple dies by suicide, found hanging from same noose:Man Hindu, woman Muslim; stayed in hotel for 18 days, marriage certificate found
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a 22-year-old man and his 19-year-old girlfriend died by suicide in a hotel. Their bodies were found hanging from the same noose. The man was Hindu, while the woman was Muslim. A police investigation revealed that both families were opposed to their relationship. The couple then fled Hardoi and came to Lucknow. They had been staying in a hotel room for 18 days. On Wednesday, neither of them came out of the room throughout the day. At around 8 pm, a hotel employee knocked on the door but received no response. He then looked through the window and saw the two hanging from the noose. He alerted the police. The room was opened using a spare key, and the bodies were taken down. The incident took place at the Red Building Guest House in Chinhat, Lucknow. Police found a marriage certificate issued by an Arya Samaj temple in the room. The certificate listed the woman as Nargis, alias Pooja, and the man as Amit Kumar. Police also recovered a suicide note. It read: 'We are going to die by suicide of our own free will. Our families should not be harassed after our deaths.' Both of them had signed the note at the end. ‌See 3 pictures- Hotel employee alerted police During the preliminary investigation, police found that Amit Kumar (22) was a resident of Harpalpur in Hardoi, while Nargis (19) was from Palia. Police said hotel employee Rakesh Yadav called them to report that the young man and woman had died by suicide by hanging themselves in the guest house. Soon after receiving the information, Sub-Inspector Dhananjay Singh arrived at the spot with a police team. Scarf tied to ceiling fan hook used as noose Police had the hotel room opened and found a scarf tied to the ceiling fan hook, which the couple had used as a noose. A cloth bag was also found in the room. Police recovered a marriage certificate, suicide note, keypad mobile phone and its charger, along with daily-use items. The suicide note contained the addresses of both individuals. Police then contacted their counterparts in Hardoi. Girl’s father filed kidnapping complaint on August 23 Police learnt that the girl’s father, Usman, had filed a kidnapping complaint at Harpalpur police station on August 23. In his complaint, he stated that his daughter Nargis was at home at around 3 am on August 21. Meanwhile, Amit Kumar came to the house and took Nargis with him. Usman said he searched extensively for his daughter but could not find her.

stories.title: Class 4 student missing from Gorakhpur found in Kushinagar:Mother searched lanes for 5 hours; son called and said, ‘Don’t cry, Mom’
stories.summary: A Class 4 student who went missing from Civil Lines in Gorakhpur was found in Tamkuhi Road, Kushinagar, bringing relief to the police after a five-hour search. The student went missing around 2 pm on Wednesday. His mother, accompanied by the police, searched the lanes of Civil Lines for five hours. At around 7.30 pm, she received a call from her son from an unknown number. She broke down and cried as he told her, ‘Don’t cry, Mom. I’ll come home and tell you everything.’ However, the case took an unexpected turn after the student was found, leaving the police confused for some time. When the police team took him with them and began questioning him, he initially told them that he had been kidnapped. After some time, he admitted the truth: he had boarded the Amrit Bharat train on his own. The boy, missing since the afternoon, finally met his mother around 10 pm. During the emotional reunion, she hugged him and broke down in tears. The family also thanked the police, with the child’s mother saying that the Gorakhpur police had stood by them throughout the ordeal. Child called from woman's mobile phone on train SP City Nimit Patil said that the student walked to the railway station and boarded the Amrit Bharat train to Chhapra at 4:30 p.m. A woman became suspicious after seeing him alone on the train. She spoke to him, obtained his mother's mobile number from his school ID card, and called her. After this, the Gorakhpur police informed the Sevarahi police. When the train reached Tamkuhi Road, a police team arrived at the station and took the student with them. Student seen walking alone in CCTV footage After the student went missing, the police examined footage from CCTV cameras installed at the school and nearby areas. The footage showed the student walking alone toward an auto-rickshaw, leaving his bag there, and then wandering around. After that, he walked alone toward the railway station. Told story about chocolate and losing consciousness The story the student initially told the police made the case appear to be one of kidnapping. He said that he was playing near the auto-rickshaw. During this time, a young man approached him and gave him a chocolate. After eating it, he lost consciousness. The man put him on a train. When he began crying on the way, a woman sitting nearby noticed him and called the number written on his school ID card, informing his mother. Gone missing before as well The student had previously left the school alone as well. About two months ago, he suddenly disappeared from school and reached home on foot. According to auto-rickshaw driver Ashish Kumar Jaiswal, the student had tried several times before to get off the auto-rickshaw and wander around. He had also informed the student's family about this. On Wednesday, after all the children had boarded the auto-rickshaw following school, the student said that he felt like playing and wanted to play in the water. The auto-rickshaw driver went to a shop to buy chips. When he returned, the student was missing. Full details of the incident After school, a Class 4 student traveling home by auto-rickshaw in Gorakhpur went missing. The student studies at HP Defense Academy. The auto-rickshaw driver had gone to buy chips for a girl, and when he returned, the student was not in the vehicle, although his schoolbag was still there. As soon as the student's disappearance was reported, the Cantt police, Crime Branch, and surveillance team began searching for him. The missing student has been identified as Padmanabh Giri (9), son of Manoj Giri from Raptinagar. The incident took place at around 1:40 p.m. on Wednesday in the Civil Lines area. Student's father is in Qatar The child's mother, Poonam Giri, said that her husband, Manoj Giri, lives in Qatar. They have two sons. The elder son studies in Class 4 at a school in Civil Lines, while the younger son is one year old. The family is from the Uruwa police station area. CCTV footage from five schools and establishments examined By 7 p.m., CCTV footage from five schools in Civil Lines and establishments in the surrounding area had been checked. According to the police, the student was seen on different CCTV cameras until around 2 p.m. An auto-rickshaw was parked about 150 meters from HP Defence Academy. After school ended, the auto driver had arrived there with the children at around 1:30 p.m. He placed the student's schoolbag in the auto-rickshaw. The student then went back toward the school and used the bathroom in front of it. Shortly afterward, he was also seen running back toward the auto-rickshaw. Disappeared in crowd At that time, all the nearby schools had let out. Thousands of children were present on the road. Hundreds of people had also arrived on motorcycles and in cars to pick them up. The student suddenly disappeared amid this crowd. The auto-rickshaw driver searched for the student in the surrounding area for quite some time. When he could not find him, he called the student's mother, Poonam Giri, and informed her about the incident. The family then informed the police at around 3 p.m. Had tried to run away before as well Auto-rickshaw driver Ashish Kumar Jaiswal said that the child had tried to get out of the auto-rickshaw and run away several times before. Regarding this, I had also instructed his family members to counsel the child. Ashish said, On Wednesday morning, I picked up the child from home and dropped him at school. At around 1:30 p.m., after school ended, I went inside the school and brought the children out after seating them in the auto-rickshaw. There were a total of six children in the auto-rickshaw-three from SP Defense School, two girls from Feeders School, and one girl from HP Children's School. There was a major traffic jam because the area around the school was waterlogged. Children were coming and going on foot and by bicycle as well. After seating all the children in the auto-rickshaw, Padmanabh told me that he felt like playing and wanted to go play in the water. Ashish said, I told Padmanabh to remain seated in the auto-rickshaw. After that, I went to buy chips for a girl from the cart under the tree in front of the auto-rickshaw. When I returned after about one or two minutes, Padmanabh was not in the auto-rickshaw. Ashish stated that he searched the surrounding area extensively and also called out for the child, but there was no sign of him. The police and the child's family were then informed about the incident.

stories.title: Varanasi to receive more rain today, IMD issues orange alert:Clouds hovering since morning; Ganga water level starts rising
stories.summary: Weather scientists have forecast rain in Varanasi today as well. Meanwhile, the IMD has issued an orange alert for rain in the districts on September 10. The water level of the Ganga in Varanasi has once again started rising. The water level was 69.28 meters at 8 a.m. on Thursday. According to the Central Water Commission, the water is rising at a rate of one centimeter every two hours. After a yellow alert was issued in Varanasi on Wednesday, the IMD issued an orange alert for rain on September 10. Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is expected. This rain may occur in several areas. According to meteorologist Manoj Srivastava, Varanasi will receive rain for another one or two days. Temperature is 29 degrees The temperature in Varanasi was recorded at 29 degrees at 8 a.m. Humidity was recorded at 84 percent today. Clouds continued to move across the sky. Meanwhile, people appeared worried by the humidity. The maximum daytime temperature is expected to reach 33 degrees. Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is also likely during the day. Ganga water level starts rising again After falling for four days, the water level of the Ganga has started rising again since Wednesday evening. According to the Central Water Commission, the Ganga was flowing at 69.28 meters in Varanasi at 8 a.m. The water level is rising by one centimeter every two hours. According to district administration figures, flood relief posts are active in view of the flooding. So far, 16 villages and 24 neighborhoods are still affected by the flood. A total of 877 families have been affected.

stories.title: Mayawati expels nephew Akash after rift:Says ‘he values father-in-law more’; move follows Ashok Siddharth’s political retirement
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati is angry with her nephew Akash Anand again. She has shown him the door from the party. In a post on X, she wrote, Akash was more attached to his father-in-law. Since September 3, he had not even reposted my posts. If he wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so. Therefore, from today, he has been freed from the party. Just three hours earlier, Akash’s father-in-law Ashok Siddharth had retired from politics for his son-in-law. He had expressed his support for Akash despite Mayawati’s decision. However, Mayawati did not accept his appeal and expelled her nephew Akash from the party. In fact, on Wednesday, Mayawati had set a condition for her nephew Akash’s return to the BSP. At 2.46 pm, she wrote on X, If former MP Ashok Siddharth wants what is best for his son-in-law Akash, he should retire from politics. Only then will Akash get a free hand. Akash is paying the price for his father-in-law’s selfish behaviour. Seventeen hours after Mayawati’s statement, Ashok Siddharth wrote an emotional post. Calling Mayawati his political guru, he announced that he was quitting politics for his son-in-law. It is now being believed that Mayawati may soon restore Akash to his old responsibilities in the party. Mayawati had removed Akash from his post seven days ago. She had said, ‘Akash needs to become more politically mature.’ Expelled from party on August 2, Mayawati had said he failed to improve despite repeated warnings What condition did Mayawati set for Akash’s return? Who is Ashok Siddharth?

stories.title: Ask this boy any date, he names day in seconds:Says no formula, remembers since childhood; meet UP’s genius boy
stories.summary: Ten-year-old Aditya Pandey from Prayagraj has a remarkable ability to tell the day of the week for dates without looking at a calendar. The Class 3 student can reportedly tell the day for several dates between 2019 and 2028 within seconds. When Dainik Bhaskar asked Aditya the days for random dates from different years, he answered each question in around two seconds without hesitation. What makes his ability unusual is that Aditya does not use a calendar, book or any specific formula to work out the answers. When asked how he does it, he simply said, “There is no formula. I have remembered them since childhood.” We spoke to Aditya and his family to learn more about his unusual memory. Read in detail… Mother says Aditya also has good writing skills and keeps a diary Aditya was born in 2016 in Jhunsi, Prayagraj. He studies in Class 3 at UD Convent School in Jhunsi. His father, Piyush Pandey, runs a general merchandise shop, while his mother, Ankita Pandey, is a homemaker. Aditya has a three-year-old younger sister, Divya. The family lives together with his grandparents and younger sister. His mother said Aditya is very good at using mobile phones and also has strong writing skills. He studies for around two hours at home every day. “Whatever he reads or sees once, he remembers it for a long time,” she said. Aditya also has a habit of maintaining a diary. He writes down things he plans to do as well as things he has already done. His ability extends to dates in future years Aditya's ability is not limited to dates from the past. When asked about dates in future years, he was also able to immediately tell which day of the week they would fall on. According to his parents, Aditya began showing an unusual ability to remember dates and the days associated with them from an early age. At around the age of 10, he can easily tell the day for several dates between 2019 and 2028. Random dates tested, Aditya answered immediately To test Aditya's ability, Dainik Bhaskar asked him several random dates from different years. Some were from previous years, while others were from the future. Aditya answered each one in around two seconds. He did not appear to need extra time to think about the dates or use any formula to calculate the answers. He also did not use a calendar or any other aid while answering. Remembers dates of festivals and family events Aditya's memory is not limited to dates and days of the week. He said he also remembers dates related to festivals and important events in his life. He said he can even recall when his family visited a temple and which day of the week it was. When asked when he had last visited a temple, Aditya replied that he had gone on May 26, 2026, which he said was a Tuesday. He also remembers the dates and days associated with festivals such as Raksha Bandhan, Holi and Diwali. His family said that when they discuss old events, Aditya often remembers and mentions the date connected to them. Parents call his ability ‘God-gifted’ Aditya's parents described him as a playful and energetic child. His teachers sometimes find his mischievous behaviour challenging, but he performs well academically. He stood first in his class in Classes 1 and 2. His teachers are also impressed by his memory. His parents said that when something is explained or taught to him, he remembers it easily. They consider his ability to remember dates, along with his good academic performance, a source of happiness for the family. We asked Aditya whether he memorises the days for so many dates by rote and whether he had learnt a special formula for it. His answer was simple: “There is no formula. I have remembered them since childhood.” The ease with which the 10-year-old answers such questions is what makes his unusual ability stand out. Teacher says Aditya is ‘extremely talented’ Aditya's school teacher, Swati Singh, said he is an extremely talented child. “If you explain something to him once, he never forgets it,” she said. She added that Aditya remembers the birthdays of teachers and other children at school. “Other children need to be taught and reminded about things, and sometimes we have to explain the same thing again. But if we explain something to Aditya once, he remembers it. He is a little mischievous, but he is very sharp,” she said.

stories.title: Why isn’t Rajpal Yadav returning businessman’s money?:Told HC ‘I’ll go to jail 5 times, but won’t pay’; SC says ‘Deposit money or go to jail’
stories.summary: Rajpal Yadav has received relief in a cheque bounce case. The Supreme Court has granted him interim protection from going to jail on the condition of depositing ₹5 crore. The Delhi High Court had sentenced Rajpal to three months in prison in a ₹5 crore transaction case involving Shahjahanpur-based businessman Madhav Gopal Agarwal. During the hearing, Rajpal had stated that he was ready to go to jail five times but would not pay the money because he did not take a loan; it was an investment. Why is Rajpal Yadav unwilling to return the money? Is the ₹5 crore case about a loan or an investment...? Find out the complete story in today's UP Explainer... Question-1: When and how did the dispute over money begin? Answer: According to the High Court judgment and an interview given by Madhav Gopal Agarwal to a YouTube channel, Rajpal approached Madhav Gopal in April 2010 to borrow money for the film 'Ata Pata Laapata'. He promised to repay the ₹5 crore loan along with ₹3 crore in interest. Along with the agreement, Rajpal provided a promissory note and post-dated cheques. When the film could not be completed within the time specified in the agreement, the deadline to repay the loan was extended thrice (21 September 2011, 4 April 2012, and 9 August 2012) through supplementary agreements. According to the final agreement, around ₹11.11 crore (principal + profit + interest) was to be paid. The old cheques were returned and eight new cheques for this amount were issued. As per the agreement, the film's negatives and prints were to be pledged with Madhav Gopal until the money was repaid after the film's completion, but this did not happen. The film's music was also launched without informing him. The release of the film was announced for 12 October 2012. Madhav Gopal states that because Rajpal breached the agreement, he filed a lawsuit in the Delhi High Court. The court stayed the release of the film. Following a settlement, the stay on the film's release was lifted, but the film flopped. Madhav Gopal presented the cheques in the bank as per the deadline fixed in the final agreement, but seven cheques bounced. He then filed seven criminal cheque bounce cases against Rajpal in Delhi's Karkardooma Court. On 21 April 2013, an agreement was reached between Rajpal and Madhav Gopal for a full and final settlement at ₹10.40 crore. Rajpal had already paid ₹40 lakh. The remaining ₹10 crore was to be paid in four instalments by 30 September 2014. Rajpal issued four cheques once again, but these bounced as well. On 23 April 2018, in the seven cheque bounce cases, the Karkardooma Court sentenced Rajpal to six months in prison and a fine of ₹1.60 crore in each case. Following this, Rajpal went to jail for the first time. The Delhi High Court reduced the sentence to three months. It also imposed a fine of ₹1.05 crore for each bounced cheque (totalling ₹7.35 crore for all seven cheques). Failure to pay the fine would extend the prison sentence by six months. Out of this, ₹1.75 lakh will be deposited into the government treasury, and the remainder will go to Madhav Gopal. Question-2: Does Rajpal Yadav truly not want to pay back the money? Answer: We are not making any claims regarding this. However, court rulings and statements made by Rajpal Yadav in public as well as in court suggest as much. On 30 November 2018, the Delhi High Court stated that Rajpal Yadav was prevaricating despite having the means to pay. He is working in several films. Every time, his defence remains that the payment for the film has already been received or that he is working without remuneration. Rajpal had challenged the trial court's decision in the cheque bounce case before the Sessions Court. The Sessions Court upheld the trial court's decision. Rajpal then approached the Delhi High Court against this order. During the hearing here, Rajpal stated that he would prefer going to jail five times rather than returning the money. Question-3: Why does Rajpal not want to return the money? Answer: In an interview given to a YouTube channel, Rajpal Yadav said, “In 2005, ₹10 crore worth of soil was lying in the basement of my home. I am trying to explain to the world why I am not returning the ₹5 crore. At the time the money was taken, 70 per cent of the film was already complete. Madhav Gopal invested ₹5 crore after watching that much of the film. The film was scheduled for release on 12 October 2012. Prior to that, Madhav Gopal approached the High Court. At that time, we had no dispute... the repayment date was 28 February 2013. When the High Court permitted the release of the film, he held a press conference accusing me of cheating him.” “As a result, a film that was meant to be released in 1,000–1,200 theatres could only be released in 200. Had the film run for even three days, ₹5 crore–10 crore would have been generated through selling video, satellite, and Doordarshan rights. I want to point out that Madhav Gopal's intentions were wrong. Around ₹22 crore belonging to several people was invested in the film. Because of him, all that money went down the drain. This is the very point I am putting before the court. I will fight them my whole life over this intention, but I will not compromise,” he said. However, in a conversation with the news agency ANI on 20 August, Rajpal Yadav said that he would repay the money owed to the people or ensure it reaches their doorstep.

stories.title: UP Police seeks ₹8 lakh from constables who became SIs:Must repay training, salary costs under department condition
stories.summary: Around 1,700 personnel in the Uttar Pradesh Police Department want to leave their jobs after being selected for posts such as sub-inspector, computer operator and lekhpal. However, around 75% of them have been selected for the post of sub-inspector. The police department is not issuing them relieving letters. The department has made it a condition that they must repay the money spent on their training and the salary they received. Under this condition, each constable will have to return an average of around ₹8 lakh to the department. This is believed to be the first case in the police department where such a large number of personnel are being asked to repay such a huge amount. Selection for two posts from the same batch creates a problem In 2023, the Uttar Pradesh Police announced recruitment for 60,244 posts. Around 57,000 candidates were selected in the examination. Their training started on June 21, 2025, and continued at different recruit training centres until April 20, 2026. During this period, the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board announced recruitment for 4,543 sub-inspector posts, along with posts for computer operators and lekhpals. Thousands of personnel undergoing constable training applied for these posts. The final result of the sub-inspector recruitment was announced in July 2026. Results for the computer operator and other recruitments were also declared. The names of around 1,700 personnel undergoing constable training appeared in the merit lists. The issue can be understood from the example of Baghpat, where 21 constables were selected for the post of sub-inspector. Similarly, personnel from Ghazipur, Jaunpur, Pratapgarh, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Lucknow, Moradabad and Varanasi also appeared on the selection lists. Bond says salary must be repaid if job is left before probation ends These personnel want to leave their constable jobs, but a police department rule has created a problem. The department says candidates had to sign a bond when they joined as constables. It states that if they leave the job before completing training and probation, they will have to repay the training costs and their salary and allowances. The training cost and salary and allowances received during probation together come to around ₹8 lakh. The selected personnel will have to deposit this amount at the office of the SP, SSP or police commissioner of the district where they are posted. If the amount is not deposited, their resignations will not be accepted and their cases will remain pending. The 1,700 personnel have to return around ₹136 crore to the department. They are demanding a waiver or relief on the recovery amount. Understand the calculation behind the ₹8 lakh salary and allowances 1. Training cost: around ₹2.58 lakh Former DGP Sulkhan Singh says an average of ₹863 is spent on one constable every day during training. This includes accommodation in barracks, food, uniforms, training equipment, weapons, and the salaries of staff and instructors. During 10 months, or around 300 days, the training cost for one constable comes to around ₹2.58 lakh. 2. Salary and allowances: around ₹5.42 lakh Under the rules, a constable remains on probation for two years after recruitment. During this period, they receive their basic salary along with dearness allowance (DA), uniform allowance and other benefits. If they leave the job before completing probation, they are required to repay the salary and allowances received during this period. The amount deducted towards provident fund and pension fund also has to be returned. The total amount, including training costs, salary and allowances received during probation and pension-related deductions, comes to around ₹8 lakh. Under Section 9 of the Police Act, 1861, a police employee cannot leave duty without permission or giving two months' written notice. Accepting a resignation is the authority of the appointing officer. The conditions of the bond signed at the time of joining also apply. Former DGP Sulkhan Singh has trained police personnel for a long time. He says the rule applies not only to the police but to every government department. According to him, the purpose of a probation period is that the government is training an employee rather than taking regular work from them. Therefore, the expenses incurred during this period are recovered. Constables say: Take the training cost, but do not ask for salary The selected candidates say they are not leaving for jobs in private companies or other states. They are moving to another and better job within the Uttar Pradesh government itself. The constables say they are ready to deposit the training cost of ₹2.58 lakh. However, they argue that asking them to return their entire two years' salary is unfair because they also performed their duties during this period. Most of the candidates come from ordinary families. Arranging ₹8 lakh suddenly is very difficult for them and their families. However, the police headquarters says the old order of the Establishment Department will remain applicable. According to the department, getting another government job is an advantage for the candidate. Therefore, the bond conditions cannot be relaxed on this basis. If these constables do not pay the recovery amount demanded by the department, they will not be able to join their new posts. Sulkhan Singh says that if they leave the department without paying the amount, recovery can also be carried out through the district magistrate. 1,700 posts will become vacant again The Uttar Pradesh Police spent crores of rupees on the recruitment of 60,244 personnel. More than 3,000 constables had already failed to join the department. Now, around 1,700 trained constables will suddenly leave, leaving those posts vacant again. This means the government will have to spend money once more on fresh recruitment and training for these posts.

stories.title: ‘Terrorists were cheered during Gen-Z protests’:Raja Bhaiya says, ‘We will now have to take up arms too’; attends Shiv Mahapuran Katha in Rae Bareli
stories.summary: Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, the Kunda MLA from Pratapgarh and president of the Jansatta Party, questioned the protest organised by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. He said the demonstration was being held over the paper leak issue, but the language used there could not be accepted. Raja Bhaiya alleged that slogans were raised against Bharat Mata and terrorists were glorified during the protest. He also alleged that the movement was receiving funding from the Middle East and Pakistan. Raja Bhaiya made the statement in Raebareli on Saturday. He had gone to attend the Shri Shiv Mahapuran Katha being held at Minister Manoj Pandey's residence in Unchahar. During this, he said that it would now be necessary to take up arms along with the scriptures. Now read Raja Bhaiya's full statement... Slogans of 'Down with India' cannot be accepted Raja Bhaiya said he had no objection to the issue of the protest, but questioned the language and behaviour of the protesters. Slogans of 'Down with India' were raised during the protest, and terrorists were praised. This cannot be accepted under any circumstances. Gen-Z does not align with our civilisation and culture Referring to the term 'Gen-Z', Raja Bhaiya said it aligned neither with our civilisation nor with our culture and values. He also accused the protesters of behaving indecently during the demonstration. Raja Bhaiya questioned the alleged funding of the protesters, alleging that they were receiving funds from disruptive forces in the Middle East, Pakistan and Europe. To explain this, he said, imagine that a protest is taking place in Delhi and pizza and hamburgers are being ordered for the protesters on Zomato from London. He said, "Here, eat this pizza. What are you supposed to do? Abuse India and insult Indianness." Received blessings from storyteller Pandit Pradeep Mishra Raja Bhaiya had arrived with his son, Shivraj Pratap Singh, to listen to the religious discourse. He also sought the blessings of the narrator, Pandit Pradeep Mishra. He then spoke from the stage about the protests in Delhi and the prevailing social circumstances. See 2 pictures... From an online campaign to a movement, how did CJP's journey begin? Abhijeet Dipke launched the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) as a satirical online campaign. After the campaign went viral on social media, a large number of students joined it, and it grew into a student movement. Protests intensified after NEET-UG 2026 Following allegations of a paper leak and irregularities in NEET-UG 2026, the CJP began a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on 6 June. The students demanded Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, an impartial investigation into the paper leak and reforms to the examination system. 36-day sit-in Students, parents and young people took part in the 36-day sit-in at Jantar Mantar. Sonam Wangchuk also joined the protest. After Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on 25 July, the CJP ended the sit-in and called it a victory for the students. First such case in 12 years According to the claim, Dharmendra Pradhan is the first minister in the 12-year tenure of the Modi government since 2014 to have been forced to resign amid protests. Before this, in 2018, Minister of State for External Affairs MJ Akbar resigned amid the 'Me Too' allegations.

stories.title: Madhumita’s sister threatens legal action if Amar Mani gets ticket:Vows to launch protest, tells Congress not to take the 'killer' into its ranks
stories.summary: There is speculation that Amar Mani Tripathi, who killed poet Madhumita Shukla, may join the Congress. Madhumita's sister, Nidhi Shukla, has opposed this. In Lakhimpur, Nidhi said, "A person with a criminal background should not be admitted to the Congress." "If any political party fields Amar Mani Tripathi in an election, I will file a complaint with the Women's Commission and go to court. I will launch a protest." Nidhi Shukla was speaking to the media at around 2 p.m. on Sunday. She said, "I am hurt by Amar Mani's welcome in Pharenda" Nidhi said that Abhishek Dutt, the Congress national secretary, had visited the Pharenda Assembly constituency in Maharajganj on 8 September. During the visit, there was discussion about welcoming Amarmani Tripathi and inducting him into the Congress. I am deeply hurt by this. In 2004, when I began pursuing the Madhumita murder case, I met Sonia Gandhi, who was the Congress president at the time. After hearing me out, Sonia Gandhi assured me of her support in the fight for justice. 'Priyanka Gandhi had also distanced herself from Amarmani' Nidhi said that at the time, senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi had also maintained her distance from Amarmani Tripathi. “I am a member of the Congress party myself. Our party leadership speaks of respecting women and upholding high political standards. In such a situation, I will not accept any attempt to associate Amarmani Tripathi with the Congress,” she said. 'I have been fighting for justice for my sister for 25 years' Nidhi Shukla said, "Nearly 25 years of my life have passed fighting to secure justice for Madhumita. I will now oppose any move by any political party to provide political protection to Amarmani. If any party inducts him or attempts to field him in an election, I will stage a sit-in, go on hunger strike and launch a protest before the party's national leadership." Nidhi also sent a letter to the Election Commission Nidhi Shukla also sent a letter to the State Election Commissioner regarding the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. In it, she referred to Amarmani Tripathi's eligibility to contest the election and the criminal case pending against him. She demanded that the matter be placed on record before the official announcement of the election. Nidhi said, "Madhumita Shukla was murdered on 9 May 2003 in the area under Mahanagar police station in Lucknow. The case was investigated by the CBI. On 24 October 2007, the Special CBI Court in Dehradun sentenced Amarmani Tripathi to life imprisonment. The Supreme Court later upheld the sentence. However, he was released from prison in 2023 on the basis of remission." In the letter, citing Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, Nidhi has claimed that Amarmani's disqualification from contesting elections remains in effect until 2029. A kidnapping case registered in Basti has also been mentioned. Nidhi has alleged that court proceedings against Amarmani in the Basti case are pending. The letter also mentions the orders declaring him a criminal and attaching his property. Questions also raised over political activities Nidhi Shukla alleged that despite these cases, Amarmani has been seen involved in political activities in Maharajganj's Nautanwa and Pharenda areas. After the election notification is issued, Amarmani's eligibility to contest the election should be examined. Political parties should also avoid giving a ticket to such a person.
