stories.title: Airline fined ₹64,000 in Gorakhpur:Passenger stopped after boarding, gets justice 6 years later
stories.summary: Gorakhpur’s District Consumer Commission has delivered a major verdict in a nearly six-year-old case involving a passenger who was stopped from boarding a flight before its scheduled departure time. After a lengthy legal process and multiple hearings, the victim has finally received justice, with the commission’s decision sending the message that although justice may be delayed, it is ultimately delivered. The case concerns Jaya Upadhyay, a resident of New Shivpuri Colony in Rustampur, Gorakhpur. Her father had booked a SpiceJet Airlines ticket on February 27, 2018, for her journey from Delhi to Gorakhpur. The scheduled departure time of the flight was 9:45 a.m. On the day of the journey, Jaya Upadhyay reached Delhi Airport ahead of time, at 9:05 a.m. She completed all the formalities and also obtained her boarding pass, making it clear that she had fully complied with the prescribed travel rules. Boarding was stopped 20 minutes early Despite completing all the required procedures, when Jaya Upadhyay reached the gate to board the aircraft, SpiceJet Airlines staff stopped her just 20 minutes before the flight. The incident was shocking in itself, as boarding usually continues until the scheduled departure time. She was prevented from boarding the aircraft without any valid reason, disrupting her entire travel plan. Even the money was not refunded The matter did not end there. Even after preventing Jaya Upadhyay from boarding the flight, SpiceJet Airlines did not refund the ticket fare of ₹4,560. As a result, she suffered not only financial loss but also considerable mental distress. On the one hand, her journey was interrupted, and on the other, she did not receive her money back, making the matter even more serious. Filed a complaint with the Consumer Commission for justice After this entire sequence of events, Jaya Upadhyay did not give up and filed a complaint with the District Consumer Commission to seek justice. Her lawyers argued before the commission that the passenger had arrived ahead of time and complied with all the rules, yet she was prevented from boarding the flight and was not even refunded the money, which clearly amounted to a deficiency in service. Airline's Fault Established After Hearing During the hearing, the commission heard arguments from both sides and examined all the facts. Commission President Surendra Kumar Singh and members Krishnanand Mishra and Beena Singh found that SpiceJet Airlines' conduct was entirely irresponsible. They stated that preventing a passenger from boarding before the scheduled time and failing to refund the ticket amount were both violations of consumer rights and would be considered a deficiency in service. Order to Refund the Amount Along with Compensation and Interest In its decision, the Commission issued strict directions to SpiceJet Airlines, ordering it to refund the ticket amount of ₹4,560 along with 10% annual interest. In addition, considering the mental and financial distress suffered by the passenger, the airline was ordered to pay ₹60,000 as compensation. The airline will also have to bear the litigation expenses. Thus, overall, the airline will have to pay approximately ₹64,000. A Strong Message for Consumers This decision sends a strong message to all consumers who remain silent even after falling victim to a company's negligence. The case shows that if you raise your voice for your rights, the law stands with you. Although justice may take time, the truth ultimately prevails, and those at fault have to pay the price. Warning to Companies This decision of the District Consumer Commission has also issued a clear warning to service-providing companies to comply with their rules and responsibilities. If negligence or arbitrary conduct occurs at any level, they will face legal action and financial penalties. This decision will be regarded as a strong precedent for similar cases in the future.

stories.title: Mayawati attacks Akhilesh over blue 'gamacha':Says ‘casteist mindset will not change’; calls Congress, which offered Akash a deal, a sinking ship
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati has hit out at Akhilesh Yadav. Without naming him, she said on Friday that adopting the BSP’s blue colour, wearing a blue scarf around the neck, dressing in blue clothes or putting blue fabric on a stage would not change a party’s casteist mindset. Mayawati wrote on social media platform X: "If you genuinely care about the poor, Dalits, tribals, backward classes and other neglected sections, then all opposition parties, including the SP and Congress, must first cleanse their hearts and minds. Merely adopting the colour blue does not make anyone an Ambedkarite." In fact, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had arrived wearing a blue scarf around his neck during a press conference on August 31. Three days earlier, Akhilesh had launched a new blue uniform for the student wing, the Samajwadi Party Chhatra Sabha. He had said, "Blue is the colour of the Bahujan Samaj as well as its ideology." On the offer to her nephew Akash Anand to join the Congress, Mayawati said, "Congress is like a sinking ship. Why would anyone put their political future in darkness by joining it?" After Akash was expelled from the BSP, Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam had said that the doors of the Congress were open to Akash and that he would receive due respect there. Key points from Mayawati’s post 1. Mayawati said, ‘They say one thing and do exactly the opposite’ Mayawati said, "Opposition parties have continuously changed their colours on issues concerning backward classes and Dalits. These parties say one thing and do exactly the opposite." Questioning the Samajwadi Party’s PDA slogan, referring to backward classes, Dalits and minorities, she said the BSP was the only party fighting the real battle for the Bahujan Samaj. She described the BSP as their only well-wisher and the only Ambedkarite party. 2. ‘Those expelled from BSP are opportunists and loyal to no one’ Mayawati said, "People expelled from the BSP have switched parties several times. This gives an indication of their selfish and opportunistic politics. Such people cannot do good for any party." She said some expelled leaders, while acting at the behest of other parties, even go on to form small parties and organisations. According to her, this cannot serve the collective interests of the Bahujan Samaj. 3. ‘They cannot contest elections without alliances; power is the most important thing’ Mayawati said, "Such parties cannot even contest elections without alliances. At the same time, when a major party forms the government, they cannot stay away from joining it." The BSP chief also targeted parties that advise leaders expelled from the BSP to join them or form separate parties. She said such parties should first look within themselves. 4. ‘Babasaheb had advised the Bahujan Samaj to maintain distance from Congress’ Referring to Dr BR Ambedkar, Mayawati said that during his lifetime, he had warned members of the Bahujan Samaj to maintain distance from the Congress. She said it was important for people associated with the BSP and its movement to understand these points in the current political circumstances. 5. ‘Ashok Siddharth tried several tactics and was forced to retire from politics’ On the political retirement of Akash Anand’s father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, Mayawati said, "On the day I advised Ashok to retire from politics, he tried several tactics. When none of them worked, he was forced to announce his retirement at 6.30 am the next morning because of the compulsion and the fear of greater losses." Ashok Siddharth retired from politics, Akash expelled from BSP Mayawati expelled her nephew Akash Anand from the party again on Thursday morning. At 9 am, she wrote on X, "Akash is more attached to his father-in-law. He has become double-minded. If he wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so. Therefore, from today, he has been freed from the party." A day earlier, on Wednesday, Mayawati had set Ashok Siddharth’s retirement from politics as a condition for restoring Akash’s party position. Around 17 hours after Mayawati set the condition, Ashok Siddharth announced his retirement from politics at 7 am on Thursday. Following the announcement by Akash’s father-in-law, it was believed that Mayawati might forgive Akash. However, surprising everyone, she not only refused to restore his position but also expelled him from the party. This is the second time in three years that Mayawati has expelled Akash from the BSP. Seven days earlier, she had removed him from the post of national coordinator, the party’s number two position. From Akhilesh to Sanjay Nishad, who said what about Akash? At a press conference in Lucknow on September 10, when asked whether Akash Anand could join the SP, Akhilesh Yadav said, "You are a journalist, you tell him to come, we will take him." Nishad Party president Sanjay Nishad said, "Akash Anand should join us. He will be given full respect and a major responsibility. He could even be made national president. The dream of Ambedkar and Kanshi Ram remains incomplete, and we can all work together to fulfil it." Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai had said, "Akash Anand was speaking about his people, which Mayawati did not like." Congress leaders also believe that decisions taken by the party have played a major role in damaging Akash Anand’s political career. Read why Akash was expelled 1. According to sources, a close party leader allegedly provoked Mayawati against Ashok Siddharth, telling her that he was misleading Akash and interfering in party decisions. Mayawati subsequently made Ashok’s retirement from politics a condition for Akash’s return. 2. In a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Ashok had agreed to retire on Wednesday itself. He announced his retirement on Thursday morning. The decision was then in Akash’s hands. A senior party leader told Akash to repost Mayawati’s post and publicly thank her. However, Akash was not willing to do so. 3. Akash said, "Whatever I do, she simply does not trust me. On September 9, Mayawati wrote about Ashok Siddharth and me, including the line ‘your son-in-law...’. Akash was extremely upset over this." 4. This time, Akash was not willing to accept any position in the party. Even his father, Anand Kumar, tried to persuade him, but he refused. Akash said he was willing to work for the party independently and without holding any position. 5. When Mayawati came to know about Akash’s position, she became even more upset. She subsequently decided to expel him from the party.

stories.title: Constable dies by suicide, wife screams after seeing body:Father faints and ASP helps him; body found hanging in Ambedkar Nagar room
stories.summary: A 30-year-old constable died by suicide in Ambedkar Nagar. His body was found hanging from the window grille in his room at 5:30 a.m. on Friday. The door was locked from the inside. The incident came to light when the constable's colleague arrived to collect the mess keys. When he knocked on the door, there was no response. He informed the officers. The police broke open the door and took out the body. No suicide note was found in the room. Sandeep, a resident of Mau, was the mess clerk at the police lines. The incident took place in the Akbarpur Kotwali area, 3 km from the Collectorate. The constable had married Ranjana three years ago. They have a one-and-a-half-year-old daughter. He was the only son in his family. As soon as they were informed of the incident, his father and wife arrived. His wife, Ranjana, screamed upon seeing the body and fainted while crying. His father, Rampyare, collapsed unconscious. The ASP helped him up. Placing a hand on his shoulder, he said, 'Stay strong, please don't worry. We are with you.' ASP Tejveer Singh said: Sandeep had gone home on a two-day leave. He returned to duty on Thursday. The initial investigation suggests family discord. No information about departmental or other work-related stress has emerged. The police are also examining his mobile phone to determine the circumstances before the incident. See 4 pictures- Sandeep had joined the police force 8 years ago Sandeep Kumar was originally a resident of Nav Semar village in Mau. He joined the police force in 2018. He married Ranjana in 2023. He lived alone in a rented accommodation located behind the engineering college in Akbarpur. A fellow constable said, "On Friday, I called him several times to collect the mess keys, but he did not answer. After that, I went to his room. The door was locked from the inside. There was no response even after knocking and calling out. Suspecting something was wrong, I informed the officers. When the police opened the door, they found Sandeep's body."

stories.title: Umesh Pal’s wife says, ‘I am Brahmin, married in temple’:Says she does not know Pooja Pal’s caste; read what Atiq family lawyer asked in court
stories.summary: In the much-discussed Umesh Pal murder case at the Prayagraj District Court, his wife, Jaya Pal, testified. Tarachandra Gupta, the lawyer for Eklakh Ahmed, the accused brother-in-law of mafia don Atiq Ahmed, asked, "How did you and Umesh get married? Was it by your choice, or did someone else arrange it? Is there any record of it?" Jaya Pal replied, "I belong to the Brahmin community. I married Umesh Pal on January 19, 2005. I was an adult at the time, so everything happened with my consent. The wedding rituals were performed at a temple near my in-laws' home. The priest conducted the ceremonies. Therefore, no written record was made. I do not even know the name of the temple." The lawyer asked, "Did Umesh Pal identify himself as an eyewitness in the murder case of former MLA Raju Pal? What caste does Raju Pal's wife, Pooja Pal, belong to? Did she ever have a physical altercation with Umesh Pal?" Jaya replied that she did not know. However, she said that no physical altercation had taken place between Umesh and Pooja Pal in the Dhoomanganj police station area. Actually, the hearing in the Umesh Pal murder case has been underway in court since September 8. During the first two days, witness Jaya Pal's statement was recorded in the Special Judge SC/ST Act Court. Arguments began thereafter. On February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal and his two government gunners were shot and killed and attacked with bombs in broad daylight in Prayagraj. Umesh was the prime witness in the 2005 murder case of BSP MLA Raju Pal. Mafia don and former MP Atiq Ahmed, his brother Ashraf, his son Asad, and their aides were accused in the case. Read what Jaya said in response to the lawyer's questions- Jaya Pal said-she does not know about the relationship between Pooja and Umesh Jaya Pal said-When Umesh testified, the Samajwadi Party government was in power in UP Jaya Pal told the court-I do not know whether the court had issued any order for a CBI investigation into the Raju Pal murder case. When Umesh Pal testified in the Raju Pal murder case, the Samajwadi Party government was in power in Uttar Pradesh. I know that Atiq Ahmed was elected MLA from the City West constituency five times. Atiq Ahmed was also elected as an MP from Allahabad district. "I don't know whether Umesh Pal contested the election from the OBC community or not." Jaya Pal said that it is true that after Umesh Pal testified in the Raju Pal murder case, the district panchayat election was held. I do not know whether Umesh Pal contested that election as a member of the OBC community or not. I also do not know whether Atiq Ahmed's men and vehicles were used in campaigning during that election. Jaya told the media: I am receiving threats to blow me up with RDX Today, I am remembering the scene of my husband's murder Jaya Pal said, "I am reminded of that scene today... My husband had just left after returning from court when he was brutally beaten to death on the way. I too will be murdered, just as my husband was. Jaya Pal showed a poster of Umar, the eldest son of Atiq Ahmed. Umar is pointing a finger and signaling someone to remain silent. Who is this gesture meant for?" It is being circulated on social media every day that Umar will come, Ali will come, and Ahzam is out. My family is being tortured. I want justice. Umesh Pal's wife had reached the court with several lawyers and supporters. Earlier, on September 1 as well, Jaya Pal had recorded her statement in court. Know about the Raju Pal and Umesh Pal murder case- In 2005, BSP MLA Raju Pal was murdered in Prayagraj. Umesh Pal was among the key witnesses in the case. Eventually, this testimony became the reason for the Umesh Pal murder. On February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal was attacked in the Dhoomanganj area of Prayagraj. He was returning home. Umesh Pal and two government gunmen deployed for his security were killed in the attack. After the incident, a case was registered against Atiq Ahmed, Ashraf, Shaista Parveen, Asad, and several others on the complaint filed by Umesh Pal's wife, Jaya Pal.

stories.title: MP spurious liquor case:Main accused shot in leg and arrested after firing 3 rounds at police; wanted in case involving 31 deaths
stories.summary: The main accused in the spurious liquor case in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar was arrested on Friday after police shot him in the leg during an exchange of fire in a forest. The accused, Ravi Lakhera, allegedly opened fire at the police team three times near Khaiwaha village in the Baraytha forest area, close to the Uttar Pradesh border. One bullet hit a police vehicle. Police returned fire after Lakhera allegedly refused to stop despite warnings. One bullet hit his left leg, following which he was arrested. Sagar SP Anurag Sujania confirmed the arrest. Lakhera had a ₹20,000 reward on his arrest. Police said two men accompanying him on a motorcycle fled the spot and are being searched for. So far, 31 people have reportedly died after consuming the illicit liquor. Three more patients admitted to Bundelkhand Medical College died on Thursday. However, the administration has officially confirmed 16 deaths. Bulldozers used against illegal structures at three accused’s properties On Thursday, the administration demolished illegal portions of five houses belonging to three accused in the case. The properties included those of accused Manish Lodhi, Karni Sena divisional president Chandrabhan Singh Rajput and Ashish Sahu. Police have so far named 33 people as accused in the case. Of them, 18, including Lakhera, have been arrested. One accused has died and another is undergoing treatment in hospital. Thirteen accused are still absconding. Police say Lakhera was key figure in illicit liquor network According to the police investigation, several people were involved in the operation, from manufacturing the illicit liquor to supplying it to villages. Ravi Lakhera: Alleged mastermind behind liquor production Lakhera is originally from Mahoba in Chhatarpur district but has been living for a long time in the Gangapuram Colony area of Lalitpur, Uttar Pradesh. Police describe him as an inter-state liquor smuggler. Around 25 criminal cases have reportedly been registered against him in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and other places, most of them under the Excise Act. According to police, Lakhera had detailed knowledge of liquor production and the materials used in it. He allegedly arranged the required materials and supplied them to his network, which was involved in preparing illicit liquor. Investigators have described him as a key link and alleged mastermind of the illicit liquor network. He was also in contact with licensed liquor contractor Manish Lodhi, alias Yashwant Singh. Manish Lodhi: Licensed contractor allegedly linked to illicit liquor trade Manish Lodhi, alias Yashwant Singh, was the licensed contractor for a liquor shop in Barethi. Police said he learnt the method of making illicit liquor from Lakhera and allegedly began the illegal business under the cover of his licensed liquor trade. Eleven criminal cases have been registered against Lodhi, including six under the Excise Act. He also owned a bar on Sagar Road in Banda, which was sealed after the case came to light. Chandrabhan Singh Rajput: Alleged role in manufacturing and supply Chandrabhan Singh Rajput, alias Chandu, a resident of Tatarwara, has been accused of playing a key role in the manufacturing and supply network. He is a relative of liquor smuggler Shivanjay Rajput and allegedly came into contact with Manish Lodhi through him. Police said illicit liquor was prepared in Chandu’s maize field. Five criminal cases have been registered against him. Shivanjay Rajput: Alleged role from production to supply Shivanjay Rajput, a resident of Chhapri, was allegedly active in the network. He is related to Chandu and was in contact with Manish Lodhi. Police said Shivanjay, Lodhi and Chandu were involved in supplying the illicit liquor to nearby villages after it was prepared. Spurious allegedly made in a maize field According to police, the illicit liquor was prepared in Chandu’s maize field in Tatarwara around two days before Janmashtami. Police allege that Lakhera and Manish Lodhi provided the materials required to make the liquor. Chandu, Shivanjay and Lodhi then allegedly prepared around 50 boxes of illicit liquor. The liquor was reportedly supplied to nearby villages under the brand name ‘Sagar Gold’ through salesmen. Accused allegedly tried to destroy evidence after deaths began After people started falling ill and deaths were reported following consumption of the liquor, the accused allegedly tried to destroy evidence. Police said around 20-25 boxes of liquor were taken to the field and burnt. Materials used to prepare the liquor were allegedly disposed of in a drain. Police to question Lakhera about source of materials According to investigators, Lakhera played a key role in procuring the materials used to prepare the illicit liquor. Police allege that he and Manish Lodhi arranged items including materials for liquor production, packaging material, sacks, wrappers, labels, stickers, methanol and ethanol, among other supplies. Investigators are now trying to establish where these materials were purchased and how they were transported to Tatarwara. Police said questioning Lakhera and Lodhi could reveal further details about the network and the people involved in procuring and supplying the materials.

stories.title: Clouds over Varanasi, rain likely:Temperature stays at 30°C since morning, Ganga water level stabilises
stories.summary: Once again, the water level of the Ganga has stabilized in Varanasi. Meanwhile, the skies over Varanasi have been cloudy since Friday morning. The temperature was recorded at 30 degrees Celsius at 8 a.m. Winds are blowing at a speed of 14 kilometers per hour. Meanwhile, the difficulties of people living in the areas along the banks of the Ganga and Varuna rivers are increasing. Dark clouds cover the sky Dark clouds have covered the sky in Varanasi since Friday morning. The weather has become pleasant after rain late last night. According to the Meteorological Department, Varanasi will receive intermittent rain today. Meanwhile, the maximum temperature is expected to reach 33 degrees Celsius. Winds are currently blowing at a speed of 14 kilometers per hour, while humidity has been recorded at 79 percent. Rise in Ganga's water level stopped at 8 p.m According to the Central Water Commission, the rise in the Ganga's water level stopped again at 8 p.m. on Thursday. The Ganga is currently flowing at 69.33 meters. The water level remained stable until 8 a.m. Meanwhile, water is still present in several places in the riverside areas, forcing people to leave their homes and live in camps. 877 families affected by the flood According to the district administration, 877 families in Varanasi are currently affected by the floods. These include families affected by both the Varuna and Ganga rivers. They have been accommodated in relief camps. Meanwhile, some people are staying in private rooms they have rented. Due to the rising water levels of the Ganga and Varuna, 24 villages in Varanasi and 16 localities in the urban area are submerged. People are evacuating these areas.

stories.title: DDU to get AI-powered student assistant:Will work 24 hours a day, resolving students’ problems and providing instant answers
stories.summary: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University plans to develop a 24-hour AI-powered student assistant to address students’ academic and administrative needs. Once developed, the system will provide instant answers to common queries related to admissions, fees, examinations, results, certificates and other university services. The facility is proposed under the “Dean, AI Initiatives and Digital Transformation Office” plan put forward by Vice-Chancellor Prof. K.P. Singh. On Thursday (10 Sept), the Vice-Chancellor conducted a detailed review of preparations for “AI Manthan-2.0”. During the meeting, he assessed the action plan being prepared to use artificial intelligence (AI) to provide students with faster, better and more convenient services. All essential information to be brought under one system The proposal also includes a centralised knowledge base containing accurate and updated information from various departments, examination sections, hostels and the finance branch. This will allow students to access essential information from a single platform while improving the speed and transparency of administrative operations. AI facilities to be made student-friendly Vice-Chancellor Prof. K.P. Singh said technology should be used to make processes more convenient for students and improve the university’s overall functioning. He emphasised that all AI-based facilities should be simple, reliable and completely student-friendly. ‘AI Manthan-2.0’ to be held in Kanpur “AI Manthan-2.0” will be held on September 12 and 13, 2026, at Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University (CSJMU), Kanpur, with universities across Uttar Pradesh participating. The Vice-Chancellor directed officials to complete preparations for the event within the stipulated time and ensure that the university’s use of AI remains focused on student welfare and faster operations. He also instructed officials to submit the information sought by Raj Bhavan in an organised manner. IQAC Coordinator Prof. Ajay Singh, DSW Prof. Anubhuti Dubey, the Registrar and several other officials attended the review meeting.

stories.title: Two youths stripped naked and beaten over theft suspicion:Accused of entering house in Lucknow; police act after video surfaces
stories.summary: A case has come to light in Ambergunj under Lucknow’s Saadatganj area, where two youths were allegedly stripped and beaten with sticks after being suspected of theft. The incident reportedly took place after the two youths allegedly entered a house under construction at around 3 am on Tuesday night. According to the allegations, labourers and a mason sleeping at the site heard a noise, caught the two youths and took them to the Balaganj police outpost. It is alleged that when no action was taken there, they were brought back to the construction site and beaten with sticks. Police launched an investigation after a video of the incident surfaced on social media. Saadatganj Police have detained one person and are questioning him. The video has not been independently verified. Youths accused of stealing motor, mobile phone and ₹10,000 According to Yogendra, officer in charge of the Ambergunj outpost, Kuldeep Gupta owns a traders’ shop in the Thakurganj area and is constructing a building in Ambergunj. Only the mason and labourers stay overnight at the construction site. It was alleged that around 3 am on Tuesday (8 Sept), two youths entered the building under construction and stole a motor, a worker’s mobile phone and around ₹10,000 belonging to a mason. The workers and mason woke up after hearing a noise and caught the two youths at the spot. Youths allegedly brought back after police outpost The two youths were reportedly taken to the Balaganj police outpost by Kuldeep Gupta and an acquaintance. It is alleged that the police personnel present there took no action and sent them back. They were then allegedly taken back to the construction site to recover the stolen money and belongings. Video shows youths allegedly being stripped and beaten It is alleged that the two youths were stripped and severely beaten with sticks at the construction site. Someone recorded the incident, and the video later surfaced on social media. In the video, the two youths can allegedly be seen with their hands folded while apologising. One detained, police search for victims Saadatganj Police Station in-charge Santosh Arya said the case is being investigated on the basis of the video. Police are searching for the youths who were allegedly beaten. One person has been detained and is being questioned. Arya said further action would be taken after a written complaint is received.

stories.title: Kanpur millionaire businessman murder:5 reasons suspicion on son deepens; spoke to contract killer 309 times, went with him thrice
stories.summary: In the murder case of Kanpur's millionaire medicine trader Vineet Minocha, following the daughter-in-law Shalu, police suspicion has now deepened towards his son Subrat as well. Investigation has revealed that Subrat spoke to hitman Vishal Gautam on the phone around 309 times in three months. In the 20 days leading up to the murder, Subrat went out thrice with the contract killer Vishal and his wife Shalu. The biggest question is that despite having more than 20 employees at home and in the business, why was Subrat so close to Vishal? Why did Subrat fail to recognise Vishal, who had worked at his firm for 12 years? The first time he was shown the CCTV footage. These links have raised several questions regarding Subrat, the answers to which are now being sought in the investigation. Read the 5 points based on which the police suspect the son's role… 1. Three house helpers, 17 employees, yet why was Vishal so special? In the Vineet Minocha murder case, the police have already sent the murder accused Vishal, Rajkishore, and daughter-in-law Shalu to jail. The details that have emerged from the surveillance cell's investigation are putting the son in the dock as well. Subrat spoke to hitman Vishal Gautam 309 times on the phone over three months. This was despite Vineet having already fired him from his job. Ever since he was caught stealing, Vineet disliked him immensely. During police questioning, Subrat and Shalu stated that Vishal used to assist with household chores. However, three servants, including a maid, work at Subrat's house. Around 17 employees work at his Pharma Traders firm. In such a situation, the question arises as to what kind of bond Subrat shared with the contract killer, such that Subrat would call only Vishal for every task. 2. Subrat had gone with Vishal three times in 20 days DCP West SM Qasim Abidi stated that up until 20 days prior to the murder, Subrat had also gone to several places alongside Vishal and Shalu. He mentioned that to get duplicate keys to the flat made, Shalu, Vishal, and Subrat had gone together to Gumti No. 5. There, Shalu gave Vishal ₹1200 to get the keys made. During this time, Subrat remained seated in the car, while Shalu and Vishal went to the shop. Meanwhile, prior to this, Subrat had also taken Vishal to Parade to take him shopping. There, Shalu had even helped him with making purchases. A few days earlier, Vishal's health had deteriorated; after he remained down with a viral infection for several days without recovery, Vishal's mother had sought Subrat's help. Subrat had then taken him to a doctor for treatment as well. 3. Why did Subrat fail to recognise a servant who had worked for 12 years? Vineet Minocha was murdered at 11:28 pm on the night of 5 September. When the police reached the flat in the early morning hours, the team began examining the CCTV cameras installed at the apartment's entry gate and outside the flat. In this, Vishal and his accomplice Rajkishore were clearly captured entering and exiting the flat. Following this, the police showed the CCTV footage to Subrat to identify the accused, but he refused to recognise them. Upon insistence by the police, Subrat disclosed that the youth seen in the footage was Vishal, who used to work at his firm. Vishal had worked at Subrat's shop located on Birhana Road from 2010 to 2022. Vineet Minocha had sacked him in 2022. The question arises: why did Subrat fail to recognise a youth who had worked at his shop for 12 years? Why was he still in touch with him despite his father having fired him? Meanwhile, Dheeraj Arora, brother of the accused Shalu, stated during a press conference on Thursday that when he brought this up with his sister during a jail visit, she too was astonished as to why her husband had refused to recognise Vishal in the first place. 4. Subrat spoke to the contract killer 25 times in six days After the murder, Subrat attempted to erase the call records from his mobile phone. Certain numbers were discovered in the Call Detail Record (CDR) that were absent from his call history. An investigation by the Surveillance Team of the West Zone revealed that on the day of the murder, Vishal spoke to Shalu on the phone 14 times. Meanwhile, Vishal spoke to Subrat 25 times via WhatsApp calls between 29 August and the day of the incident. When questioned, Subrat stated that due to a lack of network coverage in the flat, he frequently made WhatsApp calls. The investigation disclosed that Shalu had deleted the call history and WhatsApp messages from the day of the incident, whereas Subrat had deleted three call logs. Following his father's murder, upon learning of his wife's involvement in the conspiracy, no significant change was observed in Subrat's demeanor. He offered no reaction after the police disclosure. The investigation has also revealed that Vineet Minocha paid his son a salary of merely ₹40,000 for his expenses. 5. Party was organised by Subrat, bill paid by medical store proprietor On the night of Vineet Minocha's murder, 5 September, his son Subrat and daughter-in-law Shalu attended a couple's kitty party at the Cosmojin Lounge located in Tilak Nagar. That the party was organised by Subrat himself was revealed on Thursday by Shalu's brother Dheeraj and sister Sonia Mehrotra. Thirty-three people associated with the pharmaceutical trade attended the couple's party. On Wednesday, a video of Subrat and Shalu dancing at the party also surfaced. Records from the restaurant revealed that the duo arrived at the party at 10:30 pm itself, whereas the party was scheduled to begin from 11:30 pm. Additionally, their departure from the lounge at 3:00 am has been confirmed. Police investigation and lounge records brought another detail to light: the party bill came to approximately ₹80,000, which was paid by a medical store proprietor. In light of this, the question arises as to under what circumstances Subrat did not make the payment. Police are now preparing to summon the guests who attended the party and the medical store proprietor who settled the bill for questioning.

Umesh Pal’s wife says, ‘I am Brahmin, married in temple':Atiq’s lawyer asks, ‘Is there any record?’; did she know about clashes with Pooja Pal?
stories.summary: The hearing in the much-discussed Umesh Pal murder case has begun in a district court in Prayagraj. The lawyer representing the accused questioned Umesh Pal’s wife and BJP leader Jaya Pal in court. Jaya was asked, “How did you and Umesh get married? Was it with your consent or did someone else arrange it? Is there any record of it?” Jaya Pal said, “I belong to the Brahmin community. I married Umesh Pal in 2005, after becoming an adult, with my own consent. We got married on January 19, 2005, at a temple near my in-laws’ house. Since the marriage took place at a temple, there was no written record.” When Jaya Pal was asked about Pooja Pal, she said she did not know which caste Pooja Pal belonged to. The lawyer asked whether Pooja Pal and Umesh Pal had ever had a physical fight. Jaya said she did not know. The hearing in the much-discussed Umesh Pal murder case has now begun in the district court. Statements of Umesh Pal’s wife and witness Jaya Pal were recorded on September 8 and 9. Arguments then began. In the Special SC/ST Act Court, advocate Tarachandra Gupta questioned Jaya Pal on behalf of the accused. Tarachandra Gupta is the lawyer for Eklak Ahmed, the accused brother-in-law of Atiq Ahmed. On February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal and his two government gunmen were shot and attacked with bombs in broad daylight in Prayagraj. Umesh Pal was a key witness in the 2005 murder of BSP MLA Raju Pal. Mafia don and former MP Atiq Ahmed, his brother Ashraf, son Asad and their associates were accused of plotting and carrying out the murder. Here is what Jaya Pal told the court, why she now claims she is receiving threats to be blown up with RDX, and what happened next. Jaya Pal says she does not know whether Pooja and Umesh were related Jaya Pal told the court that people from the Gadariya community in Prayagraj and surrounding areas use Pal as their surname. She said she was aware of this. She said Umesh Pal’s friends were present when she got married at the temple, but she did not know how many people were there. Raju Pal, the murdered MLA, belonged to the Gadariya community. Jaya said she did not know whether Pooja Pal and Umesh Pal were related. She said she knew that Umesh Pal was a witness in the FIR in the Raju Pal murder case. However, she did not know in which year Umesh Pal had given his testimony in the case. Jaya says she has no information about fight between Umesh and Pooja Jaya Pal told the court that she did not know whether any court order had been passed for a CBI investigation into the Raju Pal murder case. She also said she did not know whether Umesh Pal had denied being an eyewitness when he gave his testimony in the Raju Pal murder case. Jaya said she did not know whether Umesh Pal and Pooja Pal had a physical fight in the Dhoomanganj police station area. She said that when Umesh Pal gave his testimony in the Raju Pal murder case, the Samajwadi Party government was in power in Uttar Pradesh. Jaya said she knew that Atiq Ahmed had been elected MLA from the City West constituency five times. She also knew that Atiq Ahmed had been elected MP from Allahabad district. Jaya says she does not know whether Umesh contested the election Jaya Pal said it was true that after Umesh Pal had given his testimony in the Raju Pal murder case, a district panchayat election was held. However, she said she did not know whether Umesh Pal had contested that election as a member of the OBC community. She also said she did not know whether Atiq Ahmed’s men and vehicles had been used for campaigning in that election. Jaya Pal gave this statement in the SC/ST court on September 8. Her statement was recorded again on September 9. On September 9, Eklak Ahmed’s lawyer Tarachandra Gupta again asked her questions point by point about the Umesh Pal murder case. After this, Jaya Pal raised the issue of threats to her life and claimed that she was being threatened with being blown up using RDX. Jaya tells media she is receiving threats to be blown up with RDX On September 8, Jaya became emotional when she was questioned about her husband’s murder. She said that her life was under threat. Speaking to the media outside the court, she said she was receiving death threats on social media and was being threatened that she would be blown up with RDX. Jaya Pal questioned where accused Guddu Muslim, Sabir and Armaan were and why police were unable to find them. Jaya had brought a social media poster with her, which contained the alleged threats. She said, “My life is in danger. I was followed even today. Some people linked to the Atiq gang are still active.” She submitted an application in court seeking increased security and also provided CCTV footage. The court directed the Police Commissioner to immediately increase her security. Jaya says she remembers scene of husband's murder Jaya Pal said, “I remember that scene today... My husband had returned from court and was brutally attacked on the way. I too will be killed, just as my husband was.” She questioned why police had still not been able to arrest accused Guddu Muslim, Sabir and Armaan. Jaya also showed a poster of Atiq Ahmed’s eldest son Umar. In the poster, Umar is pointing a finger as if asking someone to remain silent. She questioned whom the gesture was directed at. She said, “Every day, social media posts say Umar will come, Ali will come, and Ahzam is out. My family is being tortured. I want justice.” Security arrangements were tightened because of Jaya Pal’s appearance in court. Umesh Pal’s wife reached the court with several lawyers and supporters. Earlier, on September 1, Jaya Pal had also recorded her statement in court. Know the Raju Pal and Umesh Pal murder cases Raju Pal murder case: In 2005, BSP MLA Raju Pal was murdered in Prayagraj. Umesh Pal was among the key witnesses in the case. His testimony later became one of the factors linked to the Umesh Pal murder case. Umesh Pal murder case: On February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal was attacked in Prayagraj’s Dhoomanganj area while returning home. Umesh Pal and two government gunmen deployed for his security were killed in the attack. Following the incident, a case was registered on the complaint of Umesh Pal’s wife Jaya Pal against Atiq Ahmed, Ashraf, Shaista Parveen, Asad and several others.

stories.title: Congress ticket seekers must show ₹20 lakh in bank account:Party funding to stop for 2027 polls; winning MLA to get ₹40 lakh ‘reward’
stories.summary: In the 2027 UP Assembly elections, the Congress will not provide party funds to its candidates to contest the election. How financially capable a ticket claimant is to fight the election will now also be taken into consideration. A person claiming a ticket will have to show around ₹20 lakh in their account. The party believes that a person who is not in a position to spend money on their own at the start of their election campaign may also find it difficult to contest the election strongly. The party has not made financial standing the sole vital basis for selecting candidates; importance is also being given to influence in the region, social equations, and ties with the organisation. First, know the reason behind stopping the ‘party fund’ According to a leader associated with the Congress, this strict step has been taken keeping in mind the experiences of the last few assembly elections. In fact, in previous elections, the Congress used to give around ₹40 lakh as an election fund to its candidates. This was provided in two phases: first ₹25 lakh, and then ₹15 lakh. However, an internal review by the party revealed that on many seats, the main objective of the claimants was not to win the election or to contest it strongly. Their focus was more on the funds received from the party. The party's internal review brought three major issues to light: - 1. Attempt to save money: Instead of putting full effort into the election campaign, many candidates used to try to save a large portion of the money received from the party. 2. Slow and weak fight: Candidates who were financially dependent on the party were unable to show the expected momentum in campaigning right up to the final days of the election. 3. Harm to the organisation: This had a direct impact on the Congress's electoral performance and the morale of its workers. As a result, the party's fight for several seats remained merely a formality. Congress ticket screening will now be based on 3 criteria According to sources, the Congress screening committee has set 3 parameters to select candidates for the 2027 elections. Now, any aspirant will have to meet these three criteria to get a ticket: 1. Financial Capacity: The aspirant must be capable of bearing the expenses of election campaigning, vehicles, and office setup at their own level. A minimum amount of ₹20 lakh should reflect in their account so that they do not face financial hardship at the very outset. 2. Social Base: What is the candidate's caste and social hold in their assembly constituency? Do they have a personal vote bank that can align with the party symbol? 3. Political Acceptability: Whether the candidate possesses the capability to stand firm against strong parties like the BJP and SP and fight the election aggressively. In other words, rather than making a mere 'ticket seeker' their nominee, the party is looking for a face ready to invest their money, time, and political strength in the election. Leaders associated with the party believe this will help filter out aspirants who seek tickets merely in expectation of financial gain. Congress focuses heavily on 125 seats This new screening system within the Congress is not merely limited to making rules. Party sources reveal that out of the total 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh, potential candidates in approximately 125 identified seats are undergoing close scrutiny. On these 125 seats, alongside its old faces, the Congress is also keeping a close eye on strong or disgruntled leaders coming from other parties, particularly the SP and BSP. Behind this lies a well-thought-out strategy by the party: to strengthen its position before seat-sharing talks with the Samajwadi Party begin. Before initiating discussions with the SP, the Congress wants to make two things crystal clear: Preparing for seat-sharing with SP based on the 2017 formula Regarding seat-sharing, the Congress is preparing to make the data from the 2017 Assembly elections its primary foundation. Prior to the 2017 elections, when the SP was in power, an alliance was formed between the SP and Congress. At that time, Congress was given 106 seats, although a friendly fight took place between both parties on 8 seats. A strategy is taking shape within the Congress that if the SP could grant more than 100 seats to the Congress while being in power in 2017, then in 2027, when both parties are in the opposition and are allies of each other, why should Congress settle for fewer than 100 seats? To defeat the BJP in UP, the Congress believes that the SP also needs them, given that the Congress possesses a strong base at the national level. Congress wants: UP leadership itself to hold talks with SP An interesting political tug-of-war is also unfolding between both parties regarding seat-sharing negotiations. The Congress high command has indicated that the responsibility for settling seat distribution in UP will lie with the state unit, led by state Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam and state president Ajay Rai. Political experts state that if Congress grants the authority for seat-sharing talks to its state unit, it will send a message that the party is according full authority to its local leadership to make independent decisions and consolidate its position within the alliance. Major overhaul in the organisation, district presidents to be replaced Congress is not limiting its preparations for the 2027 elections merely to candidate selection; it is gearing up for a complete organisational reshuffle. The party is set to replace all 134 district presidents and city presidents across Uttar Pradesh soon. Their appointments were made in March 2025. The new organisation will be structured around the principle of 'social justice and representation' set by Rahul Gandhi. The announcement of the new state executive will be made keeping in mind the district-level OBC and Dalit formula.

stories.title: How Ramji Gautam became ‘villain’ for Akash Anand:Inside story behind expulsion of father-in-law and son-in-law from party; challenges mount for Mayawati
stories.summary: The ongoing turmoil in the BSP is no longer limited to the political retirement or expulsion of a father-in-law and son-in-law. Behind it lies a battle for supremacy between two of the party’s most powerful lobbies. On one side is the party’s only Rajya Sabha MP Ramji Gautam and his supporters. On the other are Ashok Siddharth and Akash Anand. For now, the father-in-law and son-in-law duo appears to be on the back foot. The question now is whether Mayawati will come up with a new formula for Akash before the elections. So, what is really happening behind this political thriller? Here is the inside story of BSP’s new power game, Ramji Gautam’s masterstroke, Satish Chandra Mishra’s role and Akash Anand’s rebellious stand. Whenever Ashok lost power, Ramji became stronger Ramji Gautam, who comes from Lakhimpur Kheri, rose through the party’s grassroots cadre. It was Ashok Siddharth who brought Gautam into the BSP and helped him rise through the ranks. Over time, both leaders came to be counted among Mayawati’s close aides. This is where a competition between them also emerged, which gradually became deeper. It is well known within the BSP cadre that whenever Ashok Siddharth became stronger in the party, Ramji Gautam’s influence was reduced. States under his charge were taken away from him. But whenever Ashok Siddharth was sidelined, Ramji Gautam’s stature rose sharply. The same has happened this time too. As soon as action was taken against Ashok Siddharth, Ramji Gautam was given charge of Sector-1, comprising 10 states. According to sources, Ramji Gautam had told some senior party leaders as early as September 3: “If Akash Anand wants to work in the BSP, his father-in-law Ashok Siddharth will have to quit politics.” On September 9, Mayawati appeared to endorse exactly this line in her post, making it clear who had been shaping the party’s narrative. How real is the fear of a takeover? In his letter announcing political retirement, Ashok Siddharth indirectly wrote that his political rivals were influencing ‘Behenji’. Mayawati was allegedly being warned that Ashok Siddharth wanted to use Akash Anand to take control of the entire party. However, according to Election Commission records, BSP’s central unit and main body include national president Mayawati, vice-president Anand Kumar, general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra, UP BSP president Vishwanath Pal, Munqad Ali, national treasurer Sridhar, Mewalal Gautam and central office secretary RK Mittal. All of them are considered among Mayawati’s most trusted leaders. They are unlikely to support Ashok and Akash against her. Without these office-bearers, the father-in-law and son-in-law duo could not legally take control of the party, even if they wanted to. However, it is being said that the politics of influencing Mayawati’s thinking made this fear take root in the BSP supremo’s mind. Satish Chandra Mishra’s complaint against Akash triggered action BSP strategist Satish Chandra Mishra is also said to have played a crucial role in the entire development. After Akash was stripped of his posts on September 3, Ashok Siddharth reposted a social media post by a Delhi-based YouTuber. The post raised questions about the party leadership and its functioning. According to party sources, Satish Chandra Mishra sent a screenshot of the repost and complete details to Mayawati. Mayawati reportedly considered this the strongest evidence of indiscipline. She was allegedly told that the father-in-law and son-in-law duo were trying to create an atmosphere of rebellion against her within the party. After this, Mayawati increased the stature of Akash Anand’s younger brother Ishan Anand and gave him an important responsibility instead of Akash. Why is Akash Anand upset? Akash Anand is said to be increasingly restless over the BSP’s declining political graph. This became evident when he recently advised the BSP chief that the party had a fund of more than ₹650 crore. He suggested that the party should use as much of this fund as possible to help candidates win the 2027 Assembly elections. However, Mayawati ignored the advice. After this, a rally was held in Sadabad in Hathras, where Akash’s aggressive style was widely appreciated. Soon after, reports emerged in the media that Akash would also play an important role in ticket distribution this time. Leaders from the rival camp reportedly used this as an issue and conveyed to Mayawati that Ashok Siddharth was behind this too. Mayawati had taken action against Akash twice earlier as well. On both occasions, he was sidelined after being labelled politically immature. A meeting in Jewar had reportedly been fixed without Mayawati’s permission, which also upset her. It is said that Akash’s opponents presented this before Mayawati as proof that he was taking decisions independently. Mayawati later issued an order making prior permission compulsory for all of Akash’s future programmes. Akash was also directed to seek Mayawati’s approval before attending any such event. The live telecast of the Jewar meeting was later not carried on the party’s official social media page. This development is also said to have increased Akash’s resentment. After this, Akash was not invited to party meetings held on August 25, August 31 and September 3. This time too, Mayawati took action against Akash, but did not clearly spell out the action in her social media post. Akash later officially confirmed it by changing his bio on his social media account. When Mayawati referred to Akash as “your (Ashok Siddharth’s) son-in-law” in her September 9 post, the remark reportedly hurt Akash Anand’s self-respect. Sources close to Akash say he was deeply hurt by the comment. Ashok Siddharth also touched upon this emotional aspect in his post announcing political retirement. Referring to Akash, he wrote that Akash became his son-in-law later; before that, he was Mayawati’s nephew and shared a blood relationship with her. Will Akash take charge again? Akash Anand is said to have been unhappy with being repeatedly accused, removed from the party, brought back and then stripped of his influence again. He reportedly feels that his political career is being treated like a toy. This time, he has taken a firm stand. Akash has reportedly refused to accept another post in the party. When he was asked to repost Mayawati’s post, he reportedly refused. Since September 3, he has stopped reposting Mayawati’s posts. Anand Kumar, Akash Anand’s father, and some other family members are said to be trying to find a middle path and calm Akash. Elections are due in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab. If Akash Anand remains completely sidelined, the BSP could face a shortage of a young Dalit face. For now, there is little expectation that Ishan can immediately fill this space. This could benefit the Azad Samaj Party led by Chandrashekhar Azad and the SP-Congress alliance. Kanshi Ram and Mayawati follow different political models One common factor in Mayawati’s political decisions, especially those concerning Akash, has been her commitment to Kanshi Ram’s principle of not promoting dynastic politics within the party. However, there appears to be a major difference between Kanshi Ram and Mayawati in the way they built the party’s second line of leadership. In 1977, when Kanshi Ram recognised Mayawati’s potential, he was 43 years old and Mayawati was 21. Kanshi Ram groomed Mayawati for 15 years. He then made her the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1995. In 2001, he publicly declared Mayawati as his successor at a rally. In 2003, she was made the party’s national president. After Kanshi Ram’s death in 2006, Mayawati became the undisputed leader of the party. Mayawati, on the other hand, declared her nephew Akash Anand as her successor in 2023. Between 2024 and 2026, she removed him from his posts and reinstated him several times. On September 10, Akash Anand was expelled from the party for the third time. Now that relations with Akash have worsened, Mayawati is working to increase the stature of her younger nephew Ishan. While Kanshi Ram developed Mayawati into an independent and strong leader during his lifetime, the BSP structure during Mayawati’s more than 25 years of leadership has remained centred around a single, dominant leader. Several leaders who emerged as strong figures in the party were eventually pushed out. They include Swami Prasad Maurya, Naseemuddin Siddiqui, Babu Ram Kushwaha, Dara Singh Chauhan and several other prominent leaders who were once considered second only to Mayawati in the BSP. Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi says Kanshi Ram took a far-sighted decision at the right time by handing over the leadership of the movement to Mayawati, ensuring that the movement did not lose momentum. However, he says Mayawati’s policy of not allowing anyone to emerge as a strong successor has pushed the BSP’s future into uncertainty.

The Nandigram seat was vacated by Adhikari after he won both constituencies. The Rejinagar seat bypoll candidate is former district BJP president Sarkar. stories.title: Delhi to hold month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan from September 17, projects worth Rs 13,820 crore lined up
stories.summary: The Delhi government will launch a month-long public service campaign, the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan', from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced on Monday.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath announces welfare measures, tech push for lawyers in UP
stories.summary: In a strong rebuke of the previous administration, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath highlighted shortcomings in governance and infrastructure. He revealed plans to provide tablets to 400 law officers for enhanced case management. Additionally, a cashless insurance scheme of up to Rs 5 lakh will be launched for advocates, while robust police infrastructure and training facilities are being prioritized.

stories.title: 'Tareekh Pe Tareekh': 100% complete, still no keys - Inside RERA’s extension loop
stories.summary: A growing number of housing developments are running past their scheduled completion dates, leading to frequent regulatory extensions that lack a guarantee of timely delivery. MahaRERA's data highlights a substantial volume of these extensions processed annually. Developers often tout impressive completion figures while still pending crucial approvals. The oversight framework fails to secure buyer possession effectively, raising concerns about the effectiveness of the system.

stories.title: 'Forcibly defeated': Mayawati flags 'govt irregularities' in Rajasthan municipal polls
Cases against 3 DMK leaders over remarks against TN CM Vijay's speech
stories.summary: In a significant move, Chennai and Kallakurichi police have initiated legal proceedings against three DMK leaders following protest remarks made on September twelfth. Notably, former minister P K Sekarbabu has been charged in Chennai for his contentious protest speech, while DMK MP A Raja faces allegations for derogatory comments aimed at a state minister. Additional cases have also emerged in Kallakurichi and Cuddalore, all linked to the same protests.

stories.title: In 1998, 31 Przewalski’s horses entered Chernobyl and reached 137 by 2018
stories.summary: After the Chernobyl disaster, an abandoned radioactive landscape became an unlikely refuge for Przewalski’s horses, a species once lost from the wild. Introduced in 1998–99, the population suffered transport deaths and poaching but continued breeding. By 2018, 137 horses were documented in Ukraine, with others established across the Belarusian border.

stories.title: More than 19,000 housing pockets have rooftop solar systems, benefits 9 lakh households
Ram temple trust rejects claim ex-Air Marshal Mishra skipped CEO interview round
Indian-origin UK nurse wins $250,000 Global Nursing Award for boosting organ donation among South Asians
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, Indian-origin nurse Agimol Pradeep has clinched the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026, celebrated for her impactful advocacy in organ and stem-cell donation. The $250,000 award will see half allocated to Upahaar's efforts in expanding organ donation initiatives. This recognition not only emphasizes the vital contributions of nurses to healthcare but also aligns with Kerala's efforts to bolster its nursing workforce amid persistent global shortages.

'First step towards safety': Meta to report child sexual abuse cases to law enforcement

AI 'fearmongering' will be good for no one: China
Trump slams AI guardrails, calls it a 'sick conspiracy'
J&K: Police bust LeT-linked OGW network, arrest 3 for aiding terrorists
Pak ups reward for Masood Azhar by PKR 20L ahead of FATF meet
Row at Dhaka University over photos of Jinnah, Jamaat ex-chief
Kai Cenat And Gigi Alayah Reunion Rumors? North West reacts on TikTok; Fashion Week sightings revive questions
stories.summary: Kai Cenat and Gabrielle “Gigi” Alayah have sparked fresh reunion rumors after being spotted together during New York Fashion Week. Cenat was seen blowing kisses to Alayah after his Vivet runway show, with her appearing to return the gesture. North West then added to the speculation by commenting on Alayah’s TikTok, “can’t believe that u n kai are back together.” Neither has confirmed that they are dating again.

stories.title: Owens Presses For Surveillance Details: Conservative demands suspect info; Turning Point reviews footage
stories.summary: Candace Owens has questioned Turning Point Action over the vandalism of Charlie Kirk’s memorial statue at the organisation’s Arizona headquarters. She urged the group to share more details from its surveillance cameras, including descriptions of the suspects or their vehicle, so the public could help identify those responsible. Turning Point condemned the incident and said it was working with law enforcement while planning to restore the damaged statue.

stories.summary: No Talks On This So Far: TDP; LJP For Transparency

Interim EC ruling on ‘real TMC’ likely on Sept 17
BJP appeals to people to light 'Aashirwad ka Diya' on Modi's birthday
17 rebel TMC parliamentarians will join BJP before or soon after Puja: NCPI MP
Cong rejects proposal from Didi's party for bypoll pact
Streamer Ejected From Scientology Church: Peters screams for help; then urges crowd to seek Jesus
stories.summary: Braden “Clavicular” Peters was removed from the Church of Scientology in Los Angeles during his Hollywood livestream after repeatedly calling for help and claiming people were trying to kill him. Outside, he continued speaking to people near the building and repeatedly told them they needed God and Jesus Christ. A clip of the confrontation was later shared on X.

stories.title: How a 26-year-old hacker breached 165 companies and exposed 100 million people
stories.summary: A man from Canada confessed to orchestrating a massive hacking scheme in 2024, which resulted in the breach of sensitive data from over 165 organizations, affecting billions of records. The perpetrators demanded hefty ransoms and trafficked stolen information on cybercrime platforms. International law enforcement cooperation led to his arrest in Canada, and he has now pled guilty to numerous offenses, awaiting sentencing in October.

stories.title: '3 Cong CMs invited to Brics dinner but they didn't turn up'
SC faults Abu Salem's maths, junks release plea
Los Angeles home used by Apple, Google and Walmart for filming, listed for $3.245 million
stories.summary: A Woodland Hills home in Los Angeles that has hosted 173 productions since 2021 is now on the market for $3.245 million. The 4,675-sq-ft property has earned more than $1.5 million from filming. The sale also includes the established Rum Punch House filming business, industry contacts, website and production-related infrastructure.

stories.title: India to export 654MW of power to Nepal daily till Dec 31
At 84, 'Nan Barb' drives 2,000km monthly to deliver donated clothes; community raises money for truck
stories.summary: At the age of 84, Nan Barb is a remarkable woman who travels over two thousand kilometers each month. She dedicates her time to delivering donated clothing from her op shop to remote communities throughout Western Australia. Her efforts bridge the gap for those in isolated areas who require essential goods, and the community is actively fundraising to secure a larger truck to enhance her vital mission.

stories.title: ED arrests ex-OSD of Baghel for role in Chhattisgarh job scam
Jethmalani: Why wasn't FIR slapped on Varma?
stories.summary: Leading lawyers called for judicial reform and increased transparency in the system. They questioned the lack of an FIR after cash was found at a judge's residence. Chief Justice Surya Kant defended the judiciary's internal complaint redressal mechanism. He stated that most complaints arise from disgruntled litigants after court reversals. Lawyers also criticized the opaqueness in judicial appointments and transfers.

stories.title: Massachusetts dairy turned cow manure and food waste into energy; it now saves thousands on heat, fertiliser and bedding
stories.summary: Jordan Dairy Farms in Rutland, Massachusetts, embraces cutting-edge anaerobic digestion technology to revolutionize waste management. By transforming cow manure and food scraps into energy and fertilizer, the farm not only boosts its sustainability but also slashes operational costs. This innovative approach not only supports the farm’s productivity but also significantly mitigates its environmental footprint, showcasing a model for responsible agriculture.

stories.title: Britain’s wasps are unusually scarce this summer, leaving researchers struggling to find them
Texas bought a 1,700-acre Hill Country ranch for a new state park; planners want it ruggeda
stories.summary: Texas park authorities are setting in motion the development of Bear Creek State Park on a newly acquired ranch. This park promises to deliver a wild and authentic outdoor adventure, featuring backcountry trails and restricted vehicle access to help protect delicate ecosystems. The aim is to foster a serene recreational environment while also preserving the pristine night skies.

stories.title: Perez Hilton cuts Las Vegas mansion price by $350,000
stories.summary: Perez Hilton has reduced the asking price of his 6,600-square-foot Las Vegas mansion by $350,000, from $4.25 million to $3.9 million. Hilton listed the six-bedroom home in June after moving to Miami with his three children. The property includes six en-suite bedrooms, a detached casita, multigenerational suite, pool and outdoor entertaining space.

stories.title: Cleveland area lost 80% of residents; 200 new homes now planned with $182 million funding potential
stories.summary: Cleveland’s near-East Side lost most of its population, falling from nearly 100,000 residents in the 1960s to fewer than 20,000 today. The city now plans 200 new homes through its Housing Innovation District, backed by $2 million in state funding. A tax increment financing plan could generate up to $182 million over 30 years for streets, sewers, parks and other improvements.

stories.title: In 1990, mining stopped at a 55-metre-deep Swedish limestone quarry; a year later...
stories.summary: Once a bustling mining site, Dalhalla is now a stunning open-air concert venue nestled in an abandoned Swedish quarry. Renowned for its outstanding natural acoustics discovered in 1991, this breathtaking locale invites performers and audiences alike to bask in the unique ambiance created by limestone walls shaped by an ancient meteorite impact. Annually, it enchants over 100,000 visitors, adding to the charm of the Dalarna region.

stories.title: A US grandfather planned a $150,000 treehouse for his grandkids; it grew into a $325,000 castle
stories.summary: What started as a simple backyard play area vision transformed into a stunning treehouse sanctuary. Priced at $325,000, this remarkable creation boasts a pirate ship and an exciting zipline. Meticulously designed by professional engineers, the treehouse prioritizes safety and the health of the trees. Its multi-tiered layout offers cozy lofts perfect for family bonding and unforgettable gatherings, making it an enduring family attraction filled with wonder and creativity.

stories.title: Indian travel vlogger claims ‘arrest’ by Afghan ‘Mujahideen’, seeks help
This Norwegian data centre cools servers with naturally cold fjord water
stories.summary: Green Mountain employs natural cooling at Norwegian data centres, using cold fjord water and ambient air. This approach significantly reduces the energy needed for server cooling operations. At one site, 8°C fjord water cools equipment through a heat exchanger. Another facility uses outside air for cooling, achieving 330 days of free cooling annually. These methods improve energy efficiency and lower the overall power usage effectiveness.

stories.title: Ann Arbor inventor turns grandmother’s fall into a patented mobility device and company
In 2016, a Montana researcher found a rock; scans later revealed a dinosaur's finest feather
‘Same government had closed the case’: Supriya Sule questions fresh CBI probe into Disha Salian’s death
stories.summary: The CBI has registered an FIR into Disha Salian's death following a court directive. This action surprised political leaders who noted the case was previously closed. The FIR invokes serious charges, though no individuals are named as accused. Salian's father provided names of individuals he wants examined by investigators. The case remains sub judice, with calls for it not to be politicized.

stories.title: In 1835, Free Frank McWorter, a formerly enslaved man, paid $100 for 80 Illinois acres
stories.summary: The Hampshire House in Manhattan has seen its unfinished penthouse sell for $6.765 million, a staggering reduction of 83% from its original listing of $40 million. This raw attic space demanded substantial work to become livable. After years of challenges and strategic efforts, it was sold through an online auction, highlighting the complexities of luxury real estate dealings in New York City.

stories.title: Why some bats live 50 years: Longevity genes overlap with cancer and virus defenses
Brownfield To Public Works Campus: New Milford advances Century Brass plan; riverside park could follow
stories.summary: New Milford plans to redevelop a former brass mill site into a municipal campus. This project includes a new fire-training tower assembled from shipping containers. The town acquired the contaminated property after a lengthy legal dispute. Moving public works will also free up land for a riverside park. This transformation reclaims industrial land for public use and green space.

stories.title: 'Triumph of truth over jhooth ki goonj': PM Modi hails BJP victory in Rajasthan civic polls
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party secured a significant victory in Rajasthan's municipal elections. BJP emerged as the largest party, winning more wards than Congress. The party achieved majorities in four out of ten municipal corporations. Prime Minister Modi thanked voters for their support and trust. These results reflect public approval of the BJP's development policies.

stories.title: In 2018, an unbuilt penthouse shell under Hampshire House roof was marketed at $40 million
stories.summary: A half-finished penthouse situated on Manhattan's prestigious Billionaires' Row was auctioned for $6.765 million, a staggering 83% drop from its original $40 million price tag. The three-story residence within Hampshire House secured a contract following an intense online bidding war. The new owner is set to embark on a challenging and expensive task to bring the property to completion, wrapping up a lengthy real estate narrative.

stories.title: Pakistan weighs austerity measures as US-Iran war drives up fuel prices
British man admits drugging, raping wife for more than 20 years; pleads guilty to 60 charges
'Ensure actual resolution, don't just formally close complaints': Uttarakhand CM Dhami warns officials during CM Helpline 1905 review
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami reviewed the CM Helpline 1905 functioning. He directed officials to ensure swift and satisfactory resolution of public grievances. Dhami stressed that complaints must be genuinely resolved, not just closed on the portal. He also called for surprise inspections and priority for land fraud and water supply issues. Accountability will be fixed for officials causing unnecessary delays or negligence.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath announces welfare measures, tech push for lawyers in UP
You can run, but can't escape law: Mann warns gangsters
Generous gift from a dear friend: Donald Trump's daughter-in-law breaks silence on oligarch funding her wedding; says there is no mystery, no conspiracy
Cooper’s Firehouse Home: Anchor restores 1906 patrol house; 9/11 legacy endures
stories.summary: In 2010, renowned journalist Anderson Cooper acquired a historic fire patrol house in Greenwich Village, prompting concerns among preservationists about the building's fate. Fortunately, it was preserved within the South Village Historic District. A poignant feature of the property is its connection to Keith Roma, a brave Fire Patrol member lost during the 9/11 tragedy. The residence now beautifully merges its rich history with a modern home.

stories.title: 3 Italian passengers fly out of Delhi without immigration clearance: What exactly happened
Trump's Green Card rule sued by a coalition of states and local governments who call new policy 'catastrophic'
Trump moves to scrap Biden-era carbon limits on US coal & gas power plants
stories.summary: The Trump administration plans to repeal Biden-era emission limits for power plants. This action removes restrictions on a major source of greenhouse gas pollution. The Environmental Protection Agency will announce the final rule soon. Environmental groups oppose the rollback, citing health and safety concerns. Legal challenges are expected against these policy changes.

stories.title: In 1990, Tennessee siblings planted 240 acres of former fields and pastures with loblolly pine...
stories.summary: In a significant conservation move, The Land Trust for Tennessee has permanently protected an expansive 852-acre estate. Siblings Mary Ann and John Sugg dedicated years to revitalizing farmland into lush forest. Their generous donation guarantees the landscape's preservation from future commercial development. Employing contemporary forestry techniques, the land trust oversees the property, ensuring a sustainable environmental legacy for generations to come.

stories.title: Trump claims Russia, Ukraine agree to stop hitting each other's energy targets
BJP stays on top, Congress gets a warning: What Rajasthan civic polls mean for 2028 assembly elections
stories.summary: The recent civic poll outcomes in Rajasthan underscore the enduring hold of the BJP despite some setbacks. Both the Aam Aadmi Party and CPM saw significant advancements in certain districts. Meanwhile, it was a mixed bag for the Congress. The Congress victories were scattered even as it ceded some ground to emerging opponents. Independents also played a pivotal role, and this may affect the formation of local boards.

stories.title: Nearly 50 lakh hit by floods in Bihar as swollen rivers breach danger marks
DGCA sends notice to Air India as 3 foreigners bypass immigration at Delhi airport, fly to Munich
A 440-year-old Elizabethan mansion with 14 acres goes up for auction at £550,000–£600,000
stories.summary: A 440-year-old Grade I-listed Elizabethan mansion, Barlborough Hall, is heading to auction with a guide price of £550,000–£600,000. Dating to 1583, the historic property near Chesterfield boasts nearly 16,000 sq ft of accommodation and 14 acres of grounds. The mansion was linked to Sir Francis Rodes and architect Robert Smythson.

stories.title: ‘Partners, not rivals’: China FM Wang Yi reveals key PM Modi-Xi consensus
Nato officer suspended after Tinder romance with Russian-born woman sparks spying fears at UK base
Meet Angus Liddell, Melbourne student who raised $10,000, launched a 10km charity swim
stories.summary: Recognized for his outstanding community service, Angus Liddell earned Kingston’s Young Citizen of the Year award. Through his initiative to host a charity swim event, he successfully generated substantial funds for various worthy causes. Additionally, he set a remarkable fundraising record at his college and engaged in lifesaving volunteer work, showcasing the meaningful influence that young leaders can have within their communities.

stories.title: $8m campaign aims to return historic land to Wampanoag owners
stories.summary: A Native-led nonprofit launched an $8 million campaign to acquire a historic Martha's Vineyard property. This site holds deep ties to the Wampanoag community and its ancestral heritage. The Aquinnah Land Initiative aims to restore the former Aquinnah Shop restaurant for community use. A significant state grant supports the acquisition and long-term maintenance of the cliffside location.

stories.title: In 1997, a Western Australian coal mine closed; its 103-hectare void filled with 30bn litres and became Lake Kepwari
stories.summary: Lake Kepwari, a former coal mine void near Collie, Western Australia, has been transformed into a recreational hub. This artificial lake now offers swimming, boating, camping, and water sports for visitors. The transformation involved significant planning, water management, and infrastructure development over many years. Water was diverted from the Collie River South Branch to fill the large void. This project demonstrates repurposing industrial landscapes for tourism and community benefit.

stories.title: Tennessee farmer leased 100 acres of century-old family land for solar instead of selling it; the 147 MW project is now powering homes and businesses
stories.summary: A Tennessee farmer chose to lease family land for a solar project. This decision allows continued ownership while generating income for future generations. The Yum Yum Solar facility, a 147-megawatt project, became operational in May 2026. This lease provides a steady income stream, addressing farming challenges and land fragmentation. The project highlights a growing trend of farmers balancing energy production with land preservation.

stories.title: 6-year-old Perth musician wins first prize and performs at Carnegie Hall
'High IQ president' is all AI needs: Trump backs US lead, blames China for 'sick conspiracy'
Allow Canadians to live and work in Europe without a visa: Mark Carney discusses possibility of closer ties with EU countries amid tensions with US
