Family donates 47 acres to expand Audra State Park
stories.summary: In a heartfelt gesture, a West Virginia family has gifted 47 acres to Audra State Park, commemorating the legacy of Victor Thacker’s great-great-grandparents, Jacob and Sarah Thacker. This donation enriches the park's landscape and opens up new opportunities for future trail development. Park officials conveyed their sincere appreciation for this contribution that enhances the region's natural heritage, providing visitors with even more space to explore and enjoy.

stories.title: In 1996, US established a court to quickly remove foreign terrorists from the country. Afghanistan's Nazira Haji Zada became the first one to be deported three decades later
Delhi HC rejects Vimal Elaichi maker’s plea over notices to Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, Tiger Shroff
In 1995, this American doctor delivered a baby girl; 25 years later, he delivered her son
stories.summary: In a heartwarming turn of events, Dr. Bryan Cox delivered Lauren Cortez in 1995 and later welcomed her son Logan James in 2020, both at the same Texas hospital. This special reunion was marked by Cox recreating a cherished photo from Lauren’s birth while singing 'Happy Birthday' to both occasions. Surprising family ties were also unveiled between Dr. Cox and Logan's family, making the moments even more memorable.

stories.title: Delhi Police recover Brics delegate’s cash-filled bag from cab in 35 minutes
stories.summary: Delhi Police swiftly recovered a missing bag containing cash. The bag belonged to a South African Brics delegate attending a summit. Police located the cab and found the bag under a seat. The delegate received his money just before his flight departure. This quick recovery ensured the delegate's timely travel.

stories.title: Mother dies a day after voting, son wins Rajasthan civic poll by just 1 vote
AIADMK targets Vijay over UK trip, claims he signed MoU with 'Noida-based' firm
In 2020, a Michigan dam failure drained Sanford Lake; six years later, the water returned and...
stories.summary: Sanford Lake has triumphantly regained its full water levels following a devastating dam failure. This notable recovery paved the way for a cherished local beach festival to return, rejuvenating community spirits. However, the dam incident unveiled significant issues with aged infrastructure, leading to prolonged challenges. Overcoming these setbacks demanded extensive engineering efforts and hundreds of millions in funding. The lake's revival heralds a pivotal phase of economic resurgence for mid-Michigan.

stories.title: 3,500-year-old British timber monument is drying out, threatening ancient secrets
‘Your collective voice’: Rahul Gandhi invites students to ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ in Indore
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi invites students to Indore for 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' on September 19. This event offers a platform for students to voice their education system concerns. He previously held similar sessions in Kota, Dehradun, Prayagraj, and Pune. The upcoming visit has sparked a political debate between Congress and BJP leaders. Gandhi aims to collectively push for necessary changes within the education sector.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: 17 NCPI MPs to join BJP, Pakistan lists JeM chief Masood Azhar as fugitive & more
You can buy a social media account. Or sell yours
stories.summary: Social media accounts now change hands on sophisticated marketplaces where buyers shop by followers, audience, age, monetisation and price. Sellers get paid for the history and credibility they have built.

stories.title: Kejriwal-Sardesai Goa gambit: Attack defections, welcome rivals
stories.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party have unveiled their 'Goa First' coalition in preparation for the 2027 elections. This initiative aims to connect with voters disillusioned by frequent party changes. Leaders Kejriwal and Sardesai advocate a non-BJP, non-Congress option for locals. Historical elections exhibit notable shifts in party loyalties, while this alliance's inclusive approach may offer both chances and obstacles.

stories.title: 'PM Modi keeps saying 'Sab Changa Si', but actually 'Sab Mehanga Si': Congress jabs Centre over inflation
'Ban defectors from public office': CJP backs Kapil Sibal's call for ban on MPs, MLAs who switch parties
UP assembly elections and fight for Muslim votes: Decoding SP, Congress's Owaisi problem
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM is actively pursuing alliances with opposition parties in preparation for the upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh. AIMIM's strategy revolves around consolidating its Muslim voter base to compete with major parties like the Samajwadi Party and Congress, which are also targeting this demographic. Should the opposition remain divided, the BJP could exploit these fractures for electoral gains.

stories.title: 'Someone from that ward voted for me': BJP candidate gets 1 vote in Rajasthan local body polls
'Protect our children online': Macron urges EU to fast-track social media ban for children under 15
Memorial statue of slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk vandalised with red paint in Phoenix
‘Spirit of country is pluralism’: Owaisi hits back at Amit Shah’s UCC pledge, questions BJP allies’ independence
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi questioned Amit Shah's Uniform Civil Code announcement for 21 states. He argued the UCC targets Muslims and is not about equality. Owaisi challenged the BJP to implement the UCC framework in Goa. He also criticized laws like the Disturbed Areas Act and love jihad provisions. The ongoing electoral roll revision and past NRC concerns were also highlighted.

stories.title: Surrogate mom discovers baby’s dad is Chinese billionaire with 300 US-born kids seeking a Musk match
stories.summary: A Chinese billionaire is allegedly engaging in American surrogacy to have more than a hundred children, raising significant ethical concerns. One surrogate discovered that her intended father had multiple surrogacy arrangements already in progress. This scenario underscores a troubling lack of transparency in the surrogacy sector, prompting vital discussions on surrogate rights and the necessity for clearer disclosure from intended parents.

stories.title: Maharashtra govt aims to table UCC Bill in assembly winter session: CM Fadnavis
‘Complainant attacked me’: Swatantra Bhardwaj tells Delhi court, says arrest politically motivated
Himalayas nearing tipping point: Glacier loss puts India at risk
stories.summary: Recent studies reveal that Himalayan glaciers are melting at an unprecedented rate, posing a critical threat to water supplies for millions in the region. This alarming rate of ice loss not only raises concerns about water availability but also destabilizes glacial lakes, heightening the risk of catastrophic floods and landslides. The potential reduction in river flows following peak water periods further exacerbates India’s vulnerability to these environmental challenges.

stories.title: Goa club fire: Accused Luthra brothers surrender after SC rejects bail relief, sent to judicial custody
stories.summary: After the Supreme Court declined to intervene in their bail cancellation, nightclub owners Saurabh and Gaurav Luthra, along with Ajay Gupta, have surrendered to a Goa court. The seriousness of their charges, stemming from a catastrophic fire in December 2025 that resulted in twenty-five fatalities, led the Bombay High Court to cancel their bail. The charges they face include culpable homicide not amounting to murder and criminal conspiracy.

stories.title: Pakistan lists Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar as fugitive, hikes bounty ahead of FATF review
‘I was scared and angry’: Bill Clinton reveals CIA abandoned pre-9/11 plan to take out Bin Laden
Scientists taught bald ibises migration by microlight; Europe saw its first colony in 400 years
stories.summary: Conservationists successfully reintroduced northern bald ibises to Europe after centuries of absence. Young birds were trained to follow microlight aircraft south to Italy for winter. This innovative method helped them relearn ancient migration routes and return independently. By 2011, the birds began returning without human guidance, establishing a self-sustaining colony. Further management interventions are still needed to ensure the species' long-term viability.

stories.title: US may swap federal land on Georgia’s Cumberland Island for private parcels; conservation rules could reshape what happens next
stories.summary: The National Park Service is evaluating the possibility of land exchanges on Cumberland Island. The strategy involves acquiring privately owned parcels in exchange for federal lands, which will continue to be protected under conservation restrictions. The agency invites public input regarding the possible environmental repercussions of this initiative, which aims to enhance the management and consolidation of safeguarded areas on the island.

stories.title: India to supply 654MW of electricity for 18 hours daily to Nepal after deadly floods cripple power sector
Couple finds aquifer near ocean, now the water sells for $10
stories.summary: In South Australia, a couple stumbled upon a remarkable underground aquifer beneath their land, launching them into the world of fine-water production. Garnering a flawless 100 points from global judges, their bottled water highlights a rising trend in consumer preference for pure, mineral-rich beverages. This phenomenon redefines traditional perceptions of water, transforming it from a mere commodity into a sought-after luxury.

stories.title: Indian landlady breaks silence after Canadian tenant's harassment claims: ‘He hadn’t paid rent for several months’
Monsoon withdrawal from parts of west Rajasthan likely around Sept 19: IMD said in bulletin
stories.summary: The weather patterns are aligning for the withdrawal of the Southwest Monsoon in west Rajasthan around September 19. Between September 14 and 18, west Rajasthan is likely to experience isolated to scattered rainfall. A low-pressure system affecting southeast Rajasthan and neighboring Gujarat is influencing precipitation levels. Heavy rains are anticipated in Saurashtra and Kutch on September 14, along with rainfall expected in east Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh during this timeframe.

stories.title: 17 NCPI MPs to join BJP soon: Rebel TMC MP Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia's big 'Durga Puja claim
'Took 80 years to restore full glory of Vande Mataram': Amit Shah
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah linked Indian language promotion to cultural nationalism. He defended the National Education Policy's multilingualism provisions as essential. Shah stressed linguistic diversity strengthens India's rich culture and history. He highlighted Maharashtra as a prime example of a multilingual state. The policy aims to foster familiarity with diverse Indian languages and cultures.

stories.title: Couple spent 5 years searching Google Maps; found a 5-acre Finnish island and built solar home
In 1869, 100 sheep became 5,000 on Socorro Island; 1,762 removed as forest-habitat vegetation cover rose 29%-85%
stories.summary: Feral sheep introduced to Socorro Island caused severe ecological damage over decades. An eradication program removed 1,762 sheep between 2009 and 2012. Vegetation cover and soil conditions began recovering surprisingly quickly after grazing pressure ceased. This recovery demonstrated the island's remarkable ecological resilience and capacity for self-repair. However, other invasive species like feral cats remain a significant conservation challenge.

stories.title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
How Singapore turned garbage ash into a 350-hectare island where mangroves and coral now flourish
stories.summary: Singapore has pioneered a remarkable 350-hectare landfill created from incinerated waste, known as Semakau Landfill. This innovative site not only manages the nation’s scarce land but also provides a habitat for diverse marine life. With migratory birds nesting and corals thriving, this man-made island exemplifies successful waste management, projected to remain operational until 2035.

stories.title: South Africa road crash involving multiple vehicles kills 21
Ohio jail built in 1878 could become offices or a speakeasy 148 years later
He paid 75 cents for a record, and sold it for $25,200 later
stories.summary: A collector discovered a rare Velvet Underground acetate in 2002. This recording contained early versions of songs from their debut album. He later sold the acetate for $25,200 to an anonymous buyer. The acetate's existence remained largely unknown for many years. A remastered version was eventually released to the public.

stories.title: Inside Brics 2026: Video captures PM Modi’s candid moments with Xi, Putin and Prabowo
stories.summary: The Brics Summit 2026 took place in New Delhi on September 12 and 13, showcasing previously unseen moments of camaraderie among global leaders. Prime Minister Narendra Modi engaged in meaningful discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, as well as Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. The event underscored India's leadership in addressing international cooperation and pressing global challenges.

stories.title: From Mumbai’s Lalbaugcha Raja to festivities in Tamil Nadu: How India is celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi
stories.summary: Today marks the vibrant celebration of Ganesh Chaturthi across the nation, with devotees converging at prominent pandals and temples to seek Lord Ganesha's blessings. Early risers flocked to ancient sites to participate in distinctive rituals, while various pandal decorations made notable socio-political statements. This festival embodies a cultural resurgence and serves as a herald of upcoming prosperity, particularly in Bengal.

stories.title: In 1966, a thrift-store painting cost under $100; 60 years later, it sold for £189,200
stories.summary: In 1966, retired art teacher Helene Plotkin bought a painting for less than $100 at a thrift store in New York. Nearly 60 years later, the work was identified as an FCB Cadell painting. After her son researched it and AI helped decipher the signature, the artwork sold for £189,200 at auction in Edinburgh.

stories.title: Australia switched on $7.8M wastewater plant that breaks down stubborn pollutants 16x faster and processes 700 megalitres annually
stories.summary: Australia's latest advancement in wastewater management showcases a pioneering recycling system that significantly trims down energy usage. This ground-breaking technology accelerates the breakdown of stubborn pollutants far quicker than traditional systems, effectively destroying contaminants and producing purer water. Recently, the Dubbo Regional Council inaugurated this state-of-the-art treatment plant, enhancing the water security not just for Dubbo but for the broader region as well.

stories.title: Disha Salian death case: CBI registers FIR, takes over probe from Mumbai Police
Scientists built a sponge pulling water from dry air; yields 1.72L per kg/day
stories.summary: Scientists have engineered a groundbreaking wood-derived material capable of extracting water from arid air, effectively capturing moisture even at humidity levels as low as fifteen percent. Featuring a solar thermal storage component, it enables water release under dark conditions. Field experiments yielded substantial quantities of potable freshwater daily, signifying a revolutionary advancement in atmospheric water collection.

stories.title: Ex-Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal surrenders before Goa court in 2013 rape case
stories.summary: Tejpal had challenged the high court’s verdict in the Supreme Court, which directed him to surrender within two weeks. The high court’s ruling on August 6 overturned his acquittal by a Goa sessions court in 2021 and convicted him of the offence. The Supreme Court’s direction means Tejpal must begin serving his sentence, subject to any further orders in his appeal.

stories.title: Priscilla Chan helped protect a Hawaiian beach and wetland; 17 acres now protected
'Namaste Bharat': Israeli envoy wishes on Hindi Diwas, calls language ancient like Hebrew
stories.summary: Hindi Diwas is observed every year on September 14 to commemorate the adoption of Hindi in the Devanagari script as the official language of the Union by the Constituent Assembly on September 14, 1949. The observance of Hindi Diwas began on September 14, 1953, and has continued since then. Union home minister Amit Shah also extended heartfelt greetings to citizens.

stories.title: Tennessee family seeks energy campus on 850 acres, sparking resident concerns
Jersey City moves to save 20-year community garden with $1.2 million purchase
'Everyone's been bugging me': Trump to remove 10% duty on Irish whiskey
stories.summary: During the trophy presentation at the Irish Open, US President Donald Trump dropped a significant announcement: he plans to abolish the 10% tariff on Irish whiskey. This action responds to ongoing pleas from Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin and the golfing community. The Distilled Spirits Council of the United States views this as a welcomed change that will positively impact businesses and consumers in the upcoming holiday period.

stories.title: ‘Rahul now BJP’s papa’: Congress hits back at Mohan Yadav’s ‘Jhooth Ki Goonj’ dig
stories.summary: The 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' campaign, launched by Gandhi in 2026, seeks to provide a platform for student concerns, including examination irregularities, paper leaks, rising education costs, recruitment-related issues and unemployment. The campaign has previously been held in Pune, Kota, Dehradun and Prayagraj and is aimed at bringing student grievances into the national political discourse.

stories.title: Hyderabad fire: Food stall catches fire in Puppalaguda area
stories.summary: On Monday, a food kiosk in Hyderabad was engulfed in flames following a gas cylinder explosion. Thankfully, no injuries were reported despite significant property damage. In a separate incident, a bus in Visakhapatnam also caught fire; the alert driver managed to pull over just in time for all passengers to evacuate safely. Authorities are now investigating the full scope of damages from these events.

stories.title: 'As India leads, world listens': Rajnath Singh hails 18th Brics joint declaration
stories.summary: In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration after intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday. The talks were complicated by differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia conflict. An earlier meeting of Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had also ended without a joint statement.

stories.title: Shot down over Iran, hunted for 50 hrs: How US fighter survived behind enemy lines
stories.summary: A US Air Force officer survived nearly fifty hours in Iran after his jet was shot down. Over ninety American service members deployed for one of the most complex rescue operations. The officer, injured, hid in Iran's desert while Iranian forces searched for him. US forces used bombers and drones to strike Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces nearby. This mission demonstrated the US commitment to recovering its personnel.

Clavicular Claims Cultural Impact: Ludwig backs 2026 nod; streamer says he streams less
stories.summary: Clavicular has responded after Ludwig named him among his five picks for Streamer of the Year 2026, alongside Kai Cenat, IShowSpeed, Stable Ronaldo and Jynxzi. Ludwig said Clavicular may have had the biggest cultural impact on the list, despite the choice potentially causing debate. Clavicular agreed, writing, "Easily the biggest impact on culture, but I don't stream enough recently." He also said he wants to create a real impact beyond streaming.

Palo Alto’s 500-foot horizontal levee reuses wastewater to restore marshes and test sea-rise defence
stories.summary: Palo Alto engineers have created a unique horizontal levee along Harbor Marsh. This innovative structure combines native plants and treated wastewater for coastal protection. The project aims to provide habitat and adapt shorelines to rising sea levels. Researchers are monitoring its performance as a pilot for future defenses. This living shoreline offers a new model for coastal resilience and ecosystem integration.

189 years after import, possums damage half of trees in rare New Zealand forest
Since 2000, Marc Benioff and his wife bought 600 plus acres in Hawaii, only to donate 440 acres
stories.summary: Since 2000, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff and his wife, Lynne, have bought more than 600 acres in Hawaii worth nearly $100 million. They later donated 440 acres to support affordable housing on the Big Island. The Ouli Project will begin with 43 self-help homes for low- to moderate-income residents, along with parks and community spaces.

stories.title: India, France boost space cooperation with 3 key agreements between their companies
stories.summary: India and France have taken a significant leap in space collaboration, with new agreements enhancing their partnership. These arrangements include satellite launch agreements and the development of space surveillance systems. Notably, France's Safran Space will provide essential technology for India's SBS-III constellation, while RIDE! is set to facilitate the launch of two satellites for orbital data centers. This collaboration merges French innovation with India's extensive industrial expertise.

stories.title: India, Vietnam agree to accelerate defence technology sharing, boost maritime ties
stories.summary: India and Vietnam are set to boost their defense technology cooperation, emphasising the importance of maritime and defense collaboration for enhancing regional stability. This decision emerged after talks between Prime Ministers Narendra Modi and Le Minh Hung, highlighting the recent BrahMos missile system export deal. The nations will also engage in multilateral dialogues and future discussions on defense policies.

stories.title: Brics day 2: PM flags critical minerals, tech weaponisation amid global tensions
Ladakh begins reviving Tso Kar glacial lake
stories.summary: In an ambitious move, the Ladakh administration is undertaking the revival of Tso Kar glacial lake by channeling glacier water towards it. This project aims to rejuvenate the lake's ecosystem within a year, propelled by prior success with a water diversion initiative near Leh. Local villagers have voiced concerns about the lake's ecological deterioration and its broader environmental implications, prompting efforts to establish new wetlands and habitats for migratory birds.

stories.title: Former CIA official David Rush, found with 303 gold bars worth $40 million, reaches plea agreement
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors have reached a plea deal with David Rush's legal representatives, halting grand jury actions related to the stolen gold bars. Rush, previously associated with the CIA, now faces allegations linked to a fabricated classified program. The investigation revealed gold bars and luxury watches in his Virginia residence, raising significant concerns about classified information while circumventing protracted legal disputes.

stories.title: A year on, Rs 15 lakh for kin of 4 killed in Leh firing
stories.summary: Ladakh's Lieutenant Governor announced compensation for four protesters killed last September. An ex gratia of Rs 3 lakh for major injuries and Rs 1 lakh for minor injuries was also approved. This follows demonstrations demanding statehood and constitutional safeguards under Schedule Six. Authorities imposed restrictions and arrested over eighty people after the violent protests occurred. Cases against those arrested will be withdrawn and victims will receive compensation.

stories.title: Meet Henry Xie: 17-year-old student whose method made AI models more empathetic
stories.summary: A 17-year-old student created a groundbreaking training method for artificial intelligence that enhances communication skills in smaller AI models. This unique technique received impressive empathy ratings in various tests, paving the way for more advanced conversational capabilities in personal devices. By focusing on human-like interaction, the student's research pushes the boundaries of how we develop empathetic AI.

stories.title: Reed Hastings took control of Powder Mountain with $100M in 2023; now he is spending $200M more
stories.summary: Reed Hastings is transforming Utah's Powder Mountain ski resort after a significant investment. He is combining public skiing access with an exclusive private residential community. New lifts and luxury amenities are being added to enhance both operations. This hybrid model aims to fund infrastructure improvements while preserving public access. Hastings believes this approach could offer a new blueprint for ski resorts.

stories.title: In 1936, Memphis built Overton Park Shell for $14,000; 18 years later Elvis played...
stories.summary: Memphis's Overton Park Shell, a significant landmark built amidst the Great Depression, proudly celebrates its ninetieth anniversary. Known for hosting Elvis Presley's inaugural paid show in 1954, this venue escaped demolition thanks to community efforts. Now thriving as a vibrant music hub, it offers a lineup featuring both free and ticketed events, showcasing a blend of local and international talent throughout its anniversary season.

stories.title: ‘Intolerance and racism’: US senator slams Texas Republican nominee over post targeting Asian students
Uttarakhand CM Dhami encourages youth participation in shaping 'developed Uttarakhand by 2047' at 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan'
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday participated in the 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan' programme, organised on the theme 'Mere Sapno Ka Uttarakhand' at the auditorium located at the Chauras campus of Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University.

stories.title: In 2016, NSW began fencing feral cats and foxes out of three reserves; 10 years later...
stories.summary: Thirteen native animal species have returned to New South Wales conservation reserves after a decade. These species had been locally extinct and are now breeding successfully within predator-proof fences. This conservation success is the result of a ten-year partnership involving government and scientific organizations. The state has now extended this vital conservation agreement for another ten years. Future efforts will focus on expanding these reintroductions beyond fenced areas.

stories.title: 18-year-old Afghan refugee pleads guilty to murdering man in London; accused of stalking cousin's wife
Built in 1966, San Francisco's Empress of China closed in 2016; 10 years later it reopened its doors
stories.summary: The iconic Empress of China building in San Francisco has achieved community ownership after a decade-long effort. A coalition of six Asian American non-profits came together to acquire this historic site, aiming to convert it into a thriving arts and cultural campus. The restoration project aligns with broader economic and cultural revitalization goals, inviting future public sessions to influence its architectural evolution.

stories.title: In 2015, Hawaii rescued fragments of a coral found only in Kaneohe Bay; after its wild colonies...
stories.summary: Marine biologists rescued rare Hawaiian coral fragments from Kaneohe Bay in 2015. These fragments were grown into mature colonies using a land-based nursery method. The grown corals were then returned to their natural habitat in Kaneohe Bay. Field checks confirmed the reintroduced corals successfully adjusted to their surroundings. This project demonstrates the effectiveness of coral arks for preventing species extinction.

stories.title: In 2021, a developer bought an empty Park City lot for $6 million; 4 years of construction later...
stories.summary: A Park City mountain land bought for six million dollars became a thirty-seven million dollar luxury home. This sale set the highest residential price ever recorded within the city limits. The seventeen thousand square foot mansion was completed after four years of construction. It features extensive ski-in, ski-out facilities and high-end amenities for wealthy buyers. Limited supply and high demand continue to boost Utah mountain luxury housing markets.

stories.title: Mamata's TMC faction names candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls in Bengal
Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pak expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi after Houthi attacks
stories.summary: Pakistan voiced strong solidarity with Saudi Arabia following recent Houthi attacks. These strikes threaten regional peace and could disrupt global energy supplies. Prime Minister Sharif discussed these issues with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The recent Houthi advances have also intensified concerns over Red Sea shipping routes. A mutual-defense pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye is now under renewed focus.

stories.title: Chinese FM Wang Yi stepped in for Xi at PM Modi’s Brics gala dinner: Reports
How Monty Don turned a 2-acre field into a garden millions love
stories.summary: Monty Don is stepping down from Gardeners' World after 23 years. He transformed his private garden, Longmeadow, into a nationally recognized space. Viewers watched his garden evolve over three decades of television. Don learned to observe his land before making any changes. Gardening provides a sense of purpose, freedom, and empowerment for people.

stories.title: Heavy rain floods New Jersey roads, leaves 5,600 without power; vehicles stuck in rising waters
'Not our culture to impose Emergency, we believe in dialogue': Amit Shah on Gen-Z led movements
'Unacceptable': India condemns attack on commercial vessel off Oman, 13 Indians rescued
'Not IPL commentary': Congress takes shot at Ravi Shastri for post praising PM Modi
28 Tasmanian devils were moved to an island; 3,000 penguin pairs later disappeared
stories.summary: In 2012, 28 Tasmanian devils were introduced to Maria Island as an insurance population against facial tumour disease. The devils thrived, reaching up to 90, but experts say their presence came at a heavy cost to local wildlife. A survey later found Maria Island’s little penguin colonies had disappeared, wiping out an estimated 3,000 breeding pairs.

stories.title: Dubbo Wastewater Plant Starts: New catalyst breaks down stubborn pollutants; city bets on recycled water
stories.summary: This week, an innovative wastewater treatment facility was inaugurated in Dubbo, New South Wales, marking a significant upgrade in regional water management. Capable of processing large quantities of wastewater each year, the plant employs cutting-edge technology to effectively decompose challenging contaminants. The recycled water generated will have diverse applications, aiding local communities, especially in drought-affected areas, by transforming wastewater into a crucial resource.

stories.title: The Uranium rush: Inside India's scramble to fuel its nuclear ambitions
stories.summary: India is securing uranium fuel for its ambitious nuclear expansion program. Uzbekistan, Australia, and Canada are key partners in this global fuel hunt. New domestic laws allow private companies to build nuclear power plants. This move creates significant demand for uranium fuel supplies. India's long-term strategy also involves developing thorium resources.

Canadian Citizenship Certificate backlog hits 136,000, wait time now nearly 3 years
‘We will continue in Congress’: Konda Surekha rules out joining another party, eyes 2028 polls
stories.summary: Former Telangana minister Konda Surekha stated she will remain with the Congress party. She confirmed her intention to contest the upcoming 2028 Assembly elections. Surekha also expressed confidence in securing the Congress ticket for Warangal East. She indicated the party leadership is in touch following her cabinet removal. Surekha and her husband will continue working for people's issues.

stories.title: Altitude and attitude: How DGCA makes sure high-flying pilots don’t fly high
Evening news wrap: Xi rejects ‘might makes right’ logic at Brics; Anthropic CEO flags AI’s catastrophic risks & more
90-year-old iconic Twin Chimneys motel in Cheyenne torn down for a coffee drive-thru
stories.summary: The Twin Chimneys Motor Court in Cheyenne, Wyoming, was demolished this week after almost 90 years. Its distinctive twin stone chimneys, a landmark along the historic Lincoln Highway, fell in about 30 seconds. The site will now make way for a 7 Brew Coffee drive-thru stand, ending the story of the once-popular motor court.

stories.title: In 1876, Los Angeles built the Perry House; 99 years later it was moved to Heritage Square
stories.summary: Los Angeles' historic Perry Mansion celebrated its 150th anniversary by opening its second floor. This rare access allowed visitors to see preserved 19th-century rooms and raise funds. The grand Victorian residence was built in 1876 for businessman William Hayes Perry. Preservationists saved the mansion from demolition in 1975 and moved it to Heritage Square Museum. Funds raised will support ongoing structural conservation and protection of the historic wooden building.

stories.title: From PM Modi-Putin car ride to Pezeshkian hug: 5 unmissable moments of Brics Summit 2026
Plugging gap: Why 67,000 EV charging points aren't enough for India’s electric dreams
stories.summary: By 2030, India is projected to require an additional 1.25 million electric vehicle (EV) charging stations. Currently, these public chargers are limited to just ten states, and the slower charging speeds provided by many of them may pose challenges during longer trips. While home charging is an option for individuals with private parking, operators struggle with low usage rates that deter investments in smaller urban areas.

stories.title: Is UK heading for a breakup? Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland push for independence
US Republican governor candidate escapes plane crash, swims to safety after emergency lake landing
How Gujarat's villagers turned mangroves into a natural coastal shield
stories.summary: Gujarat's mangrove cover dramatically increased from 427 sq km in 1987 to over 1,177 sq km by 2026. This significant recovery is attributed to community participation and large-scale plantation programmes. Mangroves provide vital coastal protection and support marine ecosystems and local livelihoods. The government now promotes this approach nationwide through the MISHTI programme. Gujarat's success demonstrates mangroves as effective natural infrastructure for coastal defense.

stories.title: Canada explores ‘associate member’ status with EU amid US trade tensions
stories.summary: Canada explores becoming an associate member of the European Union. Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks stronger economic and strategic ties with the bloc. This move comes as Canada's trade relationship with the United States has worsened. Discussions focus on free movement of goods, services, and workers. Deeper cooperation is also being considered in energy and technology sectors.

'AAP will be extra cautious': Kejriwal on future Rajya Sabha picks after Raghav Chadha exit
Feather found in dinosaur poop may explain how birds survived the asteroid that killed dinosaurs
stories.summary: The 66-million-year-old feather found inside fossilised dinosaur poop may offer clues about why some birds survived the asteroid impact that killed most dinosaurs. Researchers found feathers, fish scales and bird bones in the coprolite. The feather’s primitive structure suggests insulation and moulting may have played a role in determining which birds survived.

stories.title: Rajasthan SET 2026: Students boycott exam in Jaipur over delayed papers, alleged irregularities
stories.summary: In Jaipur, students staged a protest and boycotted the Rajasthan SET-2026 exam due to a significant delay in the arrival of question papers, which reached the examination hall nearly thirty minutes after the scheduled start. Candidates expressed grave concerns about exam irregularities and called for a re-examination, underlining ongoing challenges faced in competitive testing in India. Official confirmation of the exam's status remains pending.

stories.title: 'World expects concrete results': PM Modi extends best wishes as Brics chairship passes to China
Amit Shah says decolonising knowledge not about erasing history, but reclaiming India's narrative
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah emphasized decolonizing India's history and knowledge authentically. He stated that true knowledge should remain free from any ideological constraints. Shah highlighted the importance of preserving India's knowledge traditions and manuscripts. He proposed creating a wider network for sharing heritage collections across India. The minister urged using Indology for the nation's and world's welfare.

stories.title: Scientists used centuries-old aurora sightings: their method placed solar minima within 2 years with more than 90% reliability
stories.summary: Ancient auroras are unlocking secrets of solar activity, offering scientists a glimpse into the Sun's behavior long before our time. By employing a new statistical method to analyze historical sky observations, researchers have pieced together eight distinct cycles of solar activity from 1560 to 1640. This intriguing study correlates well with various independent solar records, enhancing our understanding of solar dynamics pre-dating contemporary measurements.

9/11 grounded US flights, but strangers moved a liver 800 miles to save a baby
stories.summary: In 2001, six-month-old Kareena needed a liver transplant and was too sick to leave hospital. When US flights were grounded after 9/11, strangers and Tennessee National Guard members moved the donor liver nearly 800 miles from Nashville to Houston. Twenty-five years later, Kareena has graduated from college and is studying health policy in law school.

stories.title: ‘Not working with his own mind’: Mayawati alleges nephew Akash remains under Siddharth’s influence
Beyond 'seek help': What happens when students reach out for mental health support?

Martha Stewart’s 152-acre farm now has 100+ chickens and 11 pheasants
Indian-origin father dies after being struck by truck in Australia, weeks after daughter's birth
Donated 100 acre Texas ranch becomes $145mn Odessa complex
stories.summary: A Texas family's generous land gift is becoming a major sports and recreation complex. This $145 million project will serve as a neighborhood hub and tournament destination. Construction is progressing towards a significant milestone with a topping-out ceremony next month. The expansive facility will feature numerous indoor courts and outdoor fields for various sports. This new complex promises to draw visitors and boost local economic growth.

stories.title: ‘Might makes right’ logic should have been discarded long ago: Xi at Brics Summit
Air India Bhopal-Delhi flight diverted to Jaipur over technical issue, lands safely
Noida DM moves SC over student's detention under NSA after HC rebuke
Russian President Putin departs New Delhi after attending Brics Summit
Beijing tightens drone crackdown, bans possession, storage across city from Nov 15
stories.summary: As of November 15, Beijing will officially prohibit residents and businesses from owning drones. Existing drone owners must either sell their devices or dispose of them before the deadline. Infringers will face potential confiscation of their drones along with hefty fines. This regulation enhances security measures, significantly restricting drone operations within the city, following previous limitations on unauthorized flights and the classification of all airspace as restricted.

stories.title: Fresh attacks on Strait of Hormuz shipping fuel fears over oil supplies
stories.summary: During its passage through the Strait of Hormuz, a ship was hit by a projectile, raising alarms about the stability of global energy supplies following a prior drone attack. In response, Saudi Arabia has temporarily closed its crucial East-West oil pipeline as a safety measure. The escalating conflict in the Middle East poses a risk of increased energy prices, with further updates on the situation anticipated shortly.

stories.title: Ukraine deploys drone specialists to Africa, Middle East to target Russian interests: Report
Delhi building evacuated after sudden tilt, owner asked to demolish structure
stories.summary: On Sunday, a four-story structure in Shahdara's Gandhi Nagar lost its balance unexpectedly, prompting swift action from authorities. The area surrounding the building was quarantined while the Municipal Corporation of Delhi conducted an inspection, ultimately mandating its demolition. This incident comes on the heels of a tragic building collapse in Satya Niketan that led to loss of life, and officials are now closely monitoring the area to ensure community safety.

stories.title: Melbourne couple builds $880,000 recycled-bottle Earthship after moving to Tasmania
In 1973, Ontario teacher Hank Deverell built his wife a bottle house for her doll collection
stories.summary: In 1973, Ontario teacher Hank Deverell built a bottle house in Redditt, Ontario, for his wife Myrtle’s growing doll collection. Using thousands of glass bottles, mortar and 1,750 hours of labour, the project grew into a tourist attraction. The property later became known for its bottle-built structures and Myrtle’s doll collection, drawing visitors from Canada and abroad.

stories.title: Britain used waste tyres in M1 asphalt, recycling up to 750 per kilometre
stories.summary: In 2019, Britain initiated a groundbreaking trial using recycled tyre rubber for its roads, particularly targeting the M1 motorway to gauge its performance under heavy traffic. This method not only helps in managing waste tyres but also paves the way for sustainable infrastructure solutions. Tarmac's ULTIPAVE R system received the green light for broader use, marking a significant step forward in environmentally friendly road construction.

stories.title: 'I resign as CM': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke mocks MP govt after Balaghat heckling
'Is it okay?' PM Modi pauses speech as Xi appears uncomfortable; Chinese president skips gala dinner
stories.summary: At the recent BRICS Summit held in New Delhi, Prime Minister Modi and President Xi focused on strengthening their countries' long-term ties, stressing the necessity of safeguarding peace along the border. The discussions prominently featured the trade deficit and the challenge of market access. Both leaders also committed to boosting cultural and business exchanges to achieve shared growth and prosperity.

stories.title: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi meet Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim over breakfast
In 1999, David Letterman bought this 2,700-acre Montana ranch while leaving showbiz behind
stories.summary: David Letterman owns a 2,700-acre ranch in Montana that he bought in 1999, along with properties in Indiana and upstate New York. The former late-night host has spoken about leaving behind the pressures of show business and returning to Indiana with his family. His childhood home in Indianapolis has since been sold and turned into a short-term rental.

stories.title: Xi in the room, PM Modi warns against 'weaponisation of critical minerals'
At 100, Barbara Haig still drives her Mustang, putting caution before age
1876 Perry House opens rare second-floor rooms for fundraiser
stories.summary: The Perry House, built in 1876, celebrated its 150th anniversary with a special event. Visitors gained rare access to the mansion's second floor after decades of closure. This event served as a crucial fundraiser for ongoing restoration projects. The house, relocated in 1975, showcases intricate Victorian-era craftsmanship. Proceeds from the event will support the continued preservation of this historic structure.

stories.title: S Korea's revised espionage law: How it affects countries beyond North Korea
stories.summary: South Korea's expanded espionage law now covers all foreign countries, not just North Korea. This revised Criminal Act carries a minimum three-year prison sentence for espionage offenses. The amendment addresses concerns about technology and industrial espionage involving non-North Korean actors. High-profile technology leak cases, including those involving Chinese firms, preceded this change. South Korea aims to strengthen its ability to prevent leaks of strategic technologies.

stories.title: In 2001, Bear Grylls bought a £95,000 Welsh island and rebuilt its only home
stories.summary: In 2001, Bear Grylls bought a remote Welsh island for £95,000 when its only house was a “complete wreck”. He and friends spent four years rebuilding it. The island is now an off-grid family retreat, with the house powered by wind and solar energy and rainwater collected from its roof.

stories.title: In 2024, New York turned 250 Christmas trees into breakwaters to restore salt marsh
stories.summary: Discarded Christmas trees found a new purpose in Jamaica Bay, where they transformed into natural breakwaters at a wildlife refuge. The structures served to safeguard newly planted salt marsh vegetation from erosive waves. By the fall, these barriers effectively trapped sediment, partially burying themselves in the marsh. This innovative ecological restoration project showcased how recycled trees could enhance a living shoreline system, bolstering the marsh's resilience and self-protection.

stories.title: 25 years after 9/11, Ten House has just one active member left from that day
stories.summary: Sal Argano, the last firefighter from 2001 at FDNY’s Ten House, serves as a living link. He survived the September 11 attacks due to a temporary assignment elsewhere that morning. His firehouse, located across from the World Trade Center, was damaged and lost six members. Argano continues working to share firsthand accounts with younger generations and visitors. He remains at the station to preserve memories as others retire.

stories.title: The $100 billion ghost city experiment that lasted less than two years
stories.summary: Forest City's empty towers attracted a tech community seeking a new living model. Network School participants lived and worked together, testing Balaji Srinivasan's ideas. The experiment faced challenges with living conditions and official scrutiny. Less than two years after starting, operations were ordered to cease. This unusual setting provided a large experiment space for the community.

stories.title: Two giant dams starved the Danube Delta of sediment for decades
stories.summary: The Danube's sediment supply to its delta has significantly decreased due to upstream engineering works. Large dams like the Iron Gates trap sediment, altering the natural balance of the delta. This reduction in material has led to increased coastal erosion along the delta's seaward edge. Recently, ten obsolete dams were removed from smaller rivers to reconnect fragmented habitats.

This state-of-the-art facility will complement the existing range in Chandipur, Odisha, marking the DRDO's third significant site. The initiative promises to not only bolster national defense capabilities but also promote substantial growth in West Bengal's infrastructure and economy.

Brics opposes unilateral trade steps like EU carbon border tax
stories.summary: In a united front, BRICS countries protested against the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism, deeming it unfair. They underscored the importance of energy security alongside a pragmatic approach toward climate goals, making it clear that fossil fuels remain integral to the energy mix. The alliance urged for actions driven by equity and collective responsibilities, indicating their trust in multilateral efforts to confront global climate challenges.

stories.title: Modi: Global South must shape, not just follow, rules
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi opened the Brics summit, demanding urgent United Nations Security Council reforms. He stressed transforming global governance from privilege to partnership for developing nations. Modi proposed Brics draft ten proposals for inclusive global governance and multilateralism. He also called for a Seafarers Emergency Support Network for maritime workers. The summit aims to empower the Global South as rule-shapers, not rule-takers.

The declaration underscored the need for zero tolerance and criticized discrepancies in counter-terrorism responses. It affirmed that states have the primary duty to combat terrorism, asserting that terrorism must not be associated with any particular religion or nationality.

To complement the reissue, the Hearst Center hosts an exhibition spotlighting McGehee's original artworks. This initiative not only revitalizes Suckow's literary legacy but also ensures her stories resonate with contemporary audiences, bridging Iowa's rich literary history with today's readers.

The leaders reiterated the critical role of constructive dialogue in achieving regional stability. Furthermore, they collectively reaffirmed their resolve to combat terrorism in all its manifestations and called for extensive reforms of the United Nations Security Council.

stories.title: Skeleton Found In Roman Jar: archaeologists uncover 1,600-year-old victim; find hints of desperate escape
stories.summary: In a remarkable excavation at Deultum, Bulgaria, archaeologists uncovered the remains of a young man entombed within a sizable storage jar. The evidence indicates he sought refuge there during a devastating attack, likely after the flames had already engulfed the area. His plight, frozen in time as the jar was later rebuilt over, provides a poignant glimpse into the terror and desperation of ancient times.

stories.summary: Authorities in Doda's Divshetar have discovered the decomposed body of a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist from Pakistan. The remains, thought to have been buried in snow for some time after a previous operation, were found with an M4 rifle. Security forces are currently working to determine the identity of the individual as part of a broader investigation following recent encounters in the Jammu region.

stories.title: SIA searches Poonch, Udhampur in radicalisation probe
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir State Investigation Agency searched five locations Saturday. These searches occurred in Poonch and Udhampur districts for investigations. The agency is probing alleged secessionist narratives spread through online and offline channels. Investigators found individuals contacted suspicious persons across the Line of Control. Officials will share more details after the searches conclude.

stories.title: Deer Learn To Ignore Deterrents: Human shouts scare best; habituation soon blunts effect
stories.summary: Research indicates that loud human noises and bright lights were effective in driving deer and elk away from crops, while predator sounds and dog barks didn’t have the same effect. Over a period of six weeks, these animals became accustomed to the deterrents, especially those near human activity. Researchers recommend diversifying stimuli and introducing consequences to keep these animals from adapting.

She purchased the sprawling California property for $12.05 million in 2016, aged 19. The lavish 1.4-acre estate features eight bedrooms, eight bathrooms, a pool, spa, home theatre and multiple entertainment spaces.

This unexpected reunion in 2026, facilitated by mutual friends, allowed them to reflect on the emotional weight of that significant day, bringing closure and a shared sense of nostalgia for their remarkable journey.

stories.title: In the 1850s, pigs brought to Santa Cruz Island became feral
stories.summary: Feral pigs were eradicated from Santa Cruz Island, facilitating a resurgence in fox populations. With bald eagles no longer in the area, golden eagles preyed on the island's foxes. In response, conservationists captured the golden eagles and reintroduced the native bald eagles. A captive breeding initiative safeguarded the remaining island foxes from predators, resulting in a successful revival of the island's native wildlife and ecosystem.

stories.title: From Iraq to Yemen: How Iran-linked groups are putting Saudi energy routes under pressure
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its East-West oil pipeline after a drone attack. This vital energy conduit transports millions of barrels of crude oil daily. The attack has increased pressure on Iraq and raised global supply concerns. Houthi rebels in Yemen have also advanced along the Red Sea route. These events disrupt major energy and shipping routes worldwide.

The move has drawn criticism from conservation groups and advocates.

Well-known personalities like Drake and Beyoncé endorse this elite brand, which also provides personalized fittings and premium mattresses in India.

stories.title: Which countries are home to the largest number of Indian migrants?
stories.summary: United Arab Emirates and the United States host the largest Indian-born populations abroad. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan follow with significant numbers of Indian emigrants. Kuwait, the United Kingdom, and Canada also have substantial Indian communities. Australia, Oman, and Qatar are other key destinations for Indian migrants. These figures highlight the Gulf's significant role in Indian overseas migration.

Her academic pursuits began in 1930, but she put her education on hold to raise a family. At 98, she didn't stop there and accomplished the incredible feat of earning her master's degree, symbolizing a powerful testament to lifelong commitment to education.

stories.title: Donald Trump's childhood home was bought for $835,000 in 2025; it has sold for $1.93 million
stories.summary: The childhood home of Donald Trump, located in Queens, has been sold for an impressive $1.93 million. With ties to Trump's early years, its historical significance has notably heightened its market value.

stories.title: Air India pilot dies during Delhi layover
stories.summary: In a tragic incident, a Mumbai-based Air India pilot was discovered unconscious in his hotel room during a layover in Delhi on Friday. Despite immediate efforts to rush him to a hospital, he sadly succumbed. Recently transferred from Air India Express to the main airline, his brother raised the alarm after repeated calls went unanswered. Authorities are now awaiting post-mortem results to ascertain the cause of his untimely death.

Leaders engaged in high-profile diplomatic discussions during the summit. India hosted the 18th Brics summit focusing on cooperation and sustainability.

stories.title: Chicago reversed its river in 1900 to divert sewage from Lake Michigan; 126 years later, it flows backwards
stories.summary: To combat outbreaks of disease linked to polluted drinking water, Chicago undertook an extraordinary engineering project to reverse its river's flow. This initiative, aimed at diverting sewage from Lake Michigan, successfully bolstered public health over the decades. Despite facing legal struggles from neighboring Missouri and other states, the new river connection has inadvertently introduced fresh ecological challenges that could disrupt local ecosystems.

The extradition followed coordination between Indian agencies and Moldovan authorities. Singh was apprehended near the Moldova border after an Interpol Red Notice was issued. He will now face multiple criminal charges registered against him in Punjab.

stories.title: In 2001, a guard saved 6 from the burning World Trade Center; 25 years later, they are trying to save him
stories.summary: A security guard who saved lives during 9/11 now battles kidney cancer. Dereck Lovell guided survivors through the South Tower's smoke and flames. He is now awaiting a kidney transplant after his own kidneys were removed. Survivors he rescued are raising awareness for his urgent need. Lovell, who considers himself a job doer, is now receiving help.

stories.title: For decades, scientists thought North America had a cheetah; DNA links it to pumas 2.6M years ago
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking revelation, ancient DNA analysis has clarified that Miracinonyx trumani is more closely related to pumas than cheetahs. This extinct cat thrived in North America during the Pleistocene epoch and had the unique ability to fish in colder regions. While its structure suggested agility, evolutionary genetics indicated that convergence was at play, with low genetic variety likely contributing to its disappearance from the ecosystem.

stories.title: Brics New Delhi Declaration adopted: Terrorism, conflict resolution, tariff concerns addressed; key points
stories.summary: The New Delhi Declaration 2026 was unanimously adopted by BRICS nations at their summit. This declaration emphasizes conflict prevention and the peaceful resolution of international disputes. BRICS countries also backed stronger multilateralism and expressed concerns over unilateral trade measures. Prime Minister Modi called for global governance reforms and greater Global South representation. India is chairing BRICS in 2026 under a theme of resilience and cooperation.

stories.title: NIA raids 10 locations across Jammu & Kashmir in LeT-linked terror conspiracy case
stories.summary: The National Investigation Agency conducted searches at ten locations across Jammu and Kashmir. These searches are connected to a cross-border terror conspiracy involving Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba handlers. The agency seized incriminating material relevant to the ongoing investigation into the conspiracy. This investigation began after the arrest of an alleged LeT-linked Over Ground Worker earlier this year. The NIA continues to examine financial and communication trails to identify all involved individuals.

stories.title: 160-year-old St Louis church survives fire, condemnations and legal battle as residents take over restoration
stories.summary: Once deemed condemned, a 160-year-old church in St. Louis has been granted a new lease on life following a legal battle. Thanks to the Soulard Restoration Group’s successful court order, rehabilitation efforts can now commence. The St. Louis Receivership Group will finance the repairs, while local advocates are determined to protect the historic site from being torn down.

stories.title: Brazil’s 200 million termite mounds have formed over 4,000 years from soil termites dug up
stories.summary: Millions of ancient termite mounds dot Brazil's landscape, concealing a vast underground tunnel system. These structures, some nearly four thousand years old, represent immense ecosystem engineering by termites. The insects excavated extensive tunnels to access food in seasonally dry forests. This process created millions of evenly spaced cones over generations of work. The resulting pattern showcases a hidden subterranean system and its ancient origins.

The estate remains one of the nation's most expensive homes.

stories.title: San Francisco minted just 24 dimes in 1894; 9 survive, and one sold for $1.25 million in 2026

The remains included four amputated limbs, shedding light on historical medical practices during war. To honor this fallen hero, his remains will be laid to rest at Arlington National Cemetery, preserving the legacy of the Civil War.

stories.title: Iowa County’s wind turbines turn into $2.71 million for roads, bridges and schools
stories.summary: In Howard County, wind turbines have emerged as a significant revenue stream for public finances. This groundbreaking technology has shown consistent improvements in force generation over several years. stories.title: At 21, an Australian artist bought 25 acres in Tasmania; 18 months later a bushfire...
stories.summary: After a devastating bushfire, an Australian artist turned adversity into creativity by reconstructing her home from salvaged materials.
