China Southern to resume Guangzhou-Delhi flights after 6 years ahead of Xi's Brics visit
stories.summary: The announcement came ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to India for the Brics summit. The airline said the resumption would take its total operations across eight round-trip routes in South Asia to more than 100 flights a week. The Guangzhou-New Delhi service had been suspended for six years.

stories.title: US diesel prices at record $6: American farmers feel the heat as harvest season begins
stories.summary: With diesel prices hitting unprecedented levels, US farmers are grappling with steep fuel expenses that have doubled. This dramatic rise is disrupting essential operations for corn and soybean harvests, jeopardizing profitability and financial health. Additionally, the elevated diesel costs are hindering the logistics of moving harvested crops to market. Consequently, many farmers are contemplating delaying their tasks in hopes that prices will decrease soon.

stories.title: 'Married brother to bring him into USA': DHS probing Ilhan Omar's family immigration history
California governor signs law to limit U-16s social media risks
Saudi sought US military help as Houthis upped threat: Report
US diesel prices cross $6 a gallon amid Iran war
Afghan woman in first case for anti-terror court deported
As US marks 25 years of 9/11, victims' kin hit out at Saudi, former presidents
Canada court overturns 'unreasonable' visitor-visa refusal for 3 Indian applicants
stories.summary: According to Canada's 2025 Annual Report to Parliament on Immigration, India was the leading source country under the country's 'Visitor Program' in 2024, accounting for 5.8 lakh admissions, or about 11.5% of the total. Against this backdrop, the court's decision could offer some reassurance to applicants whose visitor-visa applications are refused without proper consideration of the evidence they have submitted.

stories.title: Qaida releases video of Osama's son who was reportedly killed in 2019
Tech glitch at Adani power unit hits Bangladesh grid
SC's 13 queries to FSSAI: 'Give details on shape, size, colour of food label'
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated that the FSSAI outline precise details about food warning labels, including their design, dimensions, colors, and position on food packaging. Additionally, the court emphasizes the importance of communicating junk food risks to children. FSSAI is tasked with addressing thirteen specific inquiries within ten days, noting while progress has been made, more detailed clarification is still necessary.

stories.title: PM gifts Putin Russian version of Tamil text 'Thirukkural'
stories.summary: In a significant diplomatic gesture, Prime Minister Modi presented President Putin with a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, an esteemed Tamil classic that encapsulates teachings on morality, governance, and affection. Moreover, it addresses conflict resolution and advocates for peace, aligning with Modi's stance on resolving the Ukraine crisis. This gesture symbolizes the enduring legacy of Thiruvalluvar that transcends cultural barriers.

stories.title: India to present 37 deep-tech ventures at Brics forum
Officials claim 50 outcomes, but no clarity on united declaration
Russia & Iran hit out at US 'aggression', pose a challenge for summit host India
stories.summary: Russia and Iran criticized Western sanctions and aggression at the BRICS Business Forum. Both nations called for strategies to enhance the group's resilience against external pressures. Iranian President Pezeshkian highlighted economic security's link to national and regional stability. Russian President Putin condemned Western dominance tactics and infrastructure destruction. Leaders discussed expanding trade in local currencies and leveraging the New Development Bank.

stories.title: Goyal: Pull down barriers, allow easy movement to professionals
stories.summary: Piyush Goyal urged Brics nations to dismantle trade barriers and open markets. He also called for linking payment systems and trading in local currencies. Streamlining customs and promoting services trade were also highlighted by the minister. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar emphasized transparent trade and investment practices. The goal is to foster business partnerships and market access for member nations.

stories.title: Counting Discounts
40% of global GDP is here: PM Modi
Cong drowned India, we rebuilt it: BJP
Tharoor: Hosting Brics matter of 'great prestige'
80 lakh HPV vaccine doses given since Feb launch
Now, you can port FASTag from one bank to another
NMC adds over 13,000 MBBS seats, total intake tops 1.4 lakh
Indian-origin investor's H-1B prediction: If 10% of Indians stuck in US Green Card backlog return, India’s GDP could rise 1%
Brazilian architect built a UFO-shaped house in 1974 and still lives there
In 1950, Long Beach opened Veterans Memorial Stadium; sold to its city college for $1 in 1987
stories.summary: Long Beach City College is embarking on an exciting $250 million redevelopment of its stadium. The decades-old Veterans Memorial Stadium will be replaced by a cutting-edge sports precinct that spans 18 acres. This new venue will feature a 10,000-seat outdoor stadium, an indoor arena, and specialized track and field facilities, along with dedicated football fields. With funding from Measure LB, the project is set to be unveiled in summer 2029.

stories.title: Elon Musk reacts to Irish man's discovery that he would have to wait for 14 years to get Indian citizenship
‘Did anyone go to jail in Kerala?’ Cong hits back at Omar amid Vande Mataram row
After Doda, Udhampur administration imposes 2-month ban on VPN use
Mirwaiz to attend Iranian president's event in New Delhi
PM doubles down on friendship with Iran, seeks win-win strategy; hope mounts for BRICS declaration
At 17, British apprentice Tom Lear began building a 12.5-sq-m tiny home on a trailer
stories.summary: Over the span of three years, a resourceful young carpenter dedicated his skills to constructing a mobile home crafted from reclaimed materials. With a budget of around six thousand pounds, this innovative micro-home serves as an affordable housing solution for young individuals, granting him both independence and a life free from debt. His achievement is a testament to creativity and sustainability.

stories.title: Princess Alexandra of Hanover announces engagement after 10-year romance; who is her fiancé?
Guarding Xi: Inside heightened security deployment
Modi reiterates peace message before Putin as efforts to end war gain momentum
'Will work with India, be friends': China ahead of PM Modi-Xi meeting in Delhi
Canadian tenant posts ‘harassment’ videos after clash with Indian landlady over barbecue, claims she was arrested by Surrey Police
A 27-year-old Tennessee diesel mechanic wanted to farm full-time; solar sites gave his sheep...
stories.summary: Solar grazing offers new opportunities for small livestock farmers across the American South. This practice uses sheep to manage vegetation beneath solar panels, benefiting both farmers and solar companies. Farmers gain access to pasture and income, while companies reduce maintenance costs and equipment damage risks. A Tennessee mechanic became a full-time farmer after securing grazing access to over 400 acres.

stories.title: 'We will never, ever forget': Trump commemorates 25th anniversary of 9/11 terrorist attacks
stories.summary: On the anniversary of 9/11, leaders across the United States honored the victims and reflected on the impact of the tragedy on current foreign policy. Speaking at the Pentagon, President Trump paid homage to the fallen and reaffirmed the nation’s determination, particularly in its dealings with Iran. Defense Secretary Hegseth reinforced this message, relating the historical attacks to the ongoing war on terror.

stories.title: Mamdani attends NYC 9/11 memorial despite calls from victims’ families to stay away
49 days before 9/11, a businessman took Twin Towers' lease; 25 years later, the rebuilding nears end
stories.summary: The final commercial office tower at the World Trade Center site is actively being built as the new global headquarters for American Express. This project has emerged after extensive planning and has navigated numerous hurdles. It acts as a tribute to the lives lost and rekindles commercial activity in Lower Manhattan, representing a crucial milestone in the comprehensive post-9/11 redevelopment plan.

stories.title: Thames Valley Police uncover £1.3m cannabis farm in abandoned BHS store in Slough with 1,700 plants
stories.summary: Thames Valley Police uncovered a £1.3 million cannabis factory inside a disused BHS store in Slough, finding more than 1,700 plants across two floors. The crop had a potential yield of 150.27kg and an estimated street value of £1.288 million. Two men pleaded guilty and were sentenced to 14 months in prison.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘deepest, darkest China’ gets a Brics sequel with Iran's cameo as India walks tightrope
Shashi Tharoor answers Chidambaram’s questions on Brics benefits for India; BJP takes digs
stories.summary: Shashi Tharoor defended India's BRICS summit prestige in contrast to Chidambaram's questions on its tangible benefits. The BJP criticized Chidambaram's remarks and highlighted Tharoor's differing viewpoint. Tharoor stated hosting leaders shows diplomatic convening power and value. He also noted BRICS represents a majority of the world's population. Tharoor's independent views often create internal Congress party discussions.

stories.title: California officers found 194 abandoned Dungeness crab traps off two rivers; violations wasted...
stories.summary: Two fishermen faced license suspensions and permit revocations for four years. Wildlife officers recovered 194 abandoned Dungeness crab traps off the coast. These traps caused significant waste and entanglement risks for marine wildlife. Investigations revealed serious violations including untagged gear and missed servicing requirements. This action highlights the ongoing problem of ghost fishing and its environmental impact.

stories.title: Australian SPF50+ sunscreen tests as low as SPF 4; formula maker faces multimillion-dollar lawsuits
stories.summary: An Australian sunscreen manufacturer is facing multimillion-dollar legal claims after 20 products using its base formula were recalled for failing to meet SPF claims. Ultra Violette is seeking millions after tests of its SPF50+ sunscreen returned results as low as SPF 2.9 and 4. Wild Child Laboratories entered liquidation in August.

stories.title: PM Modi presses Putin on Ukraine peace, raises safety of seafarers in Black Sea
‘Like calling 2.6% GDP growth 7.8%': AAP targets Centre over ‘hiding’ Delhi slums ahead of Brics
'Trade barriers rising globally, India building bridges': PM Modi at Brics business forum
stories.summary: "Today, while trade barriers are rising globally, India is building economic bridges. Since 2014, we have entered into free trade agreements with nearly 40 countries," PM Modi said.

stories.title: Murders planned before: Indian-origin California woman Anila Baby, charged with killing two of her best friends in separate attacks, appears in court
Builders hauled 25-ton stones 11 miles to create the ‘Devil’s Arrows’
stories.summary: Recent studies indicate that the Neolithic builders of the Devil's Arrows transported massive 25-tonne stones from Brimham Rocks, located 18 kilometers away, rather than using nearby glacial deposits. This geological research has resolved a persistent mystery regarding the stones' lineage. Additionally, a previously unaccounted for stone has been traced to a medieval cross found in Aldborough village, reinforcing local folklore about their historical significance.

stories.title: Two days after Norway King Harald's funeral, his sister princess Astrid passes away
stories.summary: Princess Astrid of Norway has sadly passed away at the age of ninety-four. Just two days before her death, she graced her brother King Harald V's state funeral, attended by many who honored the late monarch. King Harald V's passing marked a significant moment in Norwegian history, concluding the period of national mourning. This event was also Astrid's final farewell in a public capacity.

stories.title: 25 years after 9/11, the WTC's final office tower is rising; it's a 55-story, 1,226-foot building
stories.summary: Construction has officially begun on the last commercial office tower at the World Trade Center site. This impressive 55-story structure will be the new global headquarters for American Express. Spanning nearly two million square feet, it’s projected to be fully operational by 2031, contributing billions to the economy and creating thousands of new jobs. This marks a pivotal milestone in the site's redevelopment after 25 years.

stories.title: 13-year-old coder’s water campaign reaches 1 million people, saves 20 million gallons
Delhi 2047: The big plan, the bigger question
Scientists fitted GPS collars to 17 lions and 14 hyenas expecting hyenas to follow lions
stories.summary: A groundbreaking study suggests that it's the male lions that approach spotted hyenas, contrary to the belief that hyenas seek out lion remains for food. In fact, spotted hyenas are known to back away from lions, prioritizing their safety. This finding highlights the importance of spatial avoidance in hyena behavior, emphasizing their adaptive strategies to circumvent confrontations with such powerful hunters.

stories.title: H-1B is officially dead, nobody will take the risk: Indian career coach says DHS proposal language on ending 60-day grace period is brutal
What happened to Doja Cat? Twitch livestream leaves fans deeply concerned
stories.summary: Doja Cat's latest Twitch livestream has left fans worried due to her lack of clarity and focus. The rapper shared feelings of exhaustion regarding her music career and interactions with fans, which raised eyebrows following her earlier admissions about battling alcohol and marijuana issues. However, she later took to social media to reassure her supporters that she was, in fact, doing well.

stories.title: Instead of managing billions, Warren Buffett’s son Howard Buffett chose farming
stories.summary: Choosing a path less traveled, Howard Buffett, the son of Warren Buffett, dedicated his life to farming and conservation rather than finance. He skillfully managed farms in Nebraska and Illinois, prioritizing soil health. Warren Buffett supported his passion by purchasing a Nebraska farm for his son. As he transitions to the role of non-executive chairman at Berkshire Hathaway, Howard aims to safeguard the company’s culture following his father's legacy.

stories.title: US court rules 150,000 Mississippi residents have no constitutional right to lead-free water
stories.summary: A federal appeals court has determined that the US Constitution does not explicitly provide a right to clean drinking water. Residents of Jackson residents claimed their city was aware of unsafe water conditions but chose to mislead them. Although the court acknowledged the severity of these claims, it denied the establishment of a constitutional right to safe water and pointed to different legal recourses.

stories.title: Uttarakhand to launch month-long ‘Seva Sankalp’ campaign from Sept 17: CM Dhami
No vaccine-autism link, finds WHO review
After husband’s death, she ensured their 215 acres stay protected
stories.summary: Becky Shelton made a conscious decision to prioritize land preservation over lucrative offers from developers. By securing her properties in King George and Stafford with legal protections, she ensures these areas remain untouched for future custodians. Shelton views her role as a temporary steward of the earth, taking action to prevent the encroachment of subdivisions and data centers on the natural landscape.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: PM Modi, Putin & world leaders share stage at BRICS; Delhi man found with uterus, testes & more
A San Francisco house worth $4.4 million changed hands through disputed deeds in little over a year
stories.summary: In a dramatic legal move, San Francisco authorities have initiated a lawsuit to annul eight contentious deeds associated with a luxurious $4.4 million property in the prestigious Sea Cliff area. This case has been characterized by officials as a complex scheme aimed at seizing control of the estate. After over a year of dubious ownership transitions, the city aims to rectify property records and reaffirm the rightful ownership.

stories.title: Indian-origin taxi driver drove New Yorkers for free for 40 days after 9/11
PM Modi reiterates dialogue, diplomacy in talks with Putin; accepts Russia visit invite
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi held crucial talks with Russian President Putin, highlighting dialogue and diplomacy as essential pathways forward. India has offered its aid in peace initiatives to mitigate the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The leaders examined their cooperative efforts across trade, energy, defence, and space sectors, alongside deliberating on pressing regional and global matters of shared concern.

stories.title: In 2002, San Antonio gave an Air Force base for redevelopment; 24 years later, it is expanding
stories.summary: San Antonio’s Brooks Development Authority is expanding beyond the former 1,308-acre Air Force base it has redeveloped since 2002. It will take control of 243 vacant acres along Southton Road and prepare the site with roads and utilities. The move aims to attract major employers and extend development across the city’s Southeast Side.

stories.title: Montana seals 20 hazards at five abandoned uranium sites that once supplied US defence program
stories.summary: Several abandoned uranium mine sites in Montana’s Pryor Mountains have been closed after assessments found physical hazards, radiation and chemical contamination risks. The project addressed 20 mine features across five historic sites, while also protecting bat habitat, rare plants and cultural resources. Officials said continued monitoring will be needed because erosion, gravity and vandalism can affect mine closures over time.

stories.title: From 2017-19, Japan recycled 6.21M phones into 5,000 Tokyo Olympic and Paralympic medals
stories.summary: Japan embarked on a groundbreaking initiative ahead of the 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games, gathering millions of used electronics and phones. This effort resulted in the extraction of significant gold, silver, and bronze from these devices by recyclers. The recovered metals were then transformed into the medals awarded at the events, reflecting a nationwide commitment to sustainability and innovative recycling practices involving local municipalities and businesses.

stories.title: JD(U) renaming on cards? Leaders back proposal to name party after Nitish
PM Modi, Putin share car ride again in Delhi, weeks after traveling together in Bishkek - watch
stories.summary: During an informal car ride in Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin rekindled their camaraderie, continuing their tradition of traveling together. This ride marks their fourth time sharing a vehicle, following earlier occasions in Bishkek and Tianjin. Their private talks during the journey underscore the depth of their diplomatic ties and mutual understanding.

stories.title: Building Brics: PM Modi-Putin talks, a Thirukkural gift and Xi's big return - key points
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Russian President Vladimir Putin during the summit. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also arrived for discussions with PM Modi. Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected for bilateral talks and the summit. The expanded Brics grouping focuses on development and cooperation among emerging economies. India hosts the summit under its theme of resilience and innovation.

stories.title: Uber exits Nigeria, Uganda: Why Africa's ride-hailing market is getting tougher
stories.summary: Uber has officially ended its operations in Nigeria and Uganda, marking a significant retreat from these markets. This decision comes as a result of escalating operating expenses and fierce competition, which have negatively impacted ride-hailing fares and driver earnings. Rising costs for fuel and vehicle upkeep weighed heavily on drivers' incomes. Despite this setback, Uber continues to prioritize other sub-Saharan African markets where growth seems promising.

stories.title: In the 1950s, Hugo Meyer bought abandoned Vermont farms; his family has protected 18,000+ acres
stories.summary: In a remarkable effort, the Meyer family has preserved thousands of acres in the Worcester Range of Vermont, committing to a sustainable approach to timber management. This conservation initiative plays a vital role in protecting significant wildlife corridors and northern hardwood ecosystems, with part of the funding sourced from the U.S. Forest Service's Forest Legacy Program, paving the way for future generations to enjoy the area's natural beauty.

stories.title: After losing 75% of wetlands, Niagara River uses recycled Christmas trees to restore fish habitat
stories.summary: In an innovative approach, conservation teams are utilizing recycled Christmas trees to rejuvenate the coastal wetlands of Niagara River. This dynamic initiative, launched in 2016, spans over 1.64 kilometers, serving to calm wave action and lower erosion rates. By restoring vital aquatic habitats, the project aims to enhance the ecosystem, leading to a remarkable increase in both fish and shorebird populations alongside improved water quality.

stories.title: Former AT&T worker accused of SIM-swap scheme targeting $600,000 from victims
Punjab sets two-week deadline to distribute 33 lakh Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana cards
stories.summary: Punjab is set to roll out 33 lakh Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana cards imminently. To facilitate this, dedicated camps will be established across 2,008 villages and wards, aiming for complete distribution within a week of launching. ASHA workers and facilitators are incentivized for efficiently delivering the cards, with any remaining ones being distributed door-to-door within two weeks of the camps.

stories.title: Indian man on student visa in US sentenced to 30 months for defrauding Vietnam veteran
Brics summit: PM Modi gifts Putin Russian translation of Thirukkural
stories.summary: During a significant meeting ahead of the BRICS Summit, Prime Minister Modi gifted President Putin a translated version of the ancient Tamil text, Thirukkural, by Naira Mkrtchyan. Both leaders held bilateral talks on the sidelines of the Brics summit being held in New Delhi.

stories.title: ‘Why is government silent?’ Congress targets BJP over US ‘Mr Singh’ ad
stories.summary: In a striking move, the Congress party has chastised the Indian government for its silence on a provocative from the US Department of Homeland Security. Featuring the phrase 'Mr Singh,' the ad was seen as an affront to Indian respect. Advocacy groups chimed in, condemning the message as racial profiling. Following significant backlash, the US Department of Homeland Security ultimately decided to withdraw the contentious .

stories.title: Cong vs Cong: Tharoor rebuffs Chidambaram's view on Brics, hails summit's 'diplomatic convening power'
Scientist finds 10,000-year-old mastodon molar while surveying California creek for threatened frogs
stories.summary: While investigating a creek for frogs, a scientist stumbled upon a remarkable ancient mastodon tooth, estimated to be over ten thousand years old. Paleontologists have confirmed its belonging to a long-extinct species of Pacific mastodon. The fossil will soon be analyzed at Stanford University to determine its precise age, establishing a fascinating connection between today's conservation initiatives and the ancient ecosystems of California.

stories.title: Hawaii’s 124-year-old red mangroves now threaten native waterbirds and waterways
NPCI Bharat Bill Pay proposes new infra to fix MSME's collection problems
stories.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) Bharat BillPay has introduced a pioneering digital platform that links invoices directly to payments. This innovative framework is designed to alleviate the credit bottlenecks that many MSMEs encounter. By digitizing the order-to-cash cycle with standardized APIs and automating reconciliation, the system transforms buyer-confirmed invoices into fundable records. This development aims to enhance MSME efficiency and promote growth within the formal sector.

stories.title: Full list of world leaders attending Brics summit in New Delhi
Wigs, makeup let fraudsters pose as NFL players, scoring $20M in fake loans
stories.summary: In a stunning twist, two individuals from Georgia devised a sophisticated scheme to impersonate professional football players for financial gain. They established fake companies and produced counterfeit documentation, even going as far as using disguises during video calls. Altogether, they amassed an astonishing $19.845 million through twelve fraudulent loans from various lenders before their plot was uncovered by a players' union that detected bogus contracts.

stories.title: Algorithms should be able to explain reasoning behind decisions to customers: RBI Murmu
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India mandates that lenders provide explanations for credit application rejections, emphasizing the need for transparent algorithms. This move ensures equitable access to financial resources. Moreover, institutions are urged to safeguard against potential threats posed by quantum computing. Rather than diminishing lender accountability, technology must amplify credit accessibility and empower customer choice, while regulated entities remain liable for all services offered under their banner.

stories.title: Malaysian students built a device that turns sink wastewater into electricity
FCRA Amendment Bill: JPC to begin scrutiny on September 18, Sanjay Jaiswal to chair panel
More than 1,000 volunteers built a four-bedroom house in 50 hours, launching 35-home community
stories.summary: Over one thousand volunteers constructed a four-bedroom house in just fifty hours. This remarkable effort provided a new home for single mother Yadira Salas and her children. Volunteers worked in shifts, contributing their labor and skills to the rapid construction. Salas also actively participated, investing her own "sweat equity" into the build. This accelerated project exemplifies Habitat for Humanity's commitment to affordable homeownership.

stories.title: Alliance Air plane makes emergency landing in Delhi after engine failure
Dating to 1898, Nipomo's oldest church donated after 128 years to become a community hub
stories.summary: A historic church in Nipomo, California, dating to 1898, has been donated to the Dana Adobe and Cultural Center by its owners, John and Rebecca Prewett. The building will be developed into a museum, event venue and “Visit Nipomo” centre, while Calvary Church will continue holding Sunday services there.

stories.title: Belize Reef Restoration Effort: Lisa Carne revives storm-hit corals; project outplants 100,000 fragments
stories.summary: In 2001, Hurricane Iris wreaked havoc on Belize's coral reefs, sparking an innovative restoration effort. Marine biologist Lisa Carne took the lead in replanting coral fragments, which were often neglected. Through her organization, Fragments of Hope, more than 100,000 corals have been successfully restored, resulting in a remarkable boost in coral coverage and marine biodiversity.

stories.title: Las Vegas developers buy 940 acres of former federal desert for $94 million; 6,000-home community planned
stories.summary: A large federal desert parcel near Las Vegas will become Monument Hills, a new master-planned community. This development will feature up to 6,000 homes and various amenities for residents. The $94 million land deal is the largest BLM transaction in the valley for decades. Proceeds from the sale will fund projects across Nevada, including parks and education. First homes are anticipated to be available around spring 2028.

stories.title: PM Modi pays tribute to 9/11 victims, calls for firm stand against terror
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to the victims of the 9/11 attacks, reiterating India’s strong stance against terrorism in all its forms. Recognizing India's own experiences with cross-border terrorism, he emphasized the nation’s leadership in the global fight against this menace. Reflecting on his visit to the 9/11 Memorial in 2014, he extended solidarity with international efforts to eradicate this global threat.

stories.title: Indonesia seeks to repatriate five baby orangutans found in Odisha; trafficking network suspected
Actor Max Thieriot bought a 90-acre ranch in 2013; his Sonoma Hollywood retreat is now a vineyard
stories.summary: Max Thieriot’s roughly 90-acre Sonoma County ranch has evolved since he and his wife Lexi bought it in 2013. The property now includes the nine-acre Bodega Thieriot Pinot noir vineyard, while the rest remains hillside, woodland and pasture. Though the actor’s family now lives in Washington state for most of the year, he continues returning to the ranch during the off-season.

stories.title: Snake grows a fake spider on its tail to lure birds; scans reveal surprisingly normal bones inside
stories.summary: Researchers utilized XCT scanning technology to investigate the unique tail of a viper. The imaging uncovered the presence of standard viper vertebrae within the tail's unusual form. This finding underscores the discrepancies that can exist between external appearance and internal skeletal makeup. Fossilized remains alone may not capture the true look of an organism, while museum specimens remain crucial for advancing our understanding through innovative methods.

stories.title: Suvendu Adhikari eats fish bhog at Kalighat amid Bageshwar Baba row: What sparked the controversy
Putin, Xi and a bigger Brics: India becomes the stage for high-stakes global diplomacy test
stories.summary: New Delhi hosts the significant BRICS Summit, bringing together powerful global leaders. The expanded bloc now represents nearly half the world's population. India prioritizes practical cooperation in areas like food and energy security. The summit faces challenges from global disruptions and geopolitical rivalries. Leaders aim to achieve meaningful outcomes and strengthen collective influence.

stories.title: Scotland’s first wind farm recycled 99.9% of 26 turbines, blades became polymers
Steven Spielberg bought an LA horse ranch for $5.75M; 27 years later, he is selling it for $29.9M
stories.summary: Steven Spielberg and his wife are selling their stunning Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million, a significant increase from the $5.75 million they invested in 1999. This gorgeous property features premium equestrian facilities and lavish living quarters. Earlier dreams of a five-story riding stable were scrapped, but the ranch has been a vital component of their real estate holdings for almost three decades.

stories.title: South China Sea methane leak formed a 1km plume; worms and bacteria built a ‘worm bed’ in 2 years
stories.summary: A South China Sea drilling incident caused a significant methane leak in 2018. Ocean scientists observed an ecosystem rapidly responding to the underwater gas release. Bacteria and worms quickly formed a methane-munching 'worm bed' within two years. This new biofilter degraded methane effectively, reducing plume height significantly. However, this rapid ecosystem development caused a notable decrease in original microbial diversity.

stories.title: Man lost his ring in 1973; 53 years later, fate brings it back
stories.summary: In 1973, a Kansas student misplaced his class ring during an epic snowball fight. Fast forward fifty-three years later, campus workers discovered the ring while tending to the grounds. Interestingly, the owner and his wife were driving through the city that same day, having just discussed the ring a week earlier. Now, the couple will restore and treasure the sentimental piece.

stories.title: Miami flight overrun: Plane touched down at nearly 300 kmph despite high-speed warning
stories.summary: A 21 Air Boeing 767 touched down at Miami International Airport at an alarming speed of nearly 300 kmph. As the crew attempted to execute a go-around following the landing, they had neglected to deploy the speed brakes, leading to automated alerts about the steep descent and proximity to the ground. Investigators are now analyzing the flight data and cockpit voice recordings to uncover further insights regarding this incident.

stories.title: 1,700 passengers boarded an Alaska cruise, only for Royal Caribbean to cancel it two days later
stories.summary: Royal Caribbean cancelled an Alaska cruise after around 1,700 passengers had already boarded the ship in Vancouver. The seven-night sailing was delayed because of an unspecified technical issue and was later cancelled after passengers spent two days waiting on board. Guests were offered refunds, future cruise credit and help with travel changes.

stories.title: $250M crypto fraud allegedly funded six homes, Lamborghinis and dozens of Louis Vuitton bags
stories.summary: Christopher Alexander Delgado admitted to a $250 million crypto fraud scheme. His company, Goliath Ventures, promised investor returns from liquidity pools. Instead, funds paid earlier investors and funded a lavish personal lifestyle. Delgado purchased numerous luxury properties, vehicles, and designer accessories. He now faces significant prison time and asset forfeiture for his actions.

stories.title: After Trump renamed Lake Ontario, Pennsylvania Republican seeks ‘Lake Pennsylvania’ for Erie
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” on US maps, documents and databases. Canada has rejected the move, while several US governors have also said they will continue calling it Lake Ontario. The decision comes amid rising trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa.

stories.title: Netherlands' 9km flood barrier triggered "sand hunger," shrinking tidal flats
After 9/11, Gander sheltered 7,000 Americans as 38 planes landed after attack
In 1982, Israel released 28 wild donkeys; 44 years later, they created a desert oasis
stories.summary: In an effort to rejuvenate the parched landscape of Israel's Ramon Crater, wild donkeys were brought back into the ecosystem. These resilient animals played a crucial role by creating waterholes, which became essential for desert wildlife. Additionally, their droppings helped spread acacia seeds, promoting the growth of trees. Their natural movements resulted in water-retaining depressions, significantly transforming the area's ecology into a thriving environment that has caught global attention.

stories.title: Vermont town opens 1976 time capsule with a joint and birth-control packaging
JD Vance defends Usha's heritage, hits out at Michigan Senate candidate El-Syed
'Plotting a super-tainted majority': Congress taunts Centre over delay in Parliament prorogation
'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
stories.summary: As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees. Leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the MEA.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary
stories.summary: "On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the revered people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to the memories of Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant ji on the occasion of his auspicious birth anniversary, and offer my humble tributes," Yogi said.

stories.title: "Legacy of our ancestors...": CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails Rudrapur's transformative growth at Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday lauded the pioneering legacy and transformative contributions of the ancestors and various communities in turning Rudrapur into a vibrant industrial hub and the granary of the nation.

stories.title: BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami interact with youth in Haldwani
Discarded mine pipes become shelters for threatened northern quolls in Australia
Satya Niketan puts safety, housing at heart of DUSU battle
ED raids Ramnandi Hotels in alleged Rs 132-crore bank fraud case; 9 locations searched

Ramnandi Hotels and Resorts Ltd is accused of diverting Rs 58 crore from bank loans. The company allegedly used fake reports and personal guarantees to secure these funds. Five pledged properties were reportedly sold at undervalued prices recently. The agency suspects these actions aimed to prevent asset attachment and recover crime proceeds.

xQc Explains NoPixel Absences: Co-owner says some GTA RP stars self-excluded; others moved on

The NoPixel co-owner said some players chose to leave the server and build their own community, while others had previously criticized NoPixel. xQc argued that Summit could return if he wanted, but claimed he is staying away because his friends were not invited. NoPixel 5.0 launched on September 8.

After countless hours searching for rare seahorses in French Polynesia, a photographer captured...
stories.summary: French photographer Julien Anton won the top prize at the Ocean Photographer of the Year 2026 awards. His winning image captured a male seahorse with two newborn juveniles in French Polynesia. Anton spent many hours searching for the rare seahorse family in Mo'orea. The photograph also won the Wildlife category before receiving the grand prize. Other international photographers also received awards across various competition categories.

Teen Uses Cancer Game: Daniel Zhang turns Tumor Tactics into learning tool; reaches 1,500 K-8 students
stories.summary: In an innovative step, a San Diego teenager named Daniel Zhang crafted Tumor Tactics, an educational game designed to demystify cancer for young minds. Motivated by his grandmother's battle with the illness, Daniel aims to make intricate cancer biology accessible to children. His project has garnered funding and will be showcased at the United Nations Science Summit, alongside his role in STEAMLabs International, where he promotes STEM and arts education.

San Francisco’s Candlestick Point breaks ground; $130M phase to pave way for 7,200 homes across 270 acres
stories.summary: San Francisco’s long-delayed Candlestick Point redevelopment is finally moving forward nearly a decade after Candlestick Park was demolished. The $130 million first phase will fund roads, utilities and other infrastructure across the 270-acre site, paving the way for a massive mixed-use neighborhood featuring up to 7,200 homes, retail, offices, parks and community spaces.

Princess Diana’s 'revenge dress' up for auction at Rs 2.8 crore

Meet Mateo, 11, guitarist who stunned Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis
stories.summary: At just eleven years old, Mateo Castillo-Bonde has already made a significant impact, mesmerizing audiences with his guitar skills. His stunning solo at the State Fair, where he shared the stage with iconic producers Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, showcased his remarkable talent. After only three years of dedicated practice, sparked by a museum visit, Mateo continues to encourage others to explore their creative passions.

Brics Summit 2026: Putin to land in Delhi in few hours; Xi arriving Saturday - top developments
stories.summary: The 18th BRICS Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together world leaders, including Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. With a focus on pivotal discussions surrounding economic cooperation, technology, energy, and global governance, the summit will address pressing issues such as food and energy security, alongside current global trade tensions. This gathering aims to strengthen resilience, innovation, and sustainable collaboration among member nations.

stories.title: Brics turns 25: How a Goldman Sachs acronym became a global power bloc
stories.summary: This September, New Delhi will play host to the 18th Brics Summit. With eleven member nations and ten partner countries added to its roster, Brics has matured from an economic idea born twenty-five years ago into a vital platform for the Global South. Discussions at the summit will focus on economic collaboration, technological advancements, and essential global governance challenges.

stories.title: TN minister reiterates Rahul Gandhi for PM pitch; rules out Vijay as contender
IndiGo Lucknow-Dammam flight makes emergency landing in Ahmedabad after hoax bomb threat
Britain brought back wild bison after 6,000 years; their grazing could create new habitats
stories.summary: The historic return of wild bison to Britain, absent for 6,000 years, is made possible by the Blean Bison Project. This initiative not only aims to reinstate these creatures but also to rejuvenate the woodland ecosystem they inhabit. Through their natural grazing and movements, they are instrumental in creating diverse habitats that support biodiversity.

stories.title: The US had just two 500-foot smokestacks in 1970 and more than 180 by 1985 to dilute pollution
stories.summary: In an effort to mitigate local air pollution, American power companies constructed towering smokestacks, effectively releasing sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides into higher winds. Unfortunately, this practice contributed to acid rain, harming ecosystems throughout North America. In response, Congress revised the Clean Air Act to restrict the use of tall stacks and improve emission control by emphasizing source capture instead.

stories.title: New Jersey built a massive seawall to protect a highway and beach houses from erosion
stories.summary: In New Jersey, the construction of a seawall has safeguarded properties but has inadvertently resulted in the disappearance of the sandy shoreline. The energy from waves is redirected downwards, which has stripped away sand and left no beach visible even during low tide. This hard engineering tactic disrupts the natural flow of sand and hinders the migration of barrier islands.

stories.title: Gwyneth Paltrow turned $4.9 million Montecito property into 14,000-sq-ft estate
stories.summary: Gwyneth Paltrow bought about 2.4 acres in Montecito for $4.9 million in 2016, razed the existing structures and embarked on a ground-up project that took about six years. The result was a roughly 14,000-square-foot home powered by solar energy and equipped with a graywater system.

stories.title: New York investigator accused of tracking ex-girlfriend 3,000 times using Flock cameras; suspended after 4,000 searches
The US built nearly 2,000 km of Mississippi River levees; helping erase 4,900 sq km of coastal land
stories.summary: The construction of levees along the Mississippi River has led to significant coastal land erosion in Louisiana by obstructing critical river sediment from reaching coastal estuaries. In an effort to combat this issue, environmental agencies are now reintroducing river mud into the affected bayous. This initiative is focused on rejuvenating the coastline and revitalizing marshland ecosystems, serving as a potential blueprint for delta restoration throughout southern Louisiana.

stories.title: Can Iran hurt Trump at ballot box? Tehran’s new war strategy explained
Golden Gate University sells SF campus for $31.6 million; a 46-storey tower is proposed in its place
stories.summary: Golden Gate University has sold its longtime downtown San Francisco campus for $31.6 million after more than 170 years in the city. The seven-storey property could be demolished to make way for a proposed 46-storey tower, with developers considering either a 700-foot office building or a mixed-use project with offices and homes.

stories.title: Washington spends $113M to rebuild I-395 Potomac River Bridge
Gujarat man pleads guilty in US in $9.36 million illegal gambling case
Ladakh groups express disappointment over MHA meet; Wangchuk warns of fresh stir from Sept 19
"I gotta be the first": IShowSpeed makes history with iPhone Duo stunt at Apple event
stories.summary: During Apple's highly anticipated product launch event, streamer IShowSpeed shocked the audience by executing a daring backflip while clutching the new iPhone Duo. This groundbreaking stunt made him the very first person to try such a feat with the foldable smartphone. Miraculously, he nailed the move and kept the expensive device safe, leading to a viral sensation that captured the tech community's imagination.

stories.title: ‘My grandpa’s name was Dan Singh’: Fox anchor Alec Nolan hits back at DHS post targeting ‘Mr Singh’
A Pennsylvania family bought a 12-acre farm in 1916; 110 years and four generations later...
stories.summary: Maple Acres Farm remains Plymouth Township's last working farm, a testament to agricultural heritage. The McKeown family has preserved thirty acres of land since nineteen sixteen. This farm now serves as a community market and pick-your-own destination. It thrives by adapting its business model to suburban surroundings. Community support and family dedication ensure its continued operation.

stories.title: Evening Newswrap: Red Fort bomber’s original target revealed; Xi Jinping to visit India for Brics summit, and more
stories.summary: Umar-un-Nabi, known for the Red Fort bombing, originally aimed at Lal Mandir but redirected due to traffic and police constraints. Notably, Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to visit India next month for the upcoming Brics summit. Meanwhile, Karnataka has instituted a mandate for the singing of Vande Mataram during state government events. Trump's strategies regarding voter ID and dividends resonate with India's election approaches.

stories.title: 'Can't browbeat child': SC on CJP protester's intimidation complaint against 'influencer'
Tax startup CEO allegedly faked CPA credentials and company revenue to raise $13.3 million
stories.summary: Federal agents arrested a former startup executive in Florida just as she was set to board a cruise ship. She is accused of swindling over $13 million from venture capital funds by falsely portraying herself as a licensed CPA while fabricating revenue reports. It is alleged that the funds were misappropriated for personal luxuries, including an extravagant wedding, leaving investors with substantial financial setbacks after her company's abrupt downfall.

stories.title: No 'Nitishpur'? JD(U) sidesteps NDA partner's proposal to rename Nitish Kumar's birthplace
stories.summary: Rejecting a proposal to rename Bakhtiyarpur, Nitish Kumar's birthplace, the JD(U) underscored its leader’s preference for action over name changes. They asserted that the town’s historical essence remains intact, regardless of its name. Meanwhile, the idea was met with mockery from the RJD, illustrating the ongoing political debate surrounding historical perceptions and the lasting impact of influential figures in society.

stories.title: Newport mansion revives 1500s staircase craft with mortise-and-wedge joinery
A Taylor Swift fan helped describe 12 new insect species; 4 species named after her music and life
stories.summary: A new genus of Australian insects has been named Swiftiephylus after singer Taylor Swift. Four new species within this genus also bear names inspired by her music. These pale yellow and cream-colored insects were collected between 1995 and 2004. Their discovery highlights the vast undocumented insect diversity remaining globally. This naming brings attention to insect conservation and scientific discovery.

stories.title: Why did armed people come looking for Destiny's son? Kick streamer recalls frightening incident
stories.summary: Kick streamer Destiny recounted terrifying experiences involving armed individuals near his home. He vividly described an alarming encounter where people brandished rifles and interrogated him about his son. Moreover, Destiny shared the ordeal of being swatted, leading to police unexpectedly storming his residence. These chilling incidents have profoundly shaped his view on online threats and harassment, affecting his family members as well, including his son and mother.

stories.title: 'You are correct, my jaw did break': Stalin breaks silence on Vijay's assembly gesture
How BJP, Congress turned 80s AI trend turned into an all-out meme war
stories.summary: A new social media phenomenon has politicians reimagining their current images as vibrant 1980s portraits using AI technology. This trend has quickly morphed into a creative form of political satire, with the BJP and Congress leveraging it to exchange jabs. Leaders like Piyush Goyal and Kiren Rijiju are riding the retro wave, and even Rahul Gandhi has joined the fray with quirky AI-generated images.

States, municipalities to drive next phase of India deregulation: Niti Aayog member Gauba
Two beavers were unexpectedly released in Cornwall; they have built a dam six months later
stories.summary: Two beavers have unexpectedly settled at Helman Tor nature reserve. Their dam building and feeding activities are creating a more varied habitat. The new pools and altered water flow are attracting other wildlife species. Cornwall Wildlife Trust is monitoring the pair while planning wider reintroductions. This unexpected arrival supports the trust's long-term conservation goals.

‘Hoping draft ready by Oct’: Ladakh chief secy as UT seeks Article 371 safeguards
Giant reed came to California in the 1820s; now it crowds out native plants and fuels wildfires
stories.summary: Giant reed, a plant native to eastern Asia, was introduced to California in the 1820s for roofing material and erosion control. It has since become an invasive weed, growing rapidly and forming dense stands that displace native plants. In Southern California’s Santa Ana River Basin, arundo infestations have almost tripled fire fuel loads and also increased pressure on water resources.

stories.title: Space-based surveillance: Dhruva to get key systems worth €5m from Safran
Elk Herd Roaming Farther: Reintroduced West Virginia animals test new range; tourism tours expand
stories.summary: West Virginia's elk restoration initiative is flourishing, with the herd expanding to around 130 individuals alongside numerous native calves. Elk are venturing into new territories, showcasing a robust population increase. This revival not only highlights the animals' successful reintroduction into their habitat but also boosts local tourism, marking a remarkable triumph in wildlife conservation.

stories.title: ‘He has no business being in our country’: Indian-origin man charged in crash that killed US woman
BSP's family drama: Why no 'Anand' for Mayawati ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections?
stories.summary: Amid political turmoil, Akash Anand has again been demoted by Mayawati, who has questioned her nephew's maturity. His X profile has devolved from National Convenor to Party Worker and now to Supporter. His younger sibling, Ishan Anand, has been brought to the centre stage. Mayawati freed Akash political prospects to his father-in-law's exit from the scene, as the BSP confronts a challenging landscape with dwindling votes and approaching UP elections.

In 1974, Australian ranger proposed wildlife bridge; 52 years later, it opened over motorway
stories.summary: An innovative wildlife crossing, born from an Australian park ranger's fifty-two-year-old vision, has finally been realized. Cawleys Bridge has been modified to facilitate safe passage for important wildlife across a bustling motorway. This enhancement allows species like koalas to navigate between vital habitats such as Heathcote National Park and Garrawarra State Conservation Area. Future wildlife monitoring will assess usage patterns and guide subsequent conservation projects.

stories.title: IRCTC scam case: Delhi court orders framing of charges against Lalu, Rabri Devi and Tejashwi
stories.summary: A Delhi court has formally charged Lalu Prasad Yadav and several associates in connection with the alleged money laundering linked to IRCTC hotels. Rabri Devi and Tejashwi Yadav are implicated as well, facing accusations of conspiracy and cheating. The court indicated substantial evidence of tampering with the tender process, paving the way for the case to advance to trial following the charge framing.

SC seeks UP govt response on plea challenging MLAs, MLCs’ pension, perks
Abandoned Idaho bridge gets a second life as wildlife crossing
stories.summary: An abandoned bridge over Interstate 90 in Osburn, Idaho, was repurposed as a wildlife crossing. This initiative was championed by a local truck driver who witnessed numerous animal collisions. Conservation groups and state officials collaborated to transform the unused structure into a safe passage. Trail cameras confirmed deer regularly using the bridge, avoiding the dangerous interstate. The bridge, though temporary, successfully provided a vital crossing for animals.

stories.title: China confirms Xi Jinping's India visit for Brics summit on September 12-13, first trip in 7 years

In 1883, Hawaii introduced Guinea grass; 143 years later, it grows 9 feet and yields 9,000 seeds
stories.summary: Once celebrated for its grazing benefits, Guinea grass has become a formidable threat to Hawaii's delicate ecosystems. Since its introduction in the 19th century, it has proliferated, reaching impressive heights. This resilient perennial can generate thousands of seeds and rebound swiftly from fires, exacerbating wildfire risks by providing ample fuel across the islands. Its growth pattern serves as a stark reminder of the lasting ecological impact of imported plant species.

stories.title: FIR registered against Azam Khan, four others over Hajj land irregularities
Quote of the day by Osho: "The real question is not whether life exists after death. The real question is…"
Georgia's 1950s farm pond gets $3.1 million makeover after decades of leaks and sediment
stories.summary: Roswell Area Park in Georgia has reopened its 1950s farm pond after a $3.1 million restoration. The project rebuilt the embankment, upgraded stormwater infrastructure, removed decades of sediment, restored the walking trail and added 35 trees and turtle habitat. The pond manages runoff from a 52-acre drainage area.

stories.title: North Carolina peatland emits 130,000 tons of CO₂ yearly after 50 miles of ditches were cut
stories.summary: In a significant ecological effort, North Carolina is working to restore its ancient peatlands that suffered damage from farming practices impacting their carbon storage capabilities. The previous drainage systems caused water levels to drop, resulting in peat exposure to air and increased emissions. Restoration efforts include blocking these ditches to enhance land rehydration and restore the water table.

stories.title: Suvendu Adhikari's 'strict medicine' warning to 'anti-national' sympathisers at Jadavpur university
stories.summary: Speaking in the state assembly, Adhikari said the government would respond in the language of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose rather than Mahatma Gandhi if slogans demanding freedom for Kashmir were raised on the university campus. He also said Jadavpur University would receive Rs 1,300 crore in grants, but warned that those raising slogans such as "Bharat tere tukde honge" would be dealt with firmly.

stories.title: 500 CCTV cameras, 15000 personnel: How Delhi is turning fortress for Brics Summit
stories.summary: As the Brics summit approaches in Delhi from September 12-13, the city undergoes comprehensive preparations. An intricate security plan unfolds, with over 500 advanced CCTV cameras, including those capable of number plate recognition, set for enhanced surveillance. Authorities have established layered security protocols to facilitate the seamless movement of delegates, while Delhi Police are urged to exhibit discipline and professionalism throughout the event.

stories.title: Hong Kong cattle DNA reveals how livestock adapted to island life
Satya Niketan building collapse: SC asks Delhi HC to continue monitoring case as 'things start moving'
Visa moving from periodic checks to continuous AI driven deference as cyber threats increase
stories.summary: Visa is revolutionizing its cybersecurity strategies by implementing AI-driven continuous defense against rapidly changing threats. This proactive approach emphasizes ongoing detection and remediation rather than static periodic checks. The company has rigorously tested these advanced systems against vital infrastructure, responding to the surge in cyber fraud in India. By innovating in this manner, Visa seeks to preserve trust within the fast-evolving digital payments landscape.

stories.title: Baltimore replaces invasive pear with tulip poplar as official tree after 52 years
stories.summary: Baltimore has replaced the Chanticleer pear, its official tree since 1974, with the native tulip poplar after Maryland banned sales of the invasive callery pear. Six native species competed for the title, with residents voting before the winner was announced through a costumed tree race at Cylburn Arboretum attended by hundreds.

stories.title: Missouri volunteers place 93 cedar brush piles in Truman Lake; $75,000 grant backs 450 structures
stories.summary: Truman Lake in Missouri is undergoing remarkable enhancements for its underwater habitat. Recently, 93 cedar brush piles have been established to provide refuge and food for fish. The goal is to install a total of 450 habitat structures throughout the reservoir, backed by a $75,000 grant aimed at improving fishing experiences. Various organizations and community volunteers are joining forces for this multi-year initiative.

stories.title: Salboni land scam case: Bengal CID detains Abhishek Banerjee's PA
stories.summary: On Thursday, the Bengal CID apprehended Sumit Roy, the personal assistant to TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee. This move came after the Supreme Court denied Roy's anticipatory bail request, which also lifted the previous protection against his arrest linked to the Salboni land scam case. His bail plea had been rejected by the Calcutta High Court due to ongoing investigations into alleged government land transactions and irregularities in TMC account deposits.

stories.title: Centre tells SC it is open to tougher labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt or fat
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had recently proposed introducing the labelling system in two phases. Under the initial plan, a product would get a red warning symbol if it crossed the prescribed limits in at least two of three categories, namely added sugar, salt or saturated fat. Tighter provisions were to follow in the second phase.

stories.title: Lake Havasu’s 1992 partnership has restored fish habitat across 124 coves
In 2017, USGS released 72.57 kg of dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River; aircraft tracked it from above
stories.summary: In 2017, the US Geological Survey released 72.57 kg of Rhodamine WT dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River over 90 seconds to study how a tracer moves through flowing water. Researchers tracked the dye using instruments in the river and hyperspectral images captured from an aircraft flying 1,000 metres above the ground, with images recorded in 0.5-metre pixels across 48 spectral bands.

stories.title: 'They would kick us': Stalin takes on Vijay over 'jaw gesture', recalls Emergency-era prison days
Gateshead uses 150m-deep mine water to heat 350 homes and public buildings
stories.summary: Water from deep beneath Gateshead now heats hundreds of homes and buildings. A six-megawatt heat pump extracts warmth from mine water, feeding a district network. This system, the largest of its kind in Great Britain, became operational in March 2023. Over five kilometers of pipes distribute the heated water to various public and private properties. Researchers are studying the mine water system through the Gateshead Living Laboratory.

stories.title: TVK fields turncoats Maragatham, Sathyabama for Mathurantagam, Dharapuram bypolls
Before 9/11, families could walk to airport gates; TSA now brings it back at 13 US airports
stories.summary: A new TSA pilot programme is allowing eligible TSA PreCheck members to enter airport gate areas without buying a flight ticket. The Gateside by TSA PreCheck programme is being tested at 13 US airports, including Mesa Gateway Airport in Arizona. Visitors must get a single-day pass and complete the same security screening as ticketed travellers.

stories.title: 30 Kansas inmates donate $4,267 from their own funds to pay down local children's lunch debt
SC rejects 1993 blast accused Abu Salem's plea for early release from life term
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has dismissed gangster Abu Salem's request for early release, despite him having served twenty-five years of his sentence. This plea comes after his extradition from Portugal in November 2005. The court reaffirmed a decision by the Bombay High Court, determining that his request was premature. Abu Salem is currently incarcerated for his involvement in the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts.

stories.title: Scientists discover apple waste can remove up to 100% of lead from water
stories.summary: Researchers explored apple pomace for removing lead ions from contaminated water. Both raw and processed apple waste effectively removed lead from the solution. Extracted apple waste achieved complete lead removal under optimal experimental conditions. The biosorbents demonstrated rapid lead adsorption within the first hour of testing. These findings highlight apple pomace's potential for environmental remediation applications.

stories.title: Self-Taught Freestyler Shines: Welsh teen racks up five Guinness World Records; YouTube drives rise
stories.summary: At just fourteen years old, James Taylor from Penarth has made an impressive mark in the world of freestyle football, clinching the third spot at the world championships. With remarkable ball control skills, he holds five Guinness World Records. His dedication is evident in his daily practice and online training through YouTube, including his latest feat of completing numerous 'around-the-world' tricks in under a minute.

stories.title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
stories.summary: The alliance between the NC and Congress is witnessing persistent tensions regarding political leadership. Recent arguments over the Vande Mataram reveal significant ideological rifts. Echoes of past events, such as the contentious 1987 election, continue to influence NC's political behavior. The long-term success of this coalition hinges on its ability to balance conflicting priorities as they tackle statehood and Article 370 challenges.

stories.title: Australia’s first solar power station, built in 1981, is now heritage listed
stories.summary: Australia's innovative solar power station located at White Cliffs has received heritage listing recognition. Operational since 1981, this remote facility has consistently supplied power to a small community, demonstrating the potential of solar energy in extreme outback climates for more than a decade. Its preservation highlights the journey of renewable energy progress in Australia and serves as a symbol of the nation's aspirations for a sustainable energy future.

stories.title: Army veteran paralysed in crash returns seven years later with a degree
stories.summary: Rocky Fernandez, an Army veteran, faced a turning point when a catastrophic car accident led to paralysis. Grateful for the Houston VA's assistance in education and rehabilitation, he committed to completing a petroleum engineering degree despite ongoing health challenges. After seven grueling years of effort, he triumphantly graduated and is now eager to launch his professional journey in the petroleum engineering industry.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s estranged daughter takes aim at father and AI in a new fashion campaign
stories.summary: Vivian Wilson, daughter of billionaire Elon Musk, leads a provocative fashion campaign that takes aim at artificial intelligence. The new humorously highlights the limitations of robots in understanding human emotions. This initiative is particularly significant given her complicated relationship with Musk. Wilson raises alarms about AI's effects on creative employment and the environment while promoting the beauty of human flaws and critically examining AI's expanding footprint.

stories.title: Britain’s vulnerable sharks to be tracked with 70 tags and catch records since 1953
stories.summary: A new three-year research initiative is set to study three at-risk shark species in British waters. By using electronic tags to monitor their movements and diving behaviors, the team will analyze historical distribution data from anglers spanning decades. This comprehensive approach aims to enhance understanding of shark migration and behavior, ultimately contributing to effective conservation efforts for these essential marine creatures.

stories.title: Plant Diversity Jumps On Rewilded Farm: species on ex-arable plots leap fourfold; survey shows rapid gains
stories.summary: Wild Ken Hill’s groundbreaking rewilding initiative revealed a remarkable surge in plant diversity, with species nearly doubling within just three years. This transformation of former arable land led to a fourfold increase in plant variety, predominantly fueled by grazing animals that enhanced the ecosystem's structure. The surge in vegetation signals promising benefits for local insect and bird populations, showcasing nature's impressive capacity for rejuvenation.

stories.title: Why Trump's flight to Dallas was delayed before republican midterm convention
stories.summary: President Trump's journey to Dallas was abruptly delayed when an emergency slide was deployed from Air Force One. Ground personnel quickly assessed the situation, and the slide was subsequently removed from the plane. As a precaution, a backup aircraft was readied for the trip to the Republican midterm convention. The modified aircraft, noted as a foreign gift, is currently under scrutiny.

stories.title: 'I didn't see any benefits': Congress's P Chidambaram questions 2026 Brics, draws BJP's flak
stories.summary: With India set to host the Brics Summit 2026 in Delhi, Chidambaram said the country is part of several major international groupings but questioned whether they had delivered concrete gains for India. "I don't know how many Presidents and how many Prime Ministers are coming. I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results,” Chidambaram told news agency ANI.

stories.title: Nandan Nilekani, heading exam reform panel, named in SIR's 'no-mapping’ category
stories.summary: Nandan Nilekani, 71, is the co-founder and chairman of Bengaluru-based Infosys. He was also the founding chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India, which issues Aadhaar cards, serving with the rank of Cabinet minister in the Congress-led central government from 2009 to 2014. He was appointed co-chair of the G20 Task Force on Digital Public Infrastructure for Economic Transformation, Financial Inclusion, and Development in January 2023.

Toxic air after 9/11: Mamdani releases documents showing how New Yorkers were misled
stories.summary: In a significant move, New York City disclosed withheld documents on air quality after 9/11, suggesting that officials may have misrepresented the dangers present post-collapse of the Twin Towers. A memo warned of potential lawsuits for toxic exposure and city liability concerns. There were also fears about asbestos levels and negative public response. This revelation follows a legal challenge from the advocacy group 9/11 Health Watch.

Roman cemetery dig reveals Stone Age man buried with 2 skulls, 42 teeth and an axe
stories.summary: In a startling archaeological find, researchers uncovered a burial site dating back to the Stone Age, predating nearby Roman graves by thousands of years. The grave contained a battle axe, striking amber beads, and a unique necklace fashioned from the teeth of 42 animals. Additionally, two human skulls were discovered alongside the skeleton, offering rare insights into the rituals and practices of ancient communities.

stories.title: Napa Art Center Land Deal: di Rosa eases 162 acres into trust; future trail to Milliken Peak
stories.summary: A landmark conservation deal aims to safeguard a large portion of the di Rosa Center's Napa Valley landscape. Effectively shielding about 75% of the estate from future privatization, this agreement also secures vital financial resources for the center's ongoing operations. Exciting plans include a new public trail that will reach the summit of Milliken Peak, fostering an ideal mix of accessibility and artistic preservation.

stories.title: Indians trust the classroom, see better opportunities abroad: Global survey
stories.summary: Across 16 G20 countries covered by an Ipsos survey, Indians are unusually bullish about schools, degrees and the future of the young. Yet 76% say young people would have better opportunities abroad, pointing to a striking gap between faith in education and confidence in opportunity at home.

Motorcyclist Startles IRL Stream: Security rushes in on La Piquiña; viewers debate robbery risk
stories.summary: Kick streamer La Piquiña experienced a frightening moment while livestreaming from the streets of Colombia at night. A motorcyclist suddenly approached his outdoor desktop setup, prompting concerns that a robbery could be underway. His nearby security team quickly intervened, and the rider left before the situation escalated. The encounter later sparked debate online, with fans praising the guards while others questioned the safety of streaming from an exposed public location after dark.

stories.summary: N3on and Sneako’s friendship has taken a dramatic turn after Sneako publicly criticized N3on’s controversial AI streamer project. N3on, who announced an AI version of himself would stream 24/7 on Kick, accused Sneako of being disloyal and seeking views instead of addressing concerns privately. Sneako fired back with personal insults, while N3on defended the project and their friendship. The feud later intensified as both streamers continued trading jabs online.

Costa Rica maps nearly 500 dominant tree species to protect forest biodiversity
stories.summary: Researchers mapped Costa Rica's diverse forest ecosystems by analyzing tree species composition. Satellite observations and environmental data helped create a national forest map. This map distinguishes forest types, including secondary forests, across varied landscapes. The findings highlight the importance of dominant tree species for understanding forest function. Better field inventories are still needed to improve future forest mapping efforts.

Copenhagen’s £200m underground museum opens in 2027 with dinosaurs, 14m specimens and eight galleries
stories.summary: Copenhagen’s new £200 million Natural History Museum will open on March 6, 2027, featuring eight immersive underground galleries and a collection of 14 million specimens. Visitors can explore dinosaur skeletons, 3D exhibits and the spectacular Ocean Hall, as the museum combines historic Botanical Garden buildings with striking new underground architecture inspired by nature.

Antarctica gained 695 billion tons in 2021-23 as tropical warmth drove heavy snowfall
stories.summary: Between 2021 and 2023, Antarctica experienced a notable gain in ice mass, primarily driven by exceptional snowfall in East Antarctica. This unusual occurrence, influenced by warmer tropical ocean temperatures, caused atmospheric disturbances that transported moisture southward. Although this gain temporarily countered ongoing ice loss in other regions, it does not signify a change in Antarctica's long-term trend of declining ice mass.

Canadian couple donate 187-acre Ontario island sanctuary after protecting its wildlife for 36 years
stories.summary: Jim and Anne Purvis bought 187.4 acres on Ontario’s Wilson Island in 1989 and spent 36 years protecting the land as a family sanctuary. They have now donated the property to the Northumberland Land Trust, ensuring its forests, wetlands, grasslands and habitats for species at risk remain protected as a permanent nature reserve.

NCPCR summons Meta India head over alleged child abuse ads
stories.summary: The NCPCR has summoned Meta India's managing director regarding ads linked to child exploitation. This action follows a BBC Eye report and a formal inquiry into Meta's systems. The commission will examine Meta India's role in the s' appearance. The inquiry considers stringent provisions under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Meta stated it has zero tolerance for child exploitation and removed many suspicious accounts.

Meet Rachel Chen, 18, who won $100K for her breakthrough quantum math research using simple diagrams
stories.summary: Rachel Chen, an 18-year-old Los Angeles student, won $100,000 at the Regeneron Science Talent Search for expanding a 1997 mathematical idea involving Temperley-Lieb diagrams. Her research offers a visual way to describe complex quantum particle systems and spin representations, potentially helping researchers better understand connections between different quantum-mechanical states.

In 1973, Montana released a gall fly to control spotted knapweed; decades later...
stories.summary: Controlling invasive spotted knapweed biologically has initiated an unexpected ecological chain reaction. Gall flies, introduced as a control measure, have turned into a vital winter food source for deer mice, causing a surge in their populations and an uptick in hantavirus spread. Areas dense with knapweed report more infected mice than those with native grasslands.

stories.title: She bought a Maine island to stop clear-cutting; 90 years after Audubon opened its first camp there
stories.summary: Hog Island Audubon Camp marks an impressive ninety years of promoting environmental education and research. Located in Maine, this island was rescued from deforestation by environmentalists Millicent Todd Bingham and Mabel Loomis Todd. The camp is also the birthplace of Project Puffin, which successfully revitalized seabird numbers. Today, it remains a vital training ground for future scientists, educators, and artists, with its influence extending to bird conservation throughout North America.

Scientists seeded clouds over China’s Muz Taw Glacier; fresh snow cut ice loss by 14% to 17%
stories.summary: Scientists tested cloud seeding over China’s Muz Taw Glacier in 2018 to create artificial snowfall and slow ice loss. The experiment used silver iodide generators to encourage snow formation. Researchers found that fresh snow made the glacier surface brighter and reduced the amount of ice lost over a short period. However, they said the results are preliminary and need further testing.

stories.title: Andrew Flintoff lists his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion, bought from Phil Neville in 2021
stories.summary: England cricket legend Andrew Flintoff has put his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion on the market, four years after his life-changing Top Gear car crash. Bought from former Manchester United star Phil Neville in 2021, the 10,000 sq ft luxury property features six bedrooms, six bathrooms, four floors, a pool, gym, cinema and games room.

stories.title: Inside a $29M California mansion no one has ever lived in
stories.summary: A French-style manor in Rancho Santa Fe is now for sale at $29 million. This newly built home features antique materials and custom artisan craftsmanship throughout. The expansive residence includes a main house and a separate guest house on 3.66 acres. It boasts a zero-edge pool, gardens, and breathtaking views from its terraces. The manor comes fully furnished with art and antiques, ready for immediate occupancy.

stories.title: Canada released 26 bison into Banff in 2017; 9 years later, the herd has grown rapidly
stories.summary: Parks Canada successfully reintroduced plains bison into Banff National Park starting in 2017. The population grew from sixteen animals to about eighty by autumn 2022. Monitoring showed bison adapted to mountain habitat, preferring higher elevations for forage. Natural mortality remained low, with only two deaths recorded during the pilot. The five-year program achieved a 33% average annual population growth rate.
